# SwarmForge VS Code Extension — Specification

**Last Updated:** September 2, 2026 (BL-1338: BL-1267's adjudication
fingerprint (SHA-256 over the ticket YAML) is no longer invalidated by the
very promotion it authorized. `promote_and_route_next.sh` appends or
in-place-rewrites `assigned_to:` on promotion, AFTER the freshness gate
already ran — the fingerprint recorded at adjudication time was therefore
guaranteed stale the moment its own `confirm_promote` was acted on,
forcing a spurious re-adjudication on every promoted, previously-held
ticket (observed live on BL-1271, 2026-09-02). Fix, scoped exactly to the
human ruling (`extension/src/tools/deprecate-check.ts`'s new
`fingerprintableTicketText`): the routing stamp a promotion writes — the
appended-fresh shape and the in-place `sed`-rewritten shape alike — is
normalized out before hashing; every other field, including a genuine
edit to `assigned_to:` that is not that promotion's own write, still
changes the fingerprint and re-arms the gate (BL-1267's invariant
survives: a substantive amendment can never ride a stale clearance). No
new store, no new discharge path, no change to what
`promote_and_route_next.sh` writes. How-to:
`docs/how-to/BL-1173-deprecator-freshness-gate-cli.md` "Discharging a hold".)

**Last Updated:** September 2, 2026 (BL-1334: `is_qa_ancestor.sh`, the one
shared "is this sha QA-approved" predicate (BL-925 invariant 2), answers on
ancestry of `swarmforge-QA` plus a bounce-verdict veto (BL-952) — but the
land step's tip-pure replay mints a new commit and publishes it to `main`
without ever advancing that ref, so QA's own just-landed, approved work read
as unapproved to every ancestry-based consumer
(`check_pipeline_code_on_main.sh`, `handoffd.bb`'s push-sweep gate,
`babysitter_check.bb`) until an unrelated later merge closed the window —
observed live twice (`d7426989b2`/BL-1301, `c65d8e6728`/BL-1314), both
requiring the sanctioned `build_freshness_cli.bb sync --override` escape
hatch. Per the human ruling (option 2 of `ruling_options`), the fix does NOT
hand the land step write access to `swarmforge-QA` itself — that ref
defines approval, and a careless bump would erode exactly the property
BL-952 protects. Instead: `land_step_lib.bb`'s new
`record-land-approval!` appends `{at, ticket, commit, source}` to
`.swarmforge/land-approvals/<YYYY-MM>.jsonl` (append-only; a missing sha in
either field is refused rather than written, so a corrupt line can never
silently open the gate) on the replay success path; `is_qa_ancestor.sh`
consults that store, after the bounce veto, and grants approval only when
the record's named SOURCE itself resolves, carries no bounce verdict, and
is an ancestor of `swarmforge-QA` — checked directly rather than by
recursing into the predicate, so approval can never chain through a record
naming another record (the property that makes this still ONE predicate,
never a second, per the ticket's own constraint). `build_freshness_cli.bb`'s
drift report was rewritten to ask this predicate in `--batch` mode instead
of deciding ancestry itself with its own `merge-base` walk — removing a
second-predicate opinion the review found, not adding one. An unrecorded
land (write failure) degrades to the pre-fix behaviour
(`LAND_APPROVAL_UNRECORDED` reported, never fatal) rather than a false
approval. 48-case exhaustive property sweep (4 commit shapes × 4 land-store
states × 3 bounce states, including a reachable-but-bounced source, which a
first draft's weaker sweep could not distinguish from a correct
implementation). No new extension command or setting. See the [BL-632
commit-time guard reference](BL-632-commit-time-guard-refuses-pipeline-code-on-main.md)
for the predicate's now-updated full definition.)

**Last Updated:** September 2, 2026 (BL-1319: the coordinator's dwell/
bottleneck optimizer instrument (`extension/src/metrics/stageDwell.ts`,
BL-102) filters roles for `PIPELINE_ORDER` membership — bare stage names
only — BEFORE reading any mailbox, so a non-bare seat like `coder@sonnet2`
failed the membership test and was DROPPED, not merged: its mailbox was
never opened and its parcels never became dwell records. Consequence: a
two-seat stage was reported on its bare seat's parcels alone, understated by
omission, and could rank below a single-seat stage that was actually
faster — `nameBottleneck` ranks by median processing, so this is a wrong
optimizer decision, not a cosmetic label. Corrected mid-mint (see the
ticket's own amendment note): the original mint-time read assumed the seat
id survived into the report row and just needed folding there; the coder
found it never got that far. Fix: `stageOfSeat` (the same chokepoint BL-1040 added to
`swarmState.ts` earlier the same day, reused here rather than a third
hand-rolled `@`-split) now decides `PIPELINE_ORDER` membership and groups
survivors by stage, so a seat's mailbox is read and its records attributed
to its bare stage BEFORE the point that used to drop it —
`computeStageDwellReportForRoles` and `nameBottleneck` both fold this way.
Per-seat attribution is preserved in the underlying dwell records
(`deriveDwellRecords` still keyed on `entry.role`, and the new
`computeSeatDwellDetail` export keeps a seat-level view available for a
later ops surface) — only the report ROW is stage-keyed, never a seat id.
Single-seat output is byte-identical to before. Latent, not live, at ship
time, for the same reason as BL-1040 (no non-bare seat configured today);
live consumers (`bridge/bridgeState.ts`'s `/stage-dwell` endpoint and
`tools/stage-dwell-report.ts`) needed no new wiring, since both already call
into this module. Out of scope, checked and confirmed correct as-is:
supervisor, chase, ensure, and the babysitter already fold or iterate seats
correctly for their own purposes; BL-1040's board/stage-map path is the
same family, different files, landed separately the same day. No new
extension command or setting.)

**Last Updated:** September 2, 2026 (BL-1310: the master-main reconcile's
reset call sites (`handoffd.bb`, `swarm_heal.bb`, `post_hotfix_merge_
origin.bb`) never discard a local-ahead commit again. BL-1198/1214/1236/
1288 each narrowed WHEN `git reset --hard origin/main` may fire; none
changed what happened to the commits once it did — on 2026-08-31 the reset
destroyed seven commits of specifier work, recoverable only by luck from
the reflog before `git gc` collects it. The new shared gate,
`refuse-reset-if-local-ahead!` (`master_main_reconcile_lib.bb`), reads
local main's ahead-count fresh right before the reset would fire and
authorises the reset only when that count is a known zero; any `ahead > 0`
— including an undeterminable count — refuses instead, leaving main exactly
as found and naming the ticket in the daemon log. Per the approved human
ruling, this supersedes the "genuine rejection → reset proceeds" case in
BL-1198's and BL-1288's own docs: a rejected push authorises the reset only
when it turns out `ahead = 0`. No new extension command or setting.
Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1310-reconcile-never-discards-a-commit-it-cannot-name.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1310-reconcile-refuses-instead-of-discarding-local-ahead-commits.md`
(new); `docs/how-to/BL-1198-rematch-reset-must-push-before-discarding-local-ahead-commits.md`
and `docs/how-to/BL-1288-only-a-rejected-push-authorises-discarding-local-commits.md`
(both updated with a supersession note).)

**Last Updated:** September 1, 2026 (BL-1322: bridge startup no longer
requires `CURSOR_API_KEY` for targets that never touch Let's Talk/Cursor
routing. `createLiveCursorBridgeAgentSession`
(`extension/src/bridge/cursorBridgeAgentSession.ts`) used to call
`resolveCursorApiKey` eagerly at construction time — before any of the
returned session's methods ran — so `startBridge` failed for ANY target
missing the key, even on routes with nothing to do with Cursor (console,
pipeline board, spec tree, paused pager, epic reorder). The key resolution
moved into `ensureAgent`, the one place inside `promptAgent` that actually
opens a Cursor SDK agent; constructing the session, reading a stored agent
id (`readAgentId`), and resetting session state (`resetSession`) all now
work with no key configured, and only an actual Let's Talk prompt attempt
throws the existing `MISSING_CURSOR_API_KEY_MESSAGE` — unchanged wording,
only the timing moved. Also silently broke QA's own quality signal: 8 test
files / ~187 tests (bridgeServer, epicMakeTopBridge, epicReorderBridge,
pausedPagerBridge, specTreeBridge, startBridgeHeadlessCli,
telegramCursorBridgeCli, topicMakeTopBridge) were newly failing on
CURSOR_API_KEY with zero relationship to what they actually exercise
(BL-1313 QA pass, 2026-09-01); all 8 pass again. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1322-bridge-startup-does-not-require-cursor-api-key.feature`.)

**Last Updated:** September 1, 2026 (BL-1318: pack `window` lines now pass
through a steward staffing gate before a launch stages any tmux window —
previously a pack could pin any `agent`/`--model`/`--openai-api-base` and
`./swarm --pack …` staffed the seat with no steward consult at all, the gap
that let `opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free` — registry-`certified` globally but
`QA-gate: human-verdict-pending` and ranked on the `:coder` role-matrix only —
sit the QA seat on both Bob packs and idle instead of running
`merge_and_process`. `pack_staffing_gate` in `swarmforge/scripts/swarmforge.sh`
is the single call site, reached from `parse_config`'s per-window loop — the
only path every pack launch and every materialised
`.swarmforge/launch/<role>.sh` (the mono-router `rotate_to_role.sh` re-exec
path included) passes through. It resolves each window's provider/model
identity via a table-driven map in `pack_staffing_gate_lib.bb` (`cursor …
--model auto` → `cursor/auto`; `claude … --model claude-sonnet-5` →
`anthropic/claude-sonnet-5`; `aider --model openai/qwen3.7-plus
--openai-api-base <aliyuncs base>` → `qwen/qwen3.7-plus`, provider taken from
the api-base host, not the `openai/` prefix) and refuses any window whose
identity cannot be resolved — nothing is staffed by default. The pure decision
lives in `seat-staffing-decision` (`pack_staffing_gate_lib.bb`); the gate
requires role-matrix ranking, a `pass` compliance-gate decision (not
`human-verdict-pending`), and `assignment-eligible?`, and only READS steward
evidence — it never writes the registry, a scorecard, or a role matrix, and
never runs a compliance battery at launch time. A refusal prints the role, the
resolved provider/model, the failing check, and a runnable `model-steward`
command. Operator escape hatch: `PACK_STAFFING_SKIP_GATE=1` (same shape as
BL-1127's `LOCAL_CODER_BATTERY_SKIP_GATE=1`), which stages the seat as an
`override` — printed as a loud warning, never shown or recorded as a plain
pass. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1318-pack-launch-steward-staffing-gate.feature`. How-to:
`docs/how-to/BL-1318-pack-staffing-gate.md`, cross-linked from the BL-547 and
BL-1127 how-to pages.)

**Last Updated:** September 1, 2026 (BL-1313: the two send-time guards
that read a role's `in_process` mailbox — `swarm_handoff.bb`'s
`inbound-non-forwarding?` self-check (Article 2.4's merge-only refusal)
and `duplicate_chain_guard_lib.bb`'s BL-760 duplicate-chain check — were
blind to parcels a batch role (cleaner, hardener) holds inside an
`in_process/batch_*/` subdirectory, because both walked `in_process`
through `handoff-lib/handoff-files`, which only lists the flat top level
(`batch-dirs`, the helper that does descend, sat unused one line below
it). For the two batch roles this meant the merge-only self-check could
never fire, and BL-760's duplicate-chain guard failed open — a live
parcel sitting with the cleaner or hardener was invisible to a
competing send from anywhere else. Measured 2026-08-31: an architect
`back-all` bounce planted a `non-forwarding: true` reverse copy in the
cleaner's `batch_*/` dir; the cleaner never got the accurate refusal
(inert for it) and was instead blocked later by the duplicate-chain
guard naming the coder's mailbox, read that as a lost stamp, and
recorded a wrong root cause. Fix: `handoff_lib.bb` gains
`handoff-files-with-batches` / `my-handoff-files-with-batches`,
batch-aware twins that concatenate the flat listing with every
`batch_*` subdirectory's contents; both guards now call the batch-aware
reader for `:in_process` walks instead of the flat one. Scope held to
the two send-time guards named in the measured incident — four other
blind `in_process` reads in `handoff_lib.bb` (`stage-seat-worked-task-sets`,
the mono-router resident check's two `:blocking-file` reads,
`wait-for-delivery!`) and the six pre-existing hand-rolled batch walkers
elsewhere are deliberately out of scope, left for a survey ticket if one
of them shows a measured consequence. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1313-a-batch-held-parcel-is-visible-to-the-send-time-guards.feature`.

**Last Updated:** September 1, 2026 (BL-1316: a seat's reasoning effort
now also retunes at claim/reclaim time from the claimed ticket's
`mutation_cost` — see the Effort dial section below; BL-1303: a new commit-guard,
`check_feature_handler_registration.sh`, refuses a commit or `--no-ff`
merge on `main` that leaves a `specs/features/*.feature` file with no
registered — or no longer runnable — step handler. `specs/pipeline/runtime.js`
throws on any scenario no registered handler matches, and nothing had
refused the `main` state that creates: a feature file could land with its
handler unregistered, or registered but a script it executes missing, and
the failure surfaced later to whichever role next ran the suite, against a
parcel that did not cause it — the step-registry sibling of BL-1240's
`suite-manifest.tsv` accumulate-unseen shape. Two live incidents motivated
it, both by MERGE rather than a fresh commit: BL-1253's bounce-revert
removed a handler, its lib script, and its `index.js` registration
together, and a later resurrecting merge brought back the handler and
feature file but not the registration or the lib; separately, merge
`45625ef9cb` (2026-08-27) silently dropped BL-709's already-landed
registration line by resolving to the parent that lacked it (the BL-571/
BL-958/BL-954 silent-revert-by-merge shape). Because both incidents
happened by `--no-ff` merge, the guard is reached from BOTH commit-time
hooks — `pre-commit` (via the widened `run_commit_guards.sh`, now five
guards) and `pre-merge-commit` (previously a single-guard delegate to
`check_pipeline_code_on_main.sh` alone, now two guards) — rather than only
the one `pre-commit` had already grown a chain in. `pre-merge-commit` was
deliberately NOT repointed at the whole `run_commit_guards.sh` chain, which
would have newly subjected every merge to the commit-size/ticket-deletion
guards and the expensive `check_property_suite_drift.sh` (currently running
under an operator override for its own broken allowlist matcher, BL-1234).
The two hooks' guard-chain aggregation — run every guard, report every
violation in one refusal, never abort at the first (Article 4.4's shape in
a gate, BL-1242/BL-1252's discipline) — is shared via a new sourced
library, `swarmforge/scripts/commit_guard_chain_lib.sh`, rather than
re-derived per hook. The guard is keyed on the FEATURE side (every
`specs/features/*.feature` must resolve to a registered handler) rather
than "every `steps/*.js` file must appear in `index.js`", because eleven of
twelve currently-unregistered step files on `main` are deliberate `*Only.js`
focused re-export entry points that are each correctly registered under
their real handler's name — a file-keyed guard would have emitted eleven
false refusals alongside the one true one. See the widened "Guard-Chain
Aggregation Is Shared, Not the Whole Chain (BL-1303)" section in
`docs/reference/BL-632-commit-time-guard-refuses-pipeline-code-on-main.md`.
Acceptance: `specs/features/BL-1303-a-feature-on-main-always-has-a-registered-handler.feature`.)

**Last Updated:** August 31, 2026 (BL-1298: the land step's replay now runs
from ANY worktree, not only the main checkout. `replay!`
(`swarmforge/scripts/land_step_lib.bb`) built its scratch checkout at
`<root>/.git/land-replay-worktrees/...`; `.git` is a directory only in the
main checkout — in a linked worktree, the only place a pipeline role ever
stands, it is a FILE holding `gitdir: ...`, so the path named a child of a
regular file and `git worktree add` failed outright ("could not create
worktree ... off origin/main", measured 2026-08-30 landing BL-1295 from
`.worktrees/QA`). The only working route was passing the main checkout as
an undocumented optional third argument. New `git-common-dir` asks git
directly (`rev-parse --git-common-dir`), which resolves correctly — and
identically — from either checkout, so the same ticket and commit replay
the same way regardless of who invokes it; a git that cannot answer is a
refusal naming the root, never a path built from a guess. Second half: on
the create-failure path, `git worktree add -b` had already created the
scratch branch before failing to make the checkout, and that path returned
without deleting it — unlike the other two failure paths — so a retry
failed with "branch already exists", a different reason than the first
attempt, misdirecting whoever read it. All three failure paths now delete
the branch through one `drop-branch!`; deleting a branch that was never
created is not itself treated as a failure. Not in scope: the four
pre-existing `land-replay/*` branches already in the repository, and what a
SUCCESSFUL replay leaves behind (QA's own land action still reads that
branch). Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1298-the-replay-runs-from-a-linked-worktree.feature`.)

Prior entry —
**Last Updated:** August 31, 2026 (BL-1252: the shared pre-commit hook's
four guards — `check_commit_size.sh`, `check_ticket_deletion.sh`,
`check_pipeline_code_on_main.sh`, `check_property_suite_drift.sh` — used to
run as four sequential commands under `set -euo pipefail`, so the first
one that refused aborted the hook and a commit violating several guards was
reported one violation per commit attempt, the first-failure-stop shape
Article 4.4 forbids of a reviewing role. Extracted into
`swarmforge/scripts/run_commit_guards.sh`, which the hook now `exec`s: the
three index-inspection guards run under `set -uo pipefail` (no `-e`), one
exit status captured per guard, and a commit violating more than one is
refused ONCE with every violation named. `check_property_suite_drift.sh` is
reached only once those three pass, so an already-refused commit never
pays for `npm run test:properties`, and it still runs on every commit the
cheap three allow. No guard's predicate, threshold, or exemption changed —
only the completeness of the report — and an unexpected non-refusal exit
(a crash, a missing script) still refuses and names the failing guard.
Same shape the sibling commit-msg hook already uses (BL-1242, `61735035f`).
No new extension command or setting. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1252-commit-guard-chain-reports-every-violation.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1252-commit-guard-chain-reports-every-violation.md`.)

**Last Updated:** August 31, 2026 (BL-1210: every Telegram topic kind keeps
its icon ownership marker again, closing a two-day-old (2026-08-25–27)
regression BL-695 introduced. BL-695's classification split
(`topicThreadKind.ts`) correctly restricted git-tracked
`backlog/topics/*.json` records to `ticket` ids, but its marker-store
change went further than the tracked-record boundary required:
`recordSwarmIconId` only had a durable store for `ticket` and `supervisor`
kinds, so a marker write for an `epic`, `standing`, or `role` id (all
classify `unbound`) silently wrote nothing — while `syncTopicIcon` still
reported `updated`. No live icon behaviour broke (every epic/standing/role
caller passes `isNewTopic=true`, bypassing the ownership check the marker
feeds), but the marker was inert for 3 of 4 topic kinds and every such sync

**Last Updated:** August 30, 2026 (BL-1297: a merge commit's own changed
paths no longer come back empty, which had let the send-time scope gate,
the unregistered-test gate, and the land step's tip-pure replay all fail
open on the pipeline's most common commit shape. `own-commit-diff`
(`task_scope_gate_lib.bb`) ran `diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r
--first-parent <commit>`; git suppresses a merge's diff entirely unless
`-m` or `-c`/`--cc` is given, and `--first-parent` is a `log`/`rev-list`
traversal flag with no effect on `diff-tree`'s own diff output — so every
merge commit reported zero paths. A merge is the normal shape of a role's
own commit (every stage receives a handoff via `git merge <hash>`), so a
parcel whose only task-tagged commit was that merge collapsed to an empty
change set, which the gate reads as "no foreign paths" and passes,
unverified. New `own-commit-changed-paths` answers two distinct questions
from one walk: `:delivered` (`diff <commit>^1 <commit>`) is what content a
commit puts on the branch against its first parent alone; `:authored`
(`diff-tree --cc`) is what differs from EVERY parent, empty for an
ordinary clean receive-merge whose content was already attributed
upstream. The land step's replay reads `:delivered` (what a parcel puts on
the branch); the send-time scope gate and the unregistered-test gate both
read `:authored` (what the parcel's author actually wrote) — an earlier
version of this fix answered `:delivered` for all three callers, which
refused every forward the moment a branch had synced `main`, which is
always (measured: 25 delivered paths across 8 unrelated tickets on one
real receive-merge, versus 1 authored path — the fix's own file). A root
commit (`--root`) answers both semantics identically and is never treated
as empty. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1297-a-merge-commits-own-paths-are-not-empty.feature`.)

five other supervisors that must not change behaviour. The genuine crash path

naming it, naming nothing, or naming a live but UNRELATED process (pid reuse)
is still `crashed`, restarted through `start_operator_runtime.sh`, and still

recorded in the status file but does not reach the human channel — it is not
an incident, and announcing one every few minutes is exactly the alert

UI branch hides the dot rather than showing a fourth status kind. A blank
capture (a pane that WAS captured but returned nothing) is the other half of
that and answers for itself with `stale` rather than falling through to the
aggregate — the exact gap
that would otherwise paint a dead pane green on the next poll. `ok` is

event the operator most needs to see. Fixed: the per-pane signal now

**Last Updated:** August 30, 2026 (BL-1232: the morning briefing's
shift-velocity chart (BL-1184) is readable again — a human-reported intake
found the Y axis crushed flat by a single outlier day (~415 against an
ordinary sub-30 range), colliding X-axis date labels, and one hop between
consecutive days eating most of the plot width. The last two shared one root
cause: `nonLinearTimeX` took the log of raw age in MILLISECONDS rather than
age normalized to the series span, so the curve's shape depended on the
clock's units — over a 30-day series the single most recent day-to-day hop
could consume ~84% of the plot, packing every other day into the leftmost
sixth where index-picked labels then stacked on each other. Fixed by
normalizing age to `0..1` before the log
(`log(1 + TIME_WARP_K * normalizedAge) / log(1 + TIME_WARP_K)`,
`TIME_WARP_K = 9`) — the non-linear warp BL-1184 locked in stays non-linear
(`hasNonLinearTimeSpacing` still holds), it no longer lets one unit-of-time
choice dominate the plot. Date labels now come from a new shared
`pickLabelIndicesByPixelGap` (`briefingChartSvgCommon.ts`, reachable by any
future chart) that picks by where points actually render rather than by
series index, always keeping the most recent day and greedily accepting
candidates that clear a derived minimum pixel gap. The Y-axis crush is fixed
separately with a soft cap: `shiftVelocityAxisPlan` derives a robust body
bound from the series (`max(median × 3, p75 × 2, 1)`) and, only when the true
peak materially exceeds it, draws the axis from the bound and renders the
over-cap day as a distinct clipped marker on the cap line carrying its true
value as text — no series value is ever silently dropped or flattened, and
when the peak does not materially exceed the bound the axis behaves exactly
as before. The metric (max tickets landed per rolling 8h window per day) and
the lifecycle-adapter data source are unchanged — this ticket is
presentation-only. See the updated "The non-linear time axis" and new "The Y
axis: soft cap with a clipped-peak marker" sections in
`docs/how-to/BL-1184-briefing-shift-velocity-chart.md`. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1232-shift-velocity-chart-readable.feature`.)

**Last Updated:** August 29, 2026 (BL-1234: the property-suite standing-red
allowlist gate (`ps_suite_extract_failing_files` in
`swarmforge/scripts/property_suite_standing_allowlist_lib.sh`) refused
every commit whenever two or more allowlisted property tests were red,
which is the only case that occurs in practice once the allowlist names
more than one file — reproduced live and reported independently by both the
coder and the hardener within fifteen minutes of each other. Root cause:
`ps_allowlist_normalize_file` emits its path with no trailing newline (its
own contract is normalizing a path, not deciding line framing), so at its
one call site inside the failing-files loop, two or more normalized paths
landed on the same line before `sort -u` saw the stream; `sort -u` then
treated that concatenation as one unmatchable path, no row in the TSV
matched it, and the guard refused with a message naming a path that does
not exist. A single failing file worked by accident (`sort` itself supplies
the line's own terminator). Fixed by moving the newline to the call site so
every normalized path lands on its own line before `sort -u` runs; the
verdict now depends on which files failed, never on how many. No new
extension command or setting. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1234-property-allowlist-gate-recognises-every-red.feature`.
How-to:
`docs/how-to/BL-1175-property-suite-standing-reds-block-unrelated-commits.md`.)

**Last Updated:** August 29, 2026 (BL-1233: `sync_worktree_scripts.bb`'s
launcher guard (BL-373) — which leaves a role worktree's git-tracked script
paths to git rather than copying over them — was fully defeated by an
ambient `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE` in the launcher's environment, the live
condition on this host. `-C <worktree>` does not override those variables:
the tracked-path query answered for whichever repo `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`
named, returned an empty tracked set for the real worktree, and the
launcher read "empty" as "nothing to leave to git" and copied the launching
checkout's (often older) bytes over all ~1142 tracked script files in every
role worktree — silently, since the copy's own exit status is `0` and the
guard's "left to git (tracked)" lines simply stop printing. In the observed
incident this landed on safety gates first (BL-1196's env scrub, BL-1192's
task-scope gate), which had not yet reached `main` and so were absent from
the copied bytes. Fixed with the same two-part shape BL-1196 already
established at a different call site: the tracked-path git invocation now
scrubs `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_WORK_TREE`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE` before asking, and a new
pure `trustworthy-tracked-answer?` (`sync_worktree_scripts_lib.bb`) is the
fail-closed backstop — a tracked-path answer is trusted only when git
actually resolved a top-level for the destination worktree and it equals
that worktree's own canonicalized root; on a mismatch or an unresolved
top-level the launcher copies nothing and refuses loudly, naming both
paths. A foreign target repo that legitimately tracks none of these paths
still resolves its own top-level correctly and is unaffected — the
discriminator is a wrong or absent top-level, never an empty tracked set by
itself. Closes the open question left in the BL-1195 worktree-drift-guard
doc ("or that guard has a gap this incident exposes"). No new extension
command or setting. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1233-launcher-guard-survives-ambient-git-env.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1233-launcher-guard-survives-ambient-git-env.md`.)

**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026 (BL-1236: the master-main reconcile
conflict predicate (`merge-tree-reports-conflict?` /
`master_main_reconcile_lib.bb`, consumed by `handoffd.bb`'s reconcile sweep
and, byte-identically until this fix, by `post_hotfix_merge_origin.bb`'s CLI)
decided "would this merge conflict?" by grepping the legacy three-argument
`git merge-tree`'s unified-diff output for words like "CONFLICT" — any
merged file whose own prose happened to contain them (this repo's tickets
and evidence files do, constantly) read as a predicted conflict and drove a
`git reset --hard origin/main`, discarding already-committed work; ten
resets fired this way, one destroying a human's approval tap three minutes
after it landed. Both call sites now share one verdict built on `git
merge-tree --write-tree <a> <b>`'s own exit code — the same flag
`tree_collapse_guard_lib.bb` already uses in production — read as clean
(`0`) / conflicted (`1`) / **unavailable** (`>= 2`, or a git too old to
support the flag). Unavailable is the core change: previously a
`merge-base` failure or any git error returned `true` (conflict, reset) —
fail-open dressed as fail-closed. It is now its own surfaced,
non-destructive outcome, never collapsed into either "conflict" (reset) or
"clean" (attempt a merge that could itself fail and reset). The
genuine-conflict recovery path is unchanged; reopening it was explicitly out
of scope. No new extension command or setting — Babashka reconcile tooling.
Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1236-reconcile-conflict-prediction-from-git-verdict.feature`.

`swarmforge/scripts/backlog_hygiene_lib.bb`) now names every colliding
path's pool and lifecycle class (`path [pool/live-or-terminal]` —
`paused`/`active` are `live`, `hold`/`done` are `terminal`), states whether
the colliding files' contents are byte-identical (`CONTENT IDENTICAL`) or
not (`CONTENT DIFFERS` — fail-closed: an unreadable file is always reported
as differing, never as identical), and, when exactly one colliding copy
sits in a live pool, names that path with `keep: <path>`. Before this fix
the finding read only the ids and raw paths, so resolving a collision meant
opening every file by hand and guessing which copy was still in the
pipeline — the 2026-08-27 incident this ticket was filed for got both
wrong at once. The content read is injectable (`read-fn`, default `slurp`)
per this project's inject-side-effects rule; `format-violation`'s existing
single-arg callers are unaffected (2-arity default). No new extension
command or setting — Babashka backlog tooling. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1216-duplicate-id-finding-names-the-live-copy-and-flags-divergence.feature`.)

**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026 (BL-1192: `swarm_handoff.sh` refuses a
`git_handoff` send — on every hop, not only the documenter→QA edge BL-531
already covers — when the task's own commits since its last handoff carry
a path that positively belongs to a different ticket than the one the
`task:` header names (`task_scope_gate_lib.bb`). Identification is
positive-only, via the same exact-id-equality extractor BL-953 uses,
restricted to path shapes that actually carry a ticket id in their own
name (`backlog/**`, `specs/features/**`, `docs/how-to/**`); a functional
code path is never flagged, and fail-open covers that silence structurally.
Scope is the union of this task's own tagged commits' tree diffs, walked
from the last handoff recorded for this exact task — a literal

avalanche on a batch role's own accumulated sibling-ticket commits.
Backstops the dominant 2026-08-27 shift bounce class (ten `behavior`
bounces, six measured as entangled tips) at the hop where it first
appears instead of riding the pipeline to QA. Fail-open is absolute on any
unreadable fact, same posture as BL-953/BL-972. No new extension command
or setting. Acceptance:

**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026 (BL-1215: `/pilot`'s acceptance-contract
landing gate (`extension/src/tools/pilotAcceptanceGate.ts`) now refuses to
move a ticket into `backlog/done/` unless its implementation commit is
reachable from `origin/main` — immediately before the yaml move,
`checkOriginMainLanding` (`extension/src/tools/pilot-acceptance-gate.ts`)
fetches `origin/main` fresh and checks ancestry via `git merge-base
--is-ancestor`. Fails CLOSED: an unfetchable remote, no remote configured,
or an unresolvable commit are all treated as not-landed, the deliberate
mirror of the commit-claims check's fails-OPEN posture (BL-729) — "done" was
previously a fact about local `HEAD` alone, and an expedition's work could
pass acceptance and get a receipt while remaining unpushed (BL-1158 failed
in exactly this shape the same day). A refused land is inert (no yaml move,
no receipt) and never pushes — a human or the pilot must push and re-run.
No new extension command or setting. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1215-pilot-land-gate-verifies-the-implementation-reached-origin-main.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-727-pilot-acceptance-contract-gate.md` origin/main
landing check section.)

**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026 (BL-1208: the BL-954 bounce-revert check
(`decideBounceRevertVerdict`, `extension/src/quality/bounceRevertVerdict.ts`)
offered a ready-to-paste `git revert --no-edit <commit>` remedy whenever a
bounced commit's content was still live at the bouncing branch's tip — true
of every healthy commit that changed a file, not only a bounced defect. It
fired for real on a recovery commit that had just restored 13 files an
earlier incident had silently dropped; following the remedy would have
re-deleted every one of them. The adapter
(`extension/src/metrics/bounceRevertGitAdapter.ts`) now gathers one extra
fact per live file — `restoredFromEarlierHistory`, true only when the
bounced commit added the path (never a plain edit) and that exact content
already existed at some earlier point in the same bouncing branch's own
history, never a sibling branch's — and the remedy is withheld (set to
`null`) only when every live file is so established. The `violation`
verdict and every `liveFiles` path are still reported unchanged either way;
no-silent-clean survives untouched. No new extension command or setting —
fork/operator-substrate tooling under `extension/src/tools/`. Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1208-revert-remedy-requires-authorship-not-liveness.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1208-bounce-revert-remedy-requires-authorship-not-liveness.md`.)
Prior entry —
**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026 (BL-1214: the shared master-main reconcile
ladder's `:ff-absorb` execution (`absorb-with-merge!` in
`master_main_reconcile_lib.bb`, consumed by `handoffd.bb`, `swarm_heal.bb`,
and `post_hotfix_merge_origin.bb`) now attempts one plain 3-way `git merge
--no-edit origin/main` between the failed fast-forward and the reset
fallback. A non-conflicting two-way divergence is now absorbed losslessly
via a real 2-parent merge commit instead of being discarded by `git reset
--hard origin/main` — the plan already said "absorb", but every executor
could previously only fast-forward, so a genuine divergence always fell
through to the reset regardless of content. A real conflict still aborts
cleanly (no `MERGE_HEAD` left behind) and falls back to today's reset
recovery, byte-for-byte unchanged. Composes with BL-1198's push-before-reset
into one ladder: fast-forward → push → 3-way merge → reset. This defect had
fired in production and discarded four committed commits, including the
human's own approval of this ticket. No new extension command or setting.
Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1214-reconcile-absorbs-non-conflicting-two-way-divergence-with-a-real-merge.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1214-ff-absorb-attempts-real-merge-before-reset.md`.)

**Last Updated:** August 28, 2026 (BL-1202: the BL-570/BL-1124 pre-commit
property-suite guard (`check_property_suite_drift.sh`) now reports its
BL-1124 shared-repo canary verdict on every exit path of the suite run it
guards — green, red, or the guard itself being killed mid-run (SIGINT/
SIGTERM/SIGHUP), not only on a normal return — via an idempotent
`report_canary_once()` installed on `EXIT`/`INT`/`TERM` traps. The suite now
runs as the leader of its own process group so a kill can take the whole
group down by pgid before the canary is asserted; no process the guard
started can outlive it. Fixes the gap the 2026-08-27 19:37 incident exposed:
a client-side timeout killing the foreground `git commit` skipped the canary
entirely and left the suite's background processes rewriting the
`swarmforge-cleaner` branch ref unreaped. Every short-circuit above the point
a real suite run starts (path skip, BL-1121 reconcile-import skip, the
`SWARMFORGE_SKIP_PROPERTY_SUITE_GUARD=1` override, toolchain-missing) is
unchanged and leaves the traps a no-op. No new extension command or setting.
Acceptance:
`specs/features/BL-1202-shared-repo-canary-reports-on-every-exit-path.feature`.
How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1124-property-suite-fixtures-must-not-mutate-shared-main.md`
(updated) and `docs/how-to/BL-570-property-suite-drift-guard.md` (updated).)

BL-1086: babysitterd's
`pipeline-code-on-main` gather (check 13, BL-631) re-derived its answer from
scratch every 300s tick, spawning `is_qa_ancestor.sh` once per SHA ahead of
`swarmforge-QA`. On a `main` ~23 commits ahead this overran the daemon's 600s
freshness threshold — the heartbeat writes only after the check returns, so
a slow gather read as a dead daemon and triggered a mid-sweep restart
(`age_secs=1146`, 2026-08-22). Fix, two halves: (1) an on-disk cache
(`.swarmforge/babysitterd/pipeline-code-on-main-cache.json`, not in-memory —
each tick is a fresh process) keyed on the `main`/`origin/main`/
`swarmforge-QA` tips, invalidated the moment any moves, never populated from
an `:ancestry-unavailable? true` result; (2) `is_qa_ancestor.sh` gained a
`--batch` mode answering the whole candidate set in one process instead of
one process per SHA, remaining the single approval predicate (BL-925
invariant 2) rather than a second ancestry implementation — an unanswered or
failed batch still fails the whole sweep closed, never a partial result. No
extension command, setting, or UI change. See the new "Cached, batched
pipeline-code-on-main gather" section in
`docs/how-to/BL-611-babysitterd-runbook.md`.)

BL-1043: the onboarder and
negotiation-relay supervisors get a real startup grace, closing a hole
worse than BL-1035's — `front_desk_supervisor_lib.bb`'s
`poll-heartbeat-stale?` has a 3-arity convenience form that passes
`started-at-ms` as `nil`; the grace clause opens with
`(and started-at-ms ...)`, so with `nil` it can never fire, and the arity
even passes `stall-ms` into the grace slot, which reads to a reviewer like
a deliberate generous grace and is dead code. `onboarder_supervisor.bb:147`
and `negotiation_relay_supervisor.bb:145` both called exactly that arity,
so a freshly spawned child with no heartbeat file at all was declared
stalled on its first tick, not after any real grace. Measured live in
`.swarmforge/operator/onboarder-supervisor.log`: 39 starts, 27 stalls, 7
of 14 adjacent started→stalled pairs under ten seconds, the fastest 2.00s
against a declared 120000ms window — burning the bounded restart budget on
a fault that was never there. `cursor_bridge_supervisor.bb` already got
both halves right (a real grace plus clearing the heartbeat file at spawn)
and was the reference, not a subject — byte-for-byte unchanged. The
grace-less 3-arity is retired rather than repaired, since it has no spawn
time to measure a grace from and a reachable grace-less form under any
spelling keeps the trap open for the next supervisor: calling it now is an
arity error. A new defaulting 4-arity fills the gap it leaves — a call
site that passes `started-at-ms` without an explicit grace length gets
`default-startup-grace-ms` (90000, the same value `cursor_bridge` already
used, not a third number); the explicit 5-arity is unchanged. Both
supervisors now pass `(:started-at-ms entry)` through an env-tunable grace
of their own (`ONBOARDER_HEARTBEAT_STARTUP_GRACE_MS`,
`NEGOTIATION_RELAY_HEARTBEAT_STARTUP_GRACE_MS`, both defaulting to the
library value) and clear their heartbeat file at spawn, matching
`cursor_bridge`'s shape. Declared invariants — no child is judged stalled
before one full startup grace, and no child is judged on a heartbeat
written by a process no longer running — are property-tested 400 runs
across 8 declared classes (`bl1043_startup_grace_property_runner.bb`),
non-vacuity proven by four deliberate breaks including restoring the
shipped grace-less-3-arity defect itself. Out of scope, deliberately: the
front-desk supervisor (BL-1035's own subject) and two unrelated
pre-existing red tests on `main` (one confirmed live and independent of
this session), both surfaced to the specifier by `note` rather than fixed
here. Degraded gate: Babashka/shell only, no mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling
wired for this surface; gated by the property runner above plus
`front_desk_supervisor_lib_test_runner.bb`,
`test_onboarder_supervisor_ignores_old_heartbeat.sh`,
`test_negotiation_relay_supervisor_tick.sh`, and 5/5 acceptance scenarios.
No new extension command or setting.)

Prior entry —
BL-1075: found during BL-1069's own
review (goal 4) and minted as its narrow follow-up rather than folded in.
The swarm's hardening step set `window-size largest` as a stability
mitigation on the control-plane server — and named it as one in the ops
runbook — but tmux(1) is explicit that `resize-window` "will automatically
set window-size to manual **in the window options**", and a window option
beats the server global. The extension's `paneTailer.ts` calls
`resizeWindow` on every role window it tiles, so `largest` was unreachable
on every window the panel manages, by construction — not a race, not an
ordering bug, and not fixable by changing which writer runs last. Stopped
applying and stopped claiming a mitigation that cannot hold, on both call
paths that set it (`swarmforge/scripts/swarmforge.sh`'s
`harden_tmux_server`, `swarmforge/scripts/control_plane_lib.bb`'s
`harden-server!`) — nothing else changes: `focus-events off` is untouched
and still applied on every path that applied it before, since it is not
overridden by anything and remains the mitigation that actually holds.
`docs/how-to/BL-tmux-wsl-segfault-upgrade.md` now names only
`focus-events off` among the soft mitigations, states plainly that the
tmux ≥ 3.7 version upgrade is what actually protects the host, and adds a
sentence on why the window-size line was dropped rather than silently
disappearing. Severity `medium`, deliberately: the knob was inert and the
runbook overstated it, but nobody was actually less protected than they
would be with the knob absent — the tmux ≥ 3.7 preference (BL-1069) is the
defence that carries the load, landed and live. Explicitly deferred to a
successor ticket: what the swarm should do when the panel is about to tile
a control plane running tmux older than 3.7 — where `resize-window` arms
the exact WINDOW_SIZE_MANUAL segfault trigger per window — needs the
server-version fact BL-1069 was still building at mint time, so folding it
in here would have made this slice depend on unlanded sibling work.
`extension/src/panel/paneTailer.ts` was not modified by this parcel — the
panel is the thing the swarm-side fix stopped fighting, not itself a party
to the fix. Degraded gate on the swarm-side half only: shell + Babashka,
no mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling wired, gated by
`bl1075_window_size_ownership_property_runner.bb` (which re-measures the
window-option-beats-global mechanism every run, so a future tmux changing
that scope rule fails the test rather than silently enforcing a decision
whose premise had gone) plus the acceptance scenarios. No new extension
command or setting.)

BL-1029: the family sweep BL-1018 left
undone. tmux hands a `respawn-pane` command's trailing argument straight to
`$SHELL -c`, so that argument must itself be valid POSIX shell; five
remaining repair sites (`remote_control_health_lib.bb`, both
`handoff_lib.bb` sites, both `handoffd.bb` sites — two of the ticket's
original seven, in `swarm_ensure.bb`/`babysitter_check.bb`, had already
been converted by BL-1018 landing on `main` between mint and this pass)
still built that argument as a bare `(str "zsh '" launch-script "'")`, with
no escaping, which stops being valid shell the instant the wrapped launch
path contains an apostrophe — on such a host every one of these repair
paths would fail to restart the role it was invoked to save. All five now
route through one new shared constructor,
`swarmforge/scripts/shell_quote_lib.bb`'s `launch-command` (deliberately a
command builder, not just the quoting primitive — the `zsh ` prefix and
the quoting are one decision, and splitting them is how a site ends up
with the prefix right and the quoting wrong); BL-1018's own private
`shell-quote-single` in `single_role_repair_lib.bb` is removed, not
duplicated, and that lib now loads the shared one. The verification shape
was itself part of the ask: this defect already survived BL-1018's own
property runner behind a `str/includes?` substring check on the raw path,
which passes whether the escaping is correct or broken, so every assertion
that matters here hands the constructed argument to a REAL shell and
compares what comes back, byte for byte, to what went in — eight path
shapes (apostrophe, spaces, `$`, backslash, `;&|`, backticks, double
quotes, an embedded newline) round-tripped, with the pre-fix construction
kept as a negative control proven to actually fail in a shell. The
enumeration proving no site quotes a launch path on its own derives its
site list from the tree (`swarmforge/scripts/*.bb`, excluding the test
tree) rather than a hand-maintained list, so an eighth site written later
cannot go unrouted unnoticed — proven non-vacuous by renaming the helper
and confirming the check catches the unrouted files (which itself
surfaced and fixed a substring-match bug in the check's own site-detector
during authoring). Degraded gate: shell + Babashka only, no
mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling wired; gated by
`shell_quote_lib_test_runner.bb` and
`bl1029_respawn_quoting_property_runner.bb` (200 generated paths) plus the
acceptance scenarios; three Gherkin mutation survivors on this feature
were confirmed genuine equivalent mutants (BL-234), not a coverage gap.
No new extension command or setting — swarm-substrate repair tooling
under `swarmforge/scripts/`.)
Prior entry —
BL-991: the operator ruling
("make required_stages binding so a declared stage cannot be jumped")
enforced. Before this, `route-required-stages` treated a ticket's declared
`required_stages` set as a PRUNING list only — membership was permission:
a coder addressing QA directly on a ticket declaring the full chain was
delivered straight to QA, jumping cleaner/architect/hardender/documenter.
BL-951 (2026-08-19, above) made that jump visible with a `routing_skipped`
record; this ticket is the enforcement half BL-951 deliberately left
undone. Now, on any forward hop, the router computes `next` — the first
declared stage strictly after the sender — and whenever the literal `to:`
is later than `next` in canonical order, the handoff is redirected to
`next` instead, regardless of whether the literal target is itself a
declared stage. The same rule closes an easy-to-miss twin on the
non-member branch: declaring `[coder, cleaner, qa]`, a coder addressing
`architect` used to rewrite forward to QA (jumping the declared `cleaner`);
it now redirects to `cleaner`. A redirected hop is not a skip — the stage
it lands on still runs — so it must never appear in the envelope's
`routing_skipped=` or a `routing-skips.jsonl` line the way a genuinely
pruned undeclared stage does; conflating the two would assert a stage was
bypassed when it is precisely what will still run. Two boundaries were
deliberately preserved: an UNDECLARED stage is still pruned exactly as
BL-606 always pruned it (declaring `[coder, qa]` still lets coder address
QA directly, skipping the undeclared middle stages) — the rule binds only
what a ticket actually declares, so a docs-only ticket declaring
`[documenter, qa]` is unaffected; and sender judgement over WHERE a
bounce-fix should return to is untouched — the operator ruled that out, so
this adds no default and no coder/QA-prompt routing rule. The rewrite
REDIRECTS rather than REFUSES: a jump lands on the next declared stage
instead of erroring the sender back to re-address it, reusing the
mechanism the non-member branch already had rather than dead-ending a
committed parcel. Enforcement reaches exactly as far as routing already
reaches and no further: a backward bounce, a `rejection_reason`/
`reroute_reason` detour, the `required_stages_routing_enabled` kill switch,
and an unusable (absent/invalid/not-yet-merged) declaration all behave
exactly as they did before this ticket. Sibling contract amended in the
same parcel, not separately: BL-951's own feature file's `full-chain`
Scenario Outline row (asserting a coder→QA hop skips four stages) became
false the moment this landed — a genuine acceptance red, not a stale
assertion — and was removed, with this ticket's own scenario 01 now
carrying that case in its binding, redirected form. Degraded gate: shell +
Babashka only, no mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling wired; gated by
`bl991_binding_stages_property_runner.bb` plus the acceptance scenarios.
The coder's own reach floors on that runner caught a generator defect in
its OWN first draft — a per-run reseeded RNG pinned the declaration to
`no-cleaner` in 40 of 40 runs, leaving the entire non-member branch (the
second hole this ticket exists to close) untested — fixed by advancing one
generator across every run instead of reseeding per run; the coder
separately flagged the identical defect class in BL-1057's own in-flight
runner by note, which the specifier recorded and the hardener fixed hours
later on both BL-1057 and, independently, BL-1069's runner during this
same batch pass — three occurrences of the same class in one day. Updated
the "Dynamic Routing via Specifier-Declared
required_stages" section and added a "declared stage is binding" guardrail
to `swarmforge/handoff-protocol.md`, and cross-referenced the binding rule
from `docs/how-to/BL-623-routing-skip-trail-records-actual-hop.md` (whose
own worked examples all use an undeclared-middle-stage shape and remain
accurate unchanged). No new extension command or setting — swarm-substrate
handoff-routing tooling under `swarmforge/scripts/`.)

`WINDOW_SIZE_MANUAL` is set, fixed upstream in tmux >= 3.7 (commit
`6234d79`) but absent from Ubuntu's 3.4 package; `./swarm ensure` restores
the agents but the server crashes again within minutes. Three of the
landed hotfix's five review goals were confirmed real defects and fixed
narrowly in place, not reimplemented. The most load-bearing: the version
warning read `tmux -V`, the CLIENT on PATH, while the incident's own
signature is a client that is already fine (3.7b) in front of a SERVER
that predates the install (3.4) — so the landed warning was silent in
exactly the state the crash loop lives in. The judgement now reads `tmux
-S <socket> display-message -p '#{version}'`, the server the swarm is
actually talking to, falling back to the client only when no server
answers. Second: `prefer_local_tmux_bin` prepended `~/.local/bin`
whenever a tmux existed there with no version comparison at all, so a
host whose local build was OLDER than the one already on PATH was
silently downgraded by the function meant to upgrade it — it now compares
before preferring, on both macOS and Linux, since the prepend fired on
both. Third: `install_tmux_wsl.sh`'s guard
`[[ -z "$SRC" || ! -x "$SRC" && ! -f "$SRC" ]]` didn't mean what it read
as (`&&` binds tighter inside `[[ ]]`, so it reduced to `-z "$SRC"` alone)
and the installer downloaded an unpinned, unverified, x86_64-only build;
it now resolves against a table of architectures that actually have a
published build (refusing by name otherwise) and verifies a sha256 digest
before installing anything — with `KNOWN_SHA256` deliberately empty (a
digest is a pin, and pinning is a human commit, never an agent action), a
caller passes `TMUX_INSTALL_SHA256=<digest>` until a human adds a row. The
soft-hardening knobs (`focus-events off` on both the shell and Babashka
paths) were confirmed to never fail an `ensure`/launch/restore even when
the running tmux rejects them; `window-size largest` was investigated
(goal 4) and ultimately removed entirely by a same-day follow-up, BL-1075 — it
contended with the extension's own tiling panel, which
periodically puts the same server back into `window-size manual` (the
exact tmux 3.4 crash trigger) on every role-set change. Degraded gate,
recorded explicitly: the whole diff is shell + Babashka, so no
mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling applies; the gate is the runners under
`swarmforge/scripts/test/` plus the acceptance scenarios. Runbook
`docs/how-to/BL-tmux-wsl-segfault-upgrade.md` (already existed from the
hand-landed hotfix, updated in place for the digest requirement and the
`window-size largest` removal) was missing from `docs/index.md` — added.
No new extension command or setting; this is swarm/ops tooling only.)

BL-1015: the acting half of the
`boy-scout` epic. `node extension/out/tools/boyScoutRun.js [path-to-root]`
takes BL-1014's scan, reads an already-written cleanup proposal for the
top-ranked item from `.swarmforge/boy-scout/proposal.json` (whole new file
content per path, `after: null` to delete — no patch/diff format), and
either commits it or refuses the whole thing and states why. This run does
not generate the cleanup itself; it bounds and verifies one someone else
already wrote, because a generator that invented its own edits would have
no bound on it at all. The size envelope (3 files, 120 changed lines) is
derived from BL-634's recorded 65-insertion slice median, not chosen by
taste — a proposal at or under both limits is eligible, over either one is
refused whole and never partially applied. Every check that can refuse or
abandon runs before the first write, in order: nothing ranked; no proposal
or an empty one; the proposal names the wrong item or trespasses onto a
different ranked item's files; the diff, applied, changes nothing
measurable; the envelope is exceeded; an existing test assertion would have
to change to reach green (invariant 2 — checked verbatim as a multiset
across every language this repo tests in, so a cleanup can never smuggle in
a behaviour change wearing a refactor's clothes); the repository's existing
gate set (`npm test` in `extension/`, the same gate every pipeline role
already runs — this ticket adds no gate and weakens none) fails on the
written result, restoring the tree from a pre-write snapshot. A run that
clears every check commits exactly the paths it edited and nothing else —
never `git add -A`, which would sweep in unrelated dirt and would commit
the proposal file itself since it lives under `.swarmforge/` — staging only
the paths git does not already track and unstaging them again on a failed
add/commit, so a failure never leaves a partial commit sitting in the
index. Invariant 3: a run that cleans nothing always states which of the
six declared reasons applied (`nothing-ranked`, `no-cleanup-proposed`,
`wrong-item`, `envelope-exceeded`, `assertion-would-change`,
`gate-failed`) — a quiet no-op is otherwise indistinguishable from a clean
repository. New reference doc: `docs/reference/BL-1015-boy-scout-run.md`,
cross-linked from BL-1014's own doc and `docs/index.md`.)

BL-1066: the panel's mean-ticket-time
metric recomputed on the 2-second stage-poll tick, and one computation
walked `git log --follow` once per closed ticket — 794 `.yaml` files under
`backlog/done/` on this host (the lister recurses into milestone
subdirectories, so the corpus is larger than what sits flat in the
directory), at ~0.128s per walk, about 102 seconds of git per computation
scheduled every 2 seconds. The measured host effect was sustained
multi-core git saturation and `[git] <defunct>` zombies. The corrected
diagnosis (recorded because it changes the fix): `gitFollowHistory` uses
`execFileSync`, so one call's 794 walks always ran strictly sequentially —
the concurrency was between overlapping/repeated invocations of a call that
was simply far too slow for its own timer, not a fan-out within one call. A
new pure, `vscode`-free module, `extension/src/metrics/metricsTickGate.ts`,
is now owned by `swarmPanel.ts` as a persistent private field: a tick may
never re-enter a computation for the same target path that is still
running, and may not start a new one until the standing value has aged
past a 5-minute refresh interval — every tick still republishes a complete
metrics object, it is simply not recomputed on every one. Re-pointing the
panel at a different target (`updateTarget`) takes effect immediately
because the gate is keyed by subject, so a switch never serves the
previous repo's stale mean for the rest of the interval.
`computeMeanTicketTime` (`swarmMetrics.ts`) itself no longer shells one
`git log --follow` per file: it runs a single
`git log --full-history -M --name-status -- backlog`, indexes every
arrival (rename or add) by the path arrived at, and reads each ticket's
activation time out of that shared index by walking its rename chain —
one git subprocess per computation regardless of corpus size
(`MEAN_TICKET_TIME_GIT_SUBPROCESS_BOUND = 1`, exported and asserted).
`--full-history` and `-M` are both load-bearing for correctness, not
performance flags: default git history simplification silently prunes a
side branch whose net effect on `backlog/` was nothing — exactly the shape
of a reopen-then-reclose merged back in — and was measured to drop real
commits on the live repo without them. Checked against a deterministic
101-ticket sample of the live `backlog/done/` corpus: 98 identical
durations between the old and new algorithm, 0 that differ, 0 lost, 3
tickets the old per-file `--follow` could not measure that the new walk
can. One pre-existing, deliberately-unchanged semantic: a ticket's
measured duration ends at its file's LATEST arrival at its current path,
so a ticket re-filed after close still reports a duration inflated by the
time until the re-file — unchanged from pre-BL-1066 behavior and pinned by
a named test; flagged for the specifier as a possible separate ticket, not
addressed here. Measured on this host: git processes per computation 801 →
1, wall clock ~89s → ~815ms, on a schedule of every 2s → every 300s. No
new extension command or setting; the panel's mean-ticket-time tile still
updates and refreshes, now on its slower cadence, with correctness
unchanged and the per-tick git-subprocess storm gone. Architecture diagram
(`docs/diagrams/architecture.mmd`) updated with the new `metricsTickGate.ts`
node and its edge into `swarmMetrics.ts`.)

BL-1058: the entire shell test lane was
dark on a GNU/Linux host. `swarmforge/scripts/test/lib/tmp_cleanup.sh`
created its registry with `mktemp -t swarmforge-tmp-cleanup-registry` —
BSD/macOS syntax, where the operand is a prefix; GNU coreutils reads the
operand as a TEMPLATE and requires three trailing X's, so the call was a
hard error (`mktemp: too few X's in template ...`). Every one of the 83
shell test files that source this helper does so at the top under
`set -euo pipefail`, so the failed command substitution killed the script
before a single test body ran — including the helper's own suite, which is
why nothing caught this until the host moved from macOS to WSL2/Linux on
2026-08-22. The call is now `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/swarmforge-tmp-cleanup-registry.XXXXXX"`:
an explicit path template with six X's and no dialect-specific flag,
accepted identically by both userlands; TMPDIR is still honoured so
dropping `-t` does not silently relocate anyone's fixtures. A registry that
still cannot be created now fails loud and by name (naming the tmp-cleanup
registry and the directory), rather than propagating mktemp's own message
and leaving `set -u` to surface an unbound-variable error at some later,
unrelated `register_tmp_dir` call. BL-801's design — the registry as a FILE
keyed per top-level process, swept by a `while read` EXIT trap that touches
no array index — is untouched; only the creation call changed. The seam
that makes either dialect's exclusive syntax catchable on either host going
forward is a new mktemp shim on PATH modelling exactly one userland at a
time (`swarmforge/scripts/test/lib/mktemp_dialect_shim.sh`), with one
implementation and three consumers (the shell suite sources it, the
acceptance handlers exec it as a CLI, the property test drives it through
the same CLI) so no lane can end up modelling a userland the others do not.
Hardener verification, same ticket: `test_tmp_cleanup_lib.sh` 17/17
(scenarios 07-09 cover init under both dialects, the sweep across every
dialect × registration-site × ending combination, and the fail-loud path),
the property test 3/3 against both declared invariants, acceptance 9/9,
the full standing guard sweep 13/13, BL-113 Gherkin mutation 20/20 killed.
Non-vacuity was proven by hand-reverting the fix and reproducing the
original "too few X's" failure verbatim, then restoring it and reconfirming
green. TOOLING FALLBACK: shell-only, no `.ts`/`src` touched, so
Stryker/CRAP/DRY do not apply — the shell lane's only gate is its own unit
suite, and the hardener compensated with the hand-mutation above rather
than reporting a mutation/CRAP result that was never run. No extension
command, setting, or UI changed — pure test infrastructure, and the class
of failure this ticket exists to close (a bare mktemp dialect error at
source time, silencing every test in the file) is now caught by the
helper's own suite instead of only discoverable by a host migration.)

was ever signalled; repairing the enumeration is exactly what arms a reap
scoped to `swarmforge-bubble` to reach the operator's live tunnel, so

fixture tunnels before its first process-table assertion, selecting by the

invariants — a fixture can never bind a name any outside process could be
serving, and a run's reap can never select a pid it did not create — against
the lib's pure decision seam, with the operator's real tunnel present only

BL-1028: `promote_and_route_next.sh`
staged its `paused → active` rename with `git mv` and then asked
`commit_integrity_cli.bb` to commit it, but answered every non-zero exit —
`:no-git-dir`, `:lock-timeout`, `:add-failed`, `:commit-failed`,
`:verify-mismatch`, and a close-guard rejection alike — with a raw, unlocked
`git add`/`git commit` fallback. That `||` fires only when the CLI is
present and refused (the CLI-absent case already has its own `else`
branch), so the fallback's entire job was to override refusals, including
the two shapes — `:lock-timeout` and `:verify-mismatch` — that mean a
concurrent writer is live in the shared master checkout, exactly the case
the lock exists to serialise; commit_integrity's own header says callers
must never answer with a hand-rolled commit that races the roles committing
to `main`, and this caller did precisely that. When the fallback itself
failed, the staged `git mv` was left in the shared index with nothing to
unwind it. A refusal is now obeyed: the two paths this script staged
(`backlog/paused/<ticket>`, `backlog/active/<ticket>`) are snapshotted with
`ls-files --stage` before the `mv` and replayed with `update-index
--index-info` on refusal — never a blanket `git reset`, which on this
shared checkout would also discard another role's staged work — restoring
the ticket to `backlog/paused/` and exiting non-zero naming the refusal
reason. Reason extraction reads both refusal shapes: a `:success false`
refusal prints its JSON on stdout plus a `FAILED (reason)` line on stderr,
while a close-guard rejection exits before the JSON is ever produced and
prints only a `CLOSE BLOCKED` line — reading just one shape reported
`unknown` for the other. The CLI-absent `else` branch (a target repo that
never had the integrity guard) is deliberate degradation and stays
unchanged, now logging out loud that it committed without the guard so
that path is never mistaken for a guarded one. No extension command,
setting, or UI change — this is a swarm-machinery correctness fix to an
existing promotion call site, not user-visible behavior. Hardener pass,
same ticket: shell suite 8/8, property runner 30/30 across 5 refusal
shapes plus novel/unknown reason names, acceptance 10/10, BL-113 Gherkin
mutation 8/8 killed; independently re-derived one non-vacuity break beyond
the coder's own authoring-time proofs (keying the refusal guard on
`INTEGRITY_RC == 1` instead of `!= 0` survives the shell suite, which only
ever exits 1, but is killed by the property runner's non-1 exit codes); a
pre-existing, separately-ticketed guard failure (BL-1033) was confirmed an
ancestor of both `main` and `origin/main` before this merge, and left
alone as not this parcel's fix.
