in place rather than duplicated. Hardener pass, same ticket: extracted the
served/not-served comparison into a pure `build-served-fact?` (mirroring
BL-1035's own `own-heartbeat-ms` shape) so its `>=` boundary is directly
testable rather than only reachable through an already-resolved boolean —
behavior-preserving, no observable change. Prior entry —
BL-1041: a new CLI,
`swarmforge/scripts/rescue_orphaned_work.bb`, rescues work sitting outside
any branch (a stash entry with no worktree, most often) without the rescue
itself becoming the way the work gets lost. On 2026-08-22 a reviewed-sound
fix was applied out of a stash into a role's worktree and the stash entry
was dropped in the SAME operation — for about an hour its only two copies
were an uncommitted working tree and an evidence file a specifier had
happened to hand-copy elsewhere; a `git restore` in that window would have
destroyed it. The CLI now commits the rescued content onto a branch, reads
that commit's content back out and compares it to disk, and only THEN drops
the source stash entry — guarded explicitly (`source-release-allowed?`), so
it cannot be reached by falling through. The changed-path set is read from
the stash itself (`--include-untracked`) before the apply touches the
worktree, not derived from a post-apply `git diff`, which an architect
bounce found could sweep the receiving role's own pre-existing uncommitted
work into the rescue commit or miss a stash whose orphaned work was a
brand-new untracked file. The role whose worktree is touched is now told: a
capped (80-char) `note` names the file count and the commit sha, trimming
the reason before ever trimming the sha, since the sha is what makes the
note actionable. See
[the rescue how-to](../how-to/BL-1041-rescue-orphaned-work.md). Prior entry —
BL-1036: a front-desk restart now releases
its Telegram `getUpdates` slot instead of leaving the replacement to poll
straight into a 409 conflict, and the supervisor log now closes every
degradation it opens. Root cause, confirmed from the code rather than
assumed (the ticket required this): the bot installed no signal handler
anywhere and `defaultPost` called `fetch` with no `signal`, so SIGTERM
killed it instantly mid-long-poll with the request still open, and Telegram
held that slot until its own ~25s server-side timeout — the replacement's
first poll landed inside it. Twelve respawns, twelve conflicts, 04:30–06:14Z
2026-08-22. This **refutes** the intake's leading remedy: a longer
graceful-shutdown window could not have helped, because
`FRONT_DESK_KILL_GRACE_MS` was never reached — the child was already dead.
An unconditional pre-poll wait was rejected on the same evidence, since it
would tax every clean restart to pay for the unclean one. **The fix**:
`signal?: AbortSignal` is threaded through `TelegramPostFn` →
`callTelegramApi` → `getTelegramUpdates` (added last in each signature, so
every existing caller is unaffected); the bot creates one `AbortController`
per poll cycle and installs SIGTERM/SIGINT handlers that abort before
exiting, which is what actually closes the connection and frees the slot.
A child that ignores SIGTERM is unchanged and still bounded by the existing
backoff (this ticket makes restarts cheap, not restarts rarer — that is
BL-1037). **The observability half**: `describePollConflictWindow` stops
the degraded-poll log line from repeating Telegram's own misdirecting
"make sure that only one bot instance is running" text and instead names
the cause (`conflict window: our own predecessor poll still holds the
getUpdates slot; it is released when that long poll times out server-side,
within 25s`); and where 626,860 lines of `front-desk-supervisor.log`
previously contained not one recovery line, every `poll degraded` line is
now followed by exactly one of `poll recovered - polling normally again`
or `poll UNRESOLVED - still failing after the retry budget: <cause>` —
derived from the existing consecutive-failure/outage state, no new flag to
keep in step. Outstanding, by design: the ticket's own qa_e2e step 5 is a
live check against real Telegram (the conflict window is server-side state
no fixture can establish) and is not claimed done by this parcel. Prior
entry —
BL-1035: a respawned front-desk bot is now
judged on its own heartbeat, not its dead predecessor's, closing a restart
loop that could burn the bot's whole bounded restart budget in seconds.
`front_desk_supervisor_lib.bb`'s `poll-heartbeat-stale?` waived staleness
during the startup grace only when `last-heartbeat-ms` was `nil` — but the
heartbeat is a FILE
(`.swarmforge/operator/front-desk-poll-heartbeat.json`), rewritten by the
bot every completed poll cycle and reset by nobody at spawn. So after any
restart of a bot that had not been polling successfully, the supervisor read
the dead instance's already-stale timestamp, the nil-guard never fired, and
the replacement was declared stalled on its first tick — observed live,
06:13:56 spawned / 06:13:58 stalled / 06:14:02 respawned, against a 90s
grace written to cover the first long-poll cycle. The predicate now derives
`own-heartbeat-ms`: a heartbeat timestamp older than this child's own
`started-at-ms` carries no information about it and is treated as absent,
exactly as a genuinely missing heartbeat always was — comparing timestamps
rather than clearing the file at spawn, so it stays correct when the file is
missing, unreadable, or written by a bot that outlived a *supervisor*
restart. The waiver stays scoped to the grace window only, so a replacement
that genuinely never polls is still caught once its grace expires (BL-370's
original fault stays fixed). Three of six call sites share this predicate
and inherit the fix (`front_desk_supervisor.bb`, the reported fault;
`cursor_bridge_supervisor.bb`; `bridge_headless_supervisor.bb`); two callers
using the 3-arity form are byte-for-byte unaffected. Split 1 of 3 from the
same restart-storm intake — BL-1036 (a Telegram 409 on every respawn) and
BL-1037 (build-freshness restart cadence) are independent root causes, not
addressed here. No new command, setting, or log-format change — the
supervisor log still records each stall with the window it exceeded, per the
intake's own standing constraint. Prior entry —
BL-1014: a new on-demand, read-only CLI
(`node extension/out/tools/boyScoutScan`) ranks the repo's technical debt by
cross-source RECURRENCE rather than re-judged severity, across five live
evidence sources — deferred hardening gates, bounce recurrence (by
failure-class/role pair; per-file join is deferred), CRAP-over-threshold,
jscpd duplication, and counted runtime/ops bloat (rotated logs, mailbox
directories) — printing a ranked inventory with a checkable evidence pointer
per item. Recurrence (distinct-source count, not row count) is the whole
rank key because it is the only definition of "most annoying" that is
measurable rather than re-argued every run, which is also what makes two
runs over the same repository state produce an identical ranking. A source
that cannot be read is reported `NOT CONSULTED`, never silently folded into
"clean". Slice 1 of the new `boy-scout` epic; slice 2 (BL-1015) is what acts
on the ranking — this slice only ranks and reports, and writes nothing but
its own report to stdout. See
[the Boy Scout scan reference](BL-1014-boy-scout-scan.md). Prior entry —
BL-1011: a freshness alarm now names
which swarm sent it and which of three conditions produced its sentinel
age, in both the Telegram announce and the durable incident record.
`heartbeat_age_secs` (`daemon_log_freshness_check.sh`) returned the literal
`999999999` for three different unmeasurable conditions — the log file
missing, the log with no heartbeat line, or an unparseable newest-heartbeat
timestamp — and `process_daemon` interpolated that straight into
`age_secs=${age}` as though it were a real age, while the checker's own
swarm-name resolution lived only inside the branch that fills in missing
Telegram credentials, so a checkout whose credentials were already exported
never computed it and announced anonymously. Both together are why five
`age_secs=999999999` alarms received 2026-08-21 10:58-11:06 BST could not be
attributed to any host after a full investigation of the receiving one.
`resolve_swarm_name` is hoisted out of the credential branch and now runs
unconditionally (falling back to `primary`, never empty); `heartbeat_age_secs`
now returns `"<age> <reason>"`, and `render_age` is the one place an age
becomes human-facing text, mapping the sentinel to the word `unknown` rather
than a raw number. Every announce and every incident record now carries
`swarm=` and `reason=` (`log-absent`, `no-heartbeat-line`,
`unparseable-timestamp`, or `stale-heartbeat`) alongside the existing
`age_secs=`. See
[the freshness-watchdog how-to](../how-to/BL-675-daemon-log-freshness-watchdog.md).
Prior entry — BL-1010: a secondary swarm now publishes
fleet status under its own name instead of silently clobbering the
primary's. `holisticProjections.ts`'s `readSwarmName` read only
`swarmforge.conf`, defaulting to `primary` when the key was absent, and
never consulted `.swarmforge/swarm-identity` — the file `swarmforge.sh`'s
launcher actually writes and the file Babashka's own `swarm_identity_lib.bb`
already reads first. The two agreed on the Mac primary only by coincidence,
which is exactly what kept the bug invisible there. `readSwarmName` now
resolves identity file, then conf, then the shared default — the same order
as the Babashka resolver, with a test asserting the two languages' default
literals agree since no import can bridge them. A checkout with no compiled
`extension/out` (the WSL2 secondary-swarm shape that surfaced this ticket)
now gets a `handoffd.bb` fleet-status error naming the actual bring-up step
(`npm install && npm run compile` in `extension/`) instead of node's bare
module-not-found. See "The fleet is a composite of swarms" below. Prior
entry — BL-1022: the daemon's subprocess-API gate
now walks spawn edges, not only load-file edges, closing the blind spot that
let BL-1021's banned `clojure.java.shell` call sit unseen on the daemon's
critical path. `daemon_cycle_guard_lib_test_runner.bb`'s closure check
(BL-967) had one edge kind: `handoffd.bb` reaches `swarm_handoff.bb` by
*spawning* it, not loading it, so the walk never visited it or anything it
loads, and the gate read green while missing the file that took production
down. `resolve-daemon-reachability` (`master_checkout_drift_lib.bb`) now
follows `:load` and `:spawn` edges together, transitively and mutually
recursive, reading spawn vectors as Clojure data (`read-string`) rather than
regex-matching them so real nesting and quoting resolve correctly; three
shapes resolve statically (a bare literal, a literal behind path plumbing, a
same-file zero-arg helper), and anything else is reported as `:unresolved`
and fails the gate loudly rather than being silently skipped — the same
class of blind spot one level up. The gate also now reports `:reached-by` per
file (`:entrypoint` / `[:load f]` / `[:spawn f]`), so a closure that
silently shrinks is visible instead of passing for the wrong reason. The
pre-existing load-only entry point (`resolve-daemon-executed-paths`, the
BL-839 master-checkout drift check) is unchanged in behavior by design — it
now delegates to the same walk restricted to `:load` — since widening what
the drift check compares against `main` is a different, un-taken decision
from widening what the subprocess-API ban covers. Following the new edge
grew the daemon's reachable closure from 38 files to 53 and surfaced three
more files still carrying an unbounded `clojure.java.shell`/`process/sh`
call, reached transitively through the `swarm_handoff.bb` spawn:
`handoff_inject_lib.bb` (tmux), `pre_qa_gate_gather_lib.bb` (git), and
`salvage_lib.bb` (generic). Removing the banned API from any of the three is
explicitly out of this ticket's scope (BL-1021's kind of follow-up), so the
gate holds them as a named ratchet instead — an equality assertion, not a
subset, so a new offender fails it and so does a stale entry still listed
after a fix — and a `note` was sent to the specifier naming all three rather
than fixing or silently dropping them here. No extension command, setting,
or UI change — an internal `swarmforge/`-fork test-gate fix, gated by its own
unit/property suites (`daemon_cycle_guard_lib_test_runner.bb`,
`master_checkout_drift_lib_test_runner.bb`,
`bl1022_daemon_closure_property_runner.bb`) since Babashka has no
mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling wired. Acceptance:
[`specs/features/BL-1022-daemon-guard-closure-follows-process-spawn-edges.feature`](../../specs/features/BL-1022-daemon-guard-closure-follows-process-spawn-edges.feature),
4/4; runbook updated in the same parcel:
[`docs/how-to/BL-967-handoffd-cycle-stall-diagnosis.md`](../how-to/BL-967-handoffd-cycle-stall-diagnosis.md).); Previously
August 22, 2026 (BL-1018: what a single-role tmux session
repair may resolve to is now pinned to one pure definition,
`single_role_repair_lib.bb`'s `resolve-single-role-repair`, so repairing one
role's vanished session can never again reach the whole pack server. On
2026-08-21 ~08:26 UTC an operator single-role respawn of the specifier — the
existing shape, create the session then `respawn-pane` the launch script into
it — brought down the ENTIRE pack tmux server (socket, `handoffd`, all eight
sessions); no audit trail survived the teardown so the root mechanism is
UNPROVEN, and this ticket does not claim otherwise (BL-958's leading
hypothesis: a respawn issued against a missing session can restart a
half-alive server). The value doesn't rest on that hypothesis — constraining
what a repair may resolve to removes the whole family of ways it could reach
the server, whichever member fired. The resolver is pure (returns commands,
never runs them) with two branches that are deliberately not one command with
a flag flipped: a missing session resolves to ONE `new-session` that carries
the launch command directly, never followed by a respawn into it; a present
session resolves to ONE `respawn-pane -k` in place, never a duplicate create.
Every command is built through one constructor that prepends `tmux -S
<socket>`, so naming the socket explicitly can't be a rule an individual call
site forgets, and a refusal (blank socket/session/launch script) resolves to
NO commands rather than a best-effort one with a hole in it. Both real
callers — `babysitter_check.bb`'s `ensure-role-session!` (BL-1017's own
automated repair path, this ticket supersedes its create-then-respawn shape
described when BL-1017 shipped, see the entry below and
[the runbook](../how-to/BL-611-babysitterd-runbook.md#bounded-session-repair-for-a-vanished-standing-role-bl-1017))
and `swarm_ensure.bb`'s `ensure-standing-role!` — now resolve through it and
only run the result; `handoffd.bb`'s `do-respawn!` is deliberately NOT
converted (it respawns into a pane it just captured text from, so it can
never hit the missing-session shape, and already names `-S` explicitly),
flagged for the architect as the natural next consumer rather than silently
skipped. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** a launch-script path containing an
apostrophe (a real shape — e.g. a macOS home directory) broke the resolved
shell command outright — the resolver wrapped it in bare unescaped single
quotes, producing a string `tmux` hands to `$SHELL -c` that is not valid
shell syntax, confirmed live by feeding the exact string to `sh -c` (exits 2,
unexpected-EOF). Fixed with a proper POSIX single-quote escape
(close-quote/escaped-quote/reopen-quote); the property runner's own
substring-match assertion could never have caught this (an unescaped embed
still contains the substring; a correctly-escaped one no longer does either),
so it was replaced with a real shell round-trip through `sh -c`. Both
declared invariants — no resolved command ever affects another role's
session, and none is ever a kill-server/kill-session — are encoded in a
400-run property suite with an asserted reachability floor per shape,
verified non-vacuous by three independent breaks (dropping `-S`: 234
failures; resolving a missing session to create-then-respawn: 123; a refusal
returning its would-be command: 65). No extension command, setting, or UI
change — an internal `swarmforge/`-fork daemon safety fix. Acceptance:
[`specs/features/BL-1018-single-role-respawn-never-kills-the-server.feature`](../../specs/features/BL-1018-single-role-respawn-never-kills-the-server.feature),
4/4; live kill-one-session confirmation left as a manual QA procedure,
outside the unit testability boundary (real tmux).); Previously
August 22, 2026 (BL-582: a silently no-op Approve tap now
says so, durably, and a healthy front-desk bot stops serving a stale build
past a grace period. Three hardening gaps closed together, none of which
settle the ticket's still-open root-cause question (BL-588 and BL-1026 both
show a tap failing to record on a build the supervisor considered fresh):
(a) every callback drop path now emits a distinguishable diagnostic —
`not-my-chat`/`not-principal` taps stay answered NEVER (answering an
unauthorized tap would confirm the bot exists to a stranger) but are now
logged, while an unrecognized `callback_data` and a record that changed
nothing both answer with a toast naming why, via a new optional
`onDecisionRecorded` hook on `recordApprovalDecisionAndClose`
(`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) that answers the callback the instant the
record outcome is known rather than up front, since a callback query can
only be answered once. `pendingApprovalReply.ts`'s new
`classifyApprovalRecordNoOp`/`explainApprovalRecordNoOp` turn
`recordApprovalReply`'s bare boolean into one of six named reasons; a no-op
record now counts as `dropped`, not `posted`, in poll telemetry. (b) the
approval write already commits itself (BL-892's `commitApprovalDecision`),
now gated by a scenario so a future edit cannot quietly repoint it. (c)
`front_desk_supervisor_lib.bb` checks build freshness on the HEALTHY tick,
not only on a crash respawn — the reason a healthy bot served a stale build
for 2h23m on 2026-07-23. A newly-stale build starts a grace
(`FRONT_DESK_BUILD_GRACE_MS`, default 5 minutes); past the grace the
process restarts through the same bounded-backoff clause a crash uses.
**BL-1037 bounds how often that may happen.** A child restarted onto a fresh
build must complete one poll cycle on it before the watchdog may restart it
again — otherwise a `main` that moves faster than one grace plus
recompile-and-respawn costs a restart per commit (24 staleness detections and
12 respawns in 105 minutes on 2026-08-22, each paying a Telegram conflict
window). The staleness is **carried, not cleared**, while it waits: a deferred
restart is still owed and fires the moment the child serves, so this bounds
the rate without reopening the 2h23m stale-serving window. Deferrals are
logged as `build-stale-deferred` so the pause is visible rather than inferred
from a restart that did not happen.
Every diagnostic now lands in a new durable sink,
`.swarmforge/operator/front-desk-diagnostics.log`, closing the gap that
left the 2026-07-23 failure window with no bot output preserved anywhere.
New human-facing surface: a failed Approve tap now clears its spinner with
a toast naming why instead of clearing silently, and a stale-build front
desk self-heals within the grace window of a merge rather than serving the
old build indefinitely.); Previously

No new command or setting; the front-desk bot now names the real error on

August 21, 2026 (BL-1021: closes a critical live
handoffd deadlock — the dispatch-gap sweep froze in an uninterruptible wait,
eight log rotations on 2026-08-21, five in the ninety minutes before the
report, restart resetting only the clock. Root cause was the BL-057/BL-061
`clojure.java.shell` deadlock family recurring one process hop past the
BL-967 gate: `dispatch-gap-sweep!` doesn't *load* its collaborator
`swarm_handoff.bb`, it *spawns* it, an edge type the BL-967 closure-gate walk
never follows, so `swarm_handoff.bb` still shelled out via
`clojure.java.shell/sh` — no timeout at all — on all nine of its own
subprocess sites. Two independent halves, both required. (1) The bound
itself had a hole even for code already routed through it:
`daemon_cycle_guard_lib.bb`'s `sh!` bounded only the exit-code wait,
`(deref proc bound ::timed-out)`; when the direct child exited promptly but
something it spawned kept the inherited stdout/stderr write ends open,
`babashka.process` then resolved the `:out`/`:err` stream-pump futures with
NO bound, blocking in `read()` forever because the pipe never reached EOF —
`destroy-tree` and the timeout log line were both downstream of the timeout
branch and so never fired, which is why the log showed no timeout at all. A
deterministic control/defect pair settled this rather than leaving it
conjectured: a direct child that never exits still timed out correctly at
the bound; a child that exits immediately but leaves a backgrounded
grandchild holding the pipe did not return even 20s past a 3s bound. `sh!`
now derefs the exit wait and the stream drain together, inside one future
under the same deadline, so the bound holds at any process depth; the
exception contract is unchanged (a throw from the drain still propagates to
the caller as itself, not wrapped as the future's `ExecutionException`).
(2) `swarm_handoff.bb` moved off `clojure.java.shell` entirely — its
`command` wrapper (8 call sites) plus one direct call now route through the
existing `daemon-cycle-guard-lib/sh!` chokepoint, already in scope via
`handoff_lib.bb`'s load-file chain, so no new wiring was needed. Behavior
change worth knowing: this applies to all nine sites, not only the ones the
daemon reaches — `swarm_handoff.bb` is also the CLI every pipeline role's
`swarm_handoff.sh` invokes directly to send a handoff, so any git/tmux call
there that legitimately runs long now returns `exit 124` after the 60s
default (`SWARMFORGE_SUBPROCESS_WAIT_BOUND_MS`) instead of blocking
indefinitely. Deliberately NOT done: widening the BL-967 closure gate to
follow process-spawn edges generically, so this class of hole cannot recur
elsewhere — filed separately as BL-1022, so this critical-severity fix could
move at the speed it needed; and the freshness watchdog's restart behavior
(BL-1012), unchanged. Verified with a new four-scenario acceptance feature
(`specs/features/BL-1021-daemon-subprocess-cannot-outlive-its-wait-bound.feature`)
plus unit and property additions to `daemon_cycle_guard_lib`'s test runners,
independently re-verified at every downstream stage including two
independent break-and-restore repros against the pre-fix code. No extension
command, setting, or UI change — this is an internal swarm-daemon
reliability fix in the `swarmforge/` fork, the same category as BL-967, whose
runbook is updated in the same parcel:
[`docs/how-to/BL-967-handoffd-cycle-stall-diagnosis.md`](../how-to/BL-967-handoffd-cycle-stall-diagnosis.md).);

intermediate process exits, so the registration entry always precedes any
state a reaper sweep could observe — no register-then-orphan race window.

group…`), with the detached job's own bash wrapper separately trapping
SIGTERM to leave a `[detach_job] KILLED by SIGTERM` notice before dying, so
an agent collecting a run discovers the reaping from its own artifacts
rather than a supervisor log (invariant 3). A housekeeping pass prunes dead
registry entries past a 120s grace period so the registry can never
accumulate stale files. No `job-process-pattern` narrowing and no argv
disguising — both were considered and refused, since either would hide a
true positive. No VS Code-facing command or setting; this is swarm role
machinery. See `docs/how-to/BL-995-detached-job-registry.md`.

naming registration as mandatory, tracked separately per the ticket's own
notes.); Previously

the bridge served this session, what is cached, and which shell is
installed into one of four outcomes — FRESH (a newer served bundle),
CACHED (nothing newer, or the served bundle was rejected), STALE (bridge
unreachable, cached bundle rendered but marked unconfirmed), or BARE
(native Talk only, no bundle usable from either source) — and always
returns cleanly so a caller can always fall back to native Talk. A bundle
whose `minShellVersion` exceeds the installed shell's own version is never
returned as FRESH regardless of recency, falling through to CACHED or BARE
with a shell-behind reason a later slice turns into an update prompt —
rendering a bundle the shell can't honour is how a remote-UI app bricks
itself on a phone the human can't easily reach. `BridgeClient.resolveUiBundle`
is the device edge (HTTP fetch distinguishing an unreachable bridge from a
reachable one that answered badly, one atomically-written cache file,

## Overview

A VS Code extension that runs a multi-agent coding swarm and brings the work back as a PR. It is a **standalone orchestrator** — inspired by Uncle Bob's SwarmForge agent-orchestration model, but it spawns and manages the agent processes itself rather than driving SwarmForge or tmux. The extension lives entirely in the forge codebase. It points at any target project, runs the swarm on it, and brings the work back as a PR. The target project carries only two swarm bootstrap files and otherwise has no knowledge of the swarm machinery.

**Getting started?** See [Getting Started with SwarmForge VC](../tutorials/GettingStarted.md) for install, setup, and first run. This specification is the detailed reference.

**Diagrams:** [Architecture diagram](../diagrams/architecture.mmd) and
[Swarm workflow flow diagram](../diagrams/swarm-flow.mmd) (Mermaid sources)
depict the system as actually built. Flagging a doc/code disagreement here
per BL-095: the Overview paragraph above describes a "standalone
orchestrator" that spawns and manages agent processes itself — the code
does not do this. The extension drives an unmodified, separately-installed
SwarmForge over tmux and reads its `.swarmforge/` state files (see
`swarmforge/constitution/articles/local-engineering.prompt` and
`swarmDiscovery.ts`'s own BL-066 note); it never spawns agent processes
directly. The diagrams reflect the tmux-driving architecture.

---

## Core Design Principles

| Principle | What it means |
|---|---|
| **Forge owns the tooling** | All extension code, generic role prompts, and reusable tools built by the swarm stay in the forge repo |
| **Target stays clean** | Only `project.prompt` and `engineering.prompt` live in the target repo |
| **Target is unaware** | The target repo has no SwarmForge dependency, no lockfile entry, no import |
| **PR is the handoff** | Swarm work returns to the target via a pull request; human always reviews |
| **Human triggers, swarm executes** | The developer kicks off a run manually; the swarm runs autonomously from there |

---

## Relationship to SwarmForge (Inspired By, Not Dependent On)

The extension is a **standalone orchestrator** inspired by SwarmForge — it borrows the *model* (a sequential role pipeline, worktree-per-role, filesystem-mediated handoffs) but spawns and manages the agent processes itself. SwarmForge is **not a runtime dependency**: no fork, no vendored source, no `./swarm` wrapper, no tmux, nothing fetched at setup.

**Platform.** macOS and Linux only — tmux, the process substrate the extension drives (see the doc/code note above, BL-095), has no native Windows implementation. A Windows-hosted swarm runs via WSL2 (a real Linux userland), never natively (BL-091).

**The substrate is process + filesystem, owned in-repo.** The extension runs the swarm through its own thin orchestrator:
- spawns each agent as an `InteractiveProcess` (a `child_process.spawn` shell backend, or an in-process `vscode.lm` runtime — see Agent Backends),
- owns each process's output stream directly (`onData`), which is what makes live tiles, message-bus capture, and input forwarding all work from a single handle,
- reads and writes swarm state under `.swarmforge/` (messages, heartbeats) and `.worktrees/` in the target clone,
- configures swarm shape through this repo's own role/constitution prompt files and pack config — all *configuration in this repo*, not an external dependency.

Almost everything in this spec — hardened comms, watchdog/heartbeat, work tree, tiles, cost logic — sits on top of that owned substrate.

**Reproducibility.** Because the orchestrator, role runtimes, message bus, and all prompts live in this repo and are versioned in git, a given extension version *is* the complete definition of swarm behaviour. Nothing is fetched upstream that could silently change results between two runs of the same version. (The former `dependency-pinning.md` / `swarmforge.lock.json` discipline is therefore retired — there is no upstream artifact to pin.)

**Borrowing from SwarmForge going forward.** Uncle Bob's pipeline shape remains a useful reference; a human may consult it and port ideas deliberately into this repo's prompts or orchestrator. That is a human design act, not an automated fetch — the inspiration never re-enters as a runtime input.

---

## Repository Layout

### Forge Repo (this extension lives here)

```
swarmforge-vscode/
├── extension/                  # VS Code extension source
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── panel/              # Webview panel — tiled agent UI
│   │   ├── orchestrator/       # Agent process orchestrator (spawn, stream, worktrees, lifecycle)
│   │   ├── git/                # PR creation, branch management
│   │   ├── config/             # Target project resolution, pack selection
│   │   └── tools/              # Reusable tools accumulated by the swarm
│   └── package.json
├── roles/                      # Generic role prompts (coordinator, coder, cleaner…)
│   ├── coordinator.prompt
│   ├── coder.prompt
│   ├── cleaner.prompt
│   └── architect.prompt
└── constitution/               # Shared constitution articles
    └── articles/
```

### Target Repo (minimal footprint)

```
target-project/
├── project.prompt              # What this project is, its goals, constraints
├── engineering.prompt          # Tech stack, conventions, architectural rules
└── ... (everything else)
```

The extension clones the target repo and operates via git worktrees — one per agent role, exactly as SwarmForge does natively. The extension does not use a separate temp directory; worktrees are created under `.worktrees/` inside the clone. Nothing is committed to the target's main branch until the PR is merged by the human.
