Explicitly out of scope for this slice: a PWA compose surface and email inbound (both deferred to a possible later slice). **QA bounce: the stale-premise gate now checks the SPECIFIC pending question, not just the ticket.** The original gate only checked ticket-level status/folder, so a ticket that stayed `active`/`todo` throughout while the swarm retracted or superseded its one pending question was still reported live — a stale answer to that retracted question would have been silently accepted as an ordinary inbound message. `blTopicStore.ts` gains a structured per-question signal: an outbound message can carry `retractsPendingQuestion: true`, and `hasRetractedPendingQuestion(record)` is true only when the LATEST message (by seq) is such a retraction — an earlier retraction the swarm has since moved past (e.g. asked again) does not count. `checkPremiseLive` checks this signal after its existing folder/status guards. **The retraction flag now has a real writer, not just test fixtures.** A successful gate answer (`operator_runtime.bb`'s `bl-topic-approval-sweep!` → `operator-decide.js <backlogId> approve`, the consumer of a human reply typed into a ticket's own topic) is the real decision point where that ticket's pending question stops being live — this now threads `retractsPendingQuestion` from that approval path through the reply-outbox/SSE relay to the same `appendMessage` call that already records the confirmation reply, so every real answer path sets the flag, not only hand-built tests. **A human-facing runbook (BL-441) walks through using this channel:** `docs/how-to/BL-441-answering-offline-runbook.md` — reading a pending question from the committed BL topics (`backlog/topics/*.json`), composing and pushing an `ANSWER-*.md`, and the stale-premise caveat. The PWA does **not** currently surface pending-question state (it fetches only `backlog.json`/`docs-tree.json`/`recert-batch.json`, none of which carry that signal — its one human-facing flag, `needsApproval`, is the unrelated swarm-proposal-review mechanism), so the runbook relies on the BL topic files, not the PWA, for offline reading.

**A natural-language contract approval no longer gets misread as an objection and spliced into the contract as a fabricated clause (BL-442).** Live incident, first real end-to-end FES onboarding run 2026-07-15: the human replied "All agreed" in the negotiation topic (BL-381), and because `AGREEMENT_PATTERN`'s anchored `^\s*(agree|agreed|approve|approved|lgtm|yes)[.!]?\s*$` only matched a single bare word, "All agreed" fell through to the objection path — running an unrequested revision round whose `objectToContract` then blind-appended the reply text itself as a new contract boundary line (`"- Per operator objection: All agreed"`), so the contract the human had just approved carried a clause fabricated from the approval that approved it. Two independent fixes, both required: (a) `AGREEMENT_PATTERN` (`negotiationTelegramRouting.ts`) is broadened to also recognize common short natural-language approvals ("all agreed", "ok", "okay") while keeping the pre-existing substring guard intact — an objection that merely *contains* an approval word ("I don't agree that...") is still classified as an objection, never approval; a reply matching neither the approval nor a recognizable-objection shape now lands in a new ambiguous bucket that asks the human to disambiguate in the topic instead of silently running a revision. (b) `reviseContractFromObjection`'s blind-append fallback is removed outright — a revision that cannot derive a concrete contract change from the reply text now leaves the contract byte-unchanged and posts back "couldn't derive a change from this — rephrase?" rather than writing the raw reply as a line; a revision that *can* derive a real change still collapses the embedded reply text to a single line before splicing it in (the BL-409 sibling rule: external text entering a structured file must never carry a raw newline across a line boundary). No new human-facing command; a natural-language "yes" now just ends the negotiation, and no reply — approval or objection — can ever appear verbatim as a contract clause.

**The onboarding contract commit step now actually lands in an arbitrary foreign target, instead of requiring manual git surgery (BL-443).** First real end-to-end FES onboarding run, 2026-07-15: every one of `propose-onboarding-contract`'s three commit-path assumptions broke against a real foreign checkout, and each was worked around by hand at the time. All three fixes live in the one shared seam every bootstrap artifact already commits through (`writeFilesAndCommit`/`writeAndCommitBootstrapPlan`, `extension/src/config/targetBootstrap.ts`). (1) A target whose `.gitignore`/`.git/info/exclude` ignores `.swarmforge/` (FES carried a stale June-era exclude) used to hard-fail `git add` outright — the commit now force-adds exactly the contract paths it just wrote (`git add -f -- .swarmforge/contract.yaml CONTRACT.md`), never a broad `-f`, so an inherited ignore rule can no longer silently re-hold the onboarding gate on every fresh clone. (2) A target with no `user.name`/`user.email` configured anywhere (common on a brand-new or foreign checkout) used to die "Author identity unknown" — the commit now falls back to an explicit identity (`SwarmForge <noreply@swarmforge>`) via `git -c user.name=... -c user.email=...` only when none is configured, and logs that the fallback was used. (3) The existence-only idempotency check used to treat "the file is on disk" as "done," so once defect (1) or (2) aborted a commit, every subsequent re-run reported `committed:false` forever — no number of re-runs ever recovered. The check is now existence-AND-committed (queries `git ls-files`/status for exactly the written paths), so a written-but-uncommitted artifact from a prior partial failure now actually gets committed on the next run, while BL-382's `git diff --cached --quiet` no-op guard still keeps a genuinely-already-committed re-run a clean no-op with no empty commit. No new human-facing command; onboarding a foreign target's contract no longer needs hand git surgery.

**Channel provisioning now follows a group-to-supergroup migration instead of latching the dead pre-migration chat id forever (BL-444).** First real run of `provision-onboarding-telegram-channel` against a genuinely foreign target (free-email-scanner via `@fes_swarm_bot`), 2026-07-15: `decideChannelDetection` (`telegramChannelProvisioning.ts`) picked the FIRST chat id any `getUpdates` batch carried — but the CLI's own documented setup instructions ("create a group ... then enable Topics") are exactly what causes Telegram to silently upgrade a basic group to a supergroup with a brand-new id, emitting `migrate_to_chat_id` updates. The update queue still starts with the dead pre-migration group's own updates, so detection latched that dead id and provisioning failed identically on every re-run — first "the chat is not a forum," then "group chat was upgraded to a supergroup chat" — because the CLI's `getUpdates` offset was hardcoded to `0` on every call, so a re-run always re-saw the same poisoned queue from the start. This is the documented happy path, not an edge case: only a group created as a forum from the outset avoids the migration. Detection now scans every update and follows the newest `migrate_to_chat_id`/`migrate_from_chat_id` signal seen, rather than trusting the first chat id encountered; a `createForumTopic` "upgraded to a supergroup" error now surfaces its own `parameters.migrate_to_chat_id` and provisioning treats it as a redirect to retry against, not a terminal failure; and the CLI persists its `getUpdates` offset, confirming it past every consumed update once provisioning fully succeeds, so a later re-run never re-observes the stale pre-migration queue that poisoned it before. No new human-facing command or setup step — the documented "create a group, then enable Topics" flow is unchanged; it now actually converges.

**Every swarm role now has its own standing Telegram steering topic, and any authorised message posted in it interrupts that role's live pane — no `!` marker required yet (BL-425 slice 1).** Generalizes the single standing Operator topic (BL-346) from one shared channel into ONE topic per role — all 8 (the 7 pipeline roles plus the coordinator, which sits outside `PIPELINE_CHAIN`'s forward chain but still gets its own topic) — a new class of topic alongside the existing per-ticket BL topics and the Operator topic, not a repurposing of either. `ensureRoleTopics` (`telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`) creates each role's forum topic (named for the role) on first sight and records it in a NEW machine-local map, `.swarmforge/operator/role-topic-map.json` (`roleTopicMapStore.ts`, gitignored host-persisted state, keyed by role name directly — no reserved-subject indirection the way the single shared Operator topic needs one). Called once before the poll loop starts, same ordering rationale as `ensureOperatorTopic`: no inbound message can reach an unbound role topic and be misrouted while it is still unbound; one role's failed create is logged and skipped, never blocking the rest. This slice ships REDIRECT mode only — an explicit, DISRUPTIVE steering message. `decideSteeringAction` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) is the pure inbound decision: a message whose topic is not one of the eight role topics is `ignore` (checked first, so the existing BL-ticket/Operator/SUP routing is reached completely untouched — those topics keep their existing behavior); only inside a role topic does the principal guard (BL-239/240's `isFromMyChat`/`isFromPrincipal`, reused verbatim) apply, distinguishing an unauthorised sender (`refuse`, no nudge) from the authorised human (`redirect`). `redirectToRole` (`telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`) executes an authorised redirect as a VERIFIED, INTERRUPTING nudge into role R's live tmux pane via `swarm/verifiedInject.ts`'s `sendInstructionVerified` (never a bare unverified `Enter`, BL-152) on the swarm's own tmux socket (`.swarmforge/tmux-socket`) — the same seam the daily-briefing/idle-clear nudges already inject through, never the restricted front-desk operator's own socket (BL-334). Routing is exact: role R's topic reaches only role R's pane, resolved fresh per redirect via `resolveRolePaneTarget`, never another role's. A redirect against a not-yet-running swarm (no live pane resolved) degrades to a logged no-op rather than throwing. **Not yet built (parked in the companion `.feature.draft` until BL-233 promotes it):** the non-disruptive QUESTION mode — a plain (unmarked) message queued to the agent as a mailbox note it answers back into the topic without pulling it off its task, plus the `!`-prefix mode selector that will make an unmarked message default to QUESTION instead of always resolving to REDIRECT as it does in this slice. No new human-facing command; eight new standing topics appear per swarm (specifier, coder, cleaner, architect, hardender, documenter, QA, coordinator), and any authorised message posted in one interrupts that role's pane on its phone-visible topic — marked or not, since the `!`-prefix mode selector does not exist yet in this slice.

**Epic Telegram topics now carry distinct musical-form icons instead of their old hand-set trophy/lightning/folder icons (BL-449).** Codifies a human directive: an epic is a large-scale musical FORM, so its icon comes from that vocabulary — realised on two distinct surfaces, since Telegram can't carry the same art the PWA/fleet-console/bot-avatar surfaces do (`docs/branding/icon-system.md` §4d's owned orchestra FORM marks are arbitrary SVGs, and Telegram topic icons may only be stock stickers from the free `getForumTopicIconStickers` set, which has no notation/instrument glyphs at all — see the new rule in `swarmforge/constitution/articles/local-engineering.prompt`). A new, deliberately separate module (`epicIcon.ts`) holds an ordered musical-form performance-emoji pool (headed by 🎙 BENCHMARKING / 🎭 DYNAMIC_ROUTING / 🎬 ONBOARDING) and `resolveEpicIcon`, disjoint from both the ticket-state `ICON_EMOJI` (BL-342/417) and the standing-topic `STANDING_TOPIC_ICON` (BL-418) pools — epics are explicitly kept out of BL-342's ticket-state icon sync, since an epic topic is neither a ticket folder nor a standing topic. A newly-created epic topic is auto-assigned the next distinct pool icon at creation time (`conciergeTick.ts`'s epic-topic create path); pool exhaustion degrades to a logged, graceful reuse rather than a crash. The same resolve-or-skip posture as every other icon path applies: an emoji absent from the live sticker set is skipped, never sent as an unvalidated custom emoji id. Ownership is unchanged from BL-342's rule — the live tick only sets/updates an epic icon the swarm already owns, or a brand-new epic topic's initial icon; a human-recustomised epic icon is left alone. `backfill-epic-topic-icons.ts` is a new one-time CLI, modelled on the existing standing/ticket backfills, that is the one authorised override: it sets all three seeded epics' icons even though their current hand-assigned icons are not swarm-owned, and seeds the live tick's seen-set so it never re-treats a backfilled epic as newly-entered. No new human-facing command; the three existing epic topics (Swarm Role Benchmarking, Dynamic Routing, Onboarding a New Target Repo) show 🎙/🎭/🎬 once the backfill runs, and any future epic topic gets the next distinct performance sticker automatically.

**A live pipeline-board grid now shows every active ticket's current stage in its own standing Telegram topic (BL-452).** An Operator directive relayed 2026-07-16, jumping the paused queue: a lowkey glanceable kanban — active BL tickets on the Y axis, pipeline roles on the X axis, a single `X` mark at each ticket's current stage — real-time (reflects a stage change within a concierge tick), read-only, and living inside the front-desk bot rather than a separate service. The Operator asked for the bridge's `/pipeline` state specifically, not the handoff hop-log, but `readPipelineStages` (`swarmState.ts`) reported only each role's busy/idle status with no per-ticket data; the specifier surfaced this as the ticket's one real design fork and the human resolved it via `AskUserQuestion` (re-affirmed once more, 2026-07-16, against a follow-up "could the coordinator push instead?" — rejected, since the coordinator sits outside the forward chain and cannot author every stage transition, and the tick already polls, so pushing would just duplicate the handoff mailbox as a second source of truth): **enrich** `PipelineStage` with each role's currently-`in_process`-held ticket id(s), a cheap one-directory read, never a git-history walk. `readInProcessTicketIds` reuses the existing batch-aware handoff-header reader (`readHandoffHeaderRecordsWithBatches`/`extractTicketId`) already relied on by `ticketHoldingWindows.ts`, deliberately distinct from that module's own "current holder," which derives from completed+in_process holding *windows* — the hop-log-shaped mechanism the Operator explicitly rejected as this feature's data source. `pipelineBoard.ts` is the pure render half: `computePipelineBoardRows` places every role-held ticket first (in `PIPELINE.md`'s own role order) then every paused ticket, in its `parked` or (BL-424's own paused-scoped signal) `awaiting-approval` status column, so every active ticket lands in exactly one row with no empty rows; `renderPipelineBoard` renders a monospace grid (two-letter column glyphs — `SP CO CL AR HD DC QA CD PK AA` — sized for a phone screen) wrapped in a Telegram HTML `<pre>` block. `pipelineBoardSync.ts` is the adapter-injected I/O half: edge-triggered on the rendered *text* changing (never on any one ticket's transition), it posts once to a standing "Pipeline Board" topic (created once, its id persisted in `TickState.pipelineBoard`, the same durable-marker posture `standingIconSeenIds`/`titleAgeBuckets` already use) and edits that same message in place on every subsequent change — never re-posted, never re-edited when nothing changed, so it cannot trigger the first-tick rate-limit storm `backfill-topic-icons.ts` (BL-342) once hit, since this is always a single message, not a per-topic fan-out. `telegramClient.ts` gained `editMessageText` (message-id-addressed, distinct from `editForumTopic`'s topic-id-addressed rename/re-icon) and an optional `parse_mode` on `sendMessage`, both additive and behavior-preserving for every existing caller. Wired into `conciergeTick.ts` as a fully optional adapter pair (`readRoleHeldTickets`/`boardAdapters`), so every existing fixture across the codebase's acceptance step handlers keeps working unchanged. **Cleaner pass, same ticket:** extracted `resolveBoardTopicId`/`postOrEditBoard` out of `syncPipelineBoard` and a `syncBoardIfWired` helper out of `runConciergeTick` to bring both back under the CRAP<=6 gate, behavior-preserving. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** covered `readInProcessTicketIds` against an in_process handoff with no `task` field at all and one whose `task` field doesn't parse to a ticket id — both must be omitted, not thrown; a soft Gherkin id-mutation pass over the ticket's own Scenario Outline intentionally survives 4 mutants of the `<id>` example value, since `renderPipelineBoard` treats a ticket id as an opaque passthrough string (never validated against a closed set the way `<state>`/`<column>` are), a documented equivalent-mutant case, not a coverage gap. No new human-facing command; a "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now appears alongside the standing Operator/support topics, showing at a glance which stage holds each active ticket.

**Refinement, same feature (BL-455):** the board now groups its stage-grid rows by epic (deterministic sort), and a ticket that is `parked`/`awaiting-approval` no longer occupies a grid column at all — it moves into a separate list below the grid instead, so those two statuses are never grid columns. Every row (grid or below-grid) also carries a short slug derived from the ticket's own title, so a glance at the board no longer requires opening the ticket to know roughly what it is. `PipelineBoardRow` grew `epic`/`slug` fields; `conciergeTick.ts`'s `syncBoardIfWired` joins each role-held/paused ticket id to its backlog item's epic and title from the already-loaded folders snapshot — no new git-history walk.

**Refinement, same feature (BL-462):** three further human-requested tweaks to the live board, from the front desk via the Operator — a wider slug, an "updated at" footer, and repost-at-bottom so the board is always the topic's latest message. `PIPELINE_BOARD_SLUG_MAX_LENGTH` widened from 24 to 40; `renderPipelineBoard(data, lastChangeMs)` now appends an `updated at MMM DD HH:MM` footer (UTC, via the pure `formatUpdatedAtLabel`) below the grid, fed the last CONTENT-change instant, never the current clock. The change-gate moved from "did the rendered text change" to a two-part signature: `renderPipelineBoardBody` (the grid + parked list, deliberately EXCLUDING the footer) is the persisted `contentSignature` compared tick over tick, so a tick where nothing but the wall clock advanced changes neither the footer nor the message. `pipelineBoardSync.ts` no longer delegates to `syncEditInPlaceMessage`: on an unchanged signature it does nothing at all; on a changed signature it records the injected instant as the new last-change time, renders body+footer, deletes the previous board message (if any, via `telegramClient.ts`'s new `deleteMessage`) and posts a fresh one — always the newest message in the topic. `TickState.pipelineBoard` grew `contentSignature`/`lastChangeMs` alongside its existing `topicId`/`messageId`. The Approvals Roster (`approvalsRosterSync.ts`) is unchanged and still edits in place — only the board moved to repost-at-bottom; `editInPlaceMessageSync.ts` itself was not touched. No new human-facing command; the same "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now shows a wider per-ticket slug, an updated-at footer, and reposts to the bottom of the topic only when a ticket's stage actually changes.

**Bug fix, same feature (BL-464): the board's active rows now come from an authoritative coordinator-fed store, not an in_process scrape — closing both a missing-ticket defect and the double-row defect at the source.** The human, via the Operator front desk, reported the live board "defeats the purpose": tickets a role was ACTIVELY WORKING (BL-434, BL-450) never appeared, and BL-460 rendered on two rows at once during a stage transition. Root cause: BL-452's `readInProcessTicketIds` extracted a ticket id only from a `git_handoff`'s `task:` header, so a ticket kicked off by the coordinator's promote-via-note convention (which carries no `task:` header) was invisible until it became a downstream `git_handoff`; and pushing one row per `(role, id)` observation with no cross-role dedupe let the same ticket render twice while momentarily held at two roles. The human chose the coordinator-fed fix (`AskUserQuestion` Q2) over a smaller note-aware scraper, since the coordinator already tracks parcel location end to end. New Babashka module `pipeline_stage_lib.bb` (pure) reconciles each active role's in_process handoff — a `git_handoff`'s `task` header OR a `note`'s `message` header, closing the note-kickoff blind spot — down to exactly one role per ticket, favoring the most-downstream role on a transient two-role overlap; `pipeline_stage_cli.bb report|sync` is its one shell-callable entry point, writing the reconciled `{ticket-id: role}` map atomically to `.swarmforge/board/ticket-stage-map.json`. `swarmforge/roles/coordinator.prompt` now instructs the coordinator to run `sync` after every promotion/routing/bookkeeping/queue-sweep action — the coordinator is the real production writer this store needs, per the engineering article's named-writer/reader rule. `extension/src/swarm/swarmState.ts`'s new `readTicketStageMap`/`invertTicketStageToRoleHeldTickets` read that store and replace `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`'s prior `readPipelineStages`-derived scrape as the board's `readRoleHeldTickets` adapter (`readPipelineStages` itself is unchanged — the VS Code panel's own `currentStageLabel`/holder logic still uses it). `computePipelineBoard` also now collapses a duplicate ticket id across roles to one row (most-downstream wins) as a belt-and-braces renderer guarantee, structurally redundant with but independent of the store's own one-role-per-ticket shape. No new human-facing command; the same "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now shows every actively-worked ticket (including a freshly note-promoted one) at its true current stage, always on exactly one row.

**Shell and Babashka test harnesses now clean up their own temp dirs (BL-459, the BL-420 prevention gap).** BL-420 made the extension's Vitest suite self-clean its own `mkdtemp` dirs, but the shell (`swarmforge/scripts/test/*.sh`) and Babashka (`*_test_runner.bb`) test harnesses had no cleanup trap at all, feeding a `/tmp` accumulation of stale `sfvc-*`/`aps-*` directories an Operator directive flagged (~377k dirs, ~5.3M inodes). This is internal test-infrastructure hygiene with no human-facing command or setting. A shared `swarmforge/scripts/test/lib/tmp_cleanup.sh` registers one `EXIT` trap per script; calling `register_tmp_dir "$var"` right after each `mktemp -d` assignment adds it to that trap's cleanup list, capturing the path as an immutable string at call time so a variable reused across several directories doesn't leak a stale reference. (Companion ticket BL-458's live-orphan reaper is still in flight and is not yet part of this landed slice.)

**Two more hardening-gate blockers fixed — a tracked vitest cache blob and four bridge tests bypassing the shared mkdtemp helper (BL-714).** Both were pre-existing defects, unrelated to the tickets whose hardening passes kept rediscovering them: `node_modules/.vite/vitest/da39a3ee5e6b4b0d3255bfef95601890afd80709/results.json` had been committed by an unrelated CRAP-reduction change and matched `.gitignore`'s own `node_modules/.vite/vitest/` rule, so the ignore never re-excluded it — its serialized content happened to contain the exact retired word the BL-684 residual-word rename guard scans for, failing that guard's full-tree `git grep` scan on every run. Fixed by `git rm --cached`, leaving the path ignored rather than re-adding it to any allowlist. Separately, four tests added on the BL-696 checkpoint path (`telegramCursorBridge{Expedite,Logs,Redeploy,Update}.test.js`) called `fs.mkdtempSync` directly instead of the shared `test/helpers/tmpDir.js` (BL-420's own migration guard, `extension/test/tmpDirMigrationGuard.test.js`); migrated to `mkTmpDir` rather than weakening the guard. Same internal test-infrastructure hygiene class as BL-459 above — no human-facing command or setting, and no product behavior change. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** two real-`git` 3-parent octopus-merge fixtures for BL-630's publish-time gate (a trivial disjoint-file merge that publishes, and a hand-crafted content-bearing octopus merge — built via `commit-tree` since git's own octopus strategy refuses on conflicts — that is refused) plus a second property non-vacuity self-check proving that gate's generator/oracle pairing specifically catches a regression to exempting every `:merge? true` sha, not just a fully-bypassed gate.

**A third pre-existing hardening-gate blocker: tests that leaked `process.env` keys made the suite verdict non-deterministic (BL-720).** `extension/vitest.config.mjs`'s `poolOptions.forks.isolate: false` (BL-445's performance choice) means `process.env` persists across every test file sharing a worker, so `delete process.env.SOME_KEY` in a test's cleanup does not clean up — it permanently unsets that key for every later file in the same fork. `extension/test/cursorBridgeAgentSession.test.js` (BL-696) unconditionally deleted `CURSOR_API_KEY` at eight sites instead of following the file's own established idiom (capture the prior value, restore it or delete-if-absent in `finally`, already used at three other sites in the same file); fixed by applying that idiom to all eight. Same class as BL-420's `rawMkdtempGuard`: a guard against recurrence, not just a one-time fix. `extension/test/helpers/envRestoreGuard.js` (pure snapshot/diff/format) and `envRestoreGuardSetup.js` (the real per-test `beforeEach`/`afterEach` wiring, registered via `vitest.config.mjs`'s `setupFiles` alongside BL-420's `tmpDirSetup.js`) snapshot `process.env` before and after every test and fail loudly — naming the file, the test, and every leaked key — the moment a test leaves the environment different from what it found, reachable from a plain `npx vitest run` with no extra flags. No human-facing command or setting; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714.

**A BL-787 property fixture leaked the operator's real named-tunnel identity into cases that meant it absent (BL-867).** `extension/test/bl787NamedTunnelInvariants.property.test.js` built every fixture subprocess environment as `{ ...process.env, <case vars> }` — additive only, never subtractive. On a host that genuinely exports `SWARMFORGE_NAMED_TUNNEL`/`SWARMFORGE_NAMED_TUNNEL_HOSTNAME`/`SWARMFORGE_CLOUDFLARED_CONFIG` so the live resident-spy tunnel can run, every case meaning one of those variables ABSENT received the operator's real value instead. Two faults followed: invariant 2 ("absent named-tunnel identity fails loud, never falls back to a concrete operator domain") failed outright — `check_bubble_named_tunnel_dns.sh` sailed past its own guard on the leaked identity, and the `musicalsifu` hardcoded-default regression check fired for an unrelated reason, making a future genuine regression indistinguishable from ambient contamination; and invariant 3's `mode: 'quick'` half silently took the NAMED branch on three of its six runs instead of the quick branch it named, passing without ever exercising what it claimed to test. The scripts under test were correct throughout — only the fixture lied to them. Fix is test isolation only: a new `isolatedEnv()` helper (`extension/test/helpers/namedTunnelEnvIsolation.js`) builds each fixture's subprocess environment from the ambient environment with the four named-tunnel identity variables stripped first, then applies that case's own overrides — so a case's own choice to name a variable present or leave it absent is the only thing that determines what the subprocess sees, never what the host happened to export. No production script changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720.

**The property lane wired neither shared isolation guard, so 64 property files ran unswept and unguarded (BL-868).** `extension/vitest.config.mjs` registers `tmpDirSetup.js` (BL-420's `mkTmpDir()` sweep) and `envRestoreGuardSetup.js` (BL-720's leaked-`process.env` guard) as `setupFiles`; `extension/vitest.properties.config.mjs`, the separate minimal config the property lane runs under, registered neither. Every property test's `mkTmpDir()` calls therefore survived forever with nothing to sweep them — four property-file prefixes alone (`bl787-`, `bl861-`, `bl622-`, `bl805-`) accounted for 1527 orphaned directories (435 MB) out of 64 property files total, and the host's temp directory held 75301 entries. A property test that leaked a `process.env` key also had no guard to catch it, the same non-determinism risk BL-720 closed for the unit lane. Fix: `vitest.properties.config.mjs` now registers the same two `setupFiles`, in the same order, as `vitest.config.mjs`. No production script changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-867.

**BL-606's earlier unscoped step pattern shadowed BL-623's exact one under the full step registry, false-failing a done ticket's durable acceptance contract on a clean baseline (BL-800).** `specs/pipeline/steps/bl606RequiredStagesRoutingSteps.js`'s generic `/^the parcel is delivered to (.+)$/` registered before `specs/pipeline/steps/bl623RoutingSkipTrailSteps.js`'s exact `/^the parcel is delivered to QA$/` in `steps/index.js`'s load order, so `stepRegistry.js`'s first-match resolution for unscoped patterns always gave BL-623's step text to BL-606's handler, which asserts on `ctx.bounceHandoff` — never set by BL-623's scenarios 02/04, which send no bounce. The focused `bl623Only.js` entry point BL-623's own 2026-07-30 QA pass ran loads only bl623's steps, so the collision was never exercised until the BL-761 architect pass ran the feature through the default full-registry entry point on 2026-08-04. Fix: `bl623RoutingSkipTrailSteps.js` now registers its colliding step via `registry.defineScoped(pattern, handler, FEATURE_NAME)` — `stepRegistry.js`'s existing BL-425 feature-scoping mechanism — so it resolves to BL-623's own handler whenever BL-623's feature is running, independent of registration order; `bl606RequiredStagesRoutingSteps.js` is untouched, and its own feature still resolves 18/18 under the default entry point. Carries a coder-authored property test (`extension/test/bl800StepRegistryScopingConsistency.property.test.js`) proving the declared invariant — the focused and full registries resolve every one of BL-623's real steps to the same handler (by source-string equality, since each entry point builds an independent registry instance) — over the real feature file via the real gherkin-parser, with a second permanent test reproducing the exact pre-fix BL-606-shadows-BL-623 failure against a self-contained fixture registry to prove the checker is non-vacuous. Acceptance-harness fix only; BL-623's recorded routing-skip-trail behavior (`docs/how-to/BL-623-routing-skip-trail-records-actual-hop.md`) is unchanged. No production behavior changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-867/BL-868.

**`tmp_cleanup.sh` lost registrations made inside command-substitution subshells, leaking temp roots everywhere and false-failing a passing suite on stock macOS bash (BL-801).** `register_tmp_dir` appended to a parent-shell array, but the tree-wide convention `ROOT="$(make_root)"` runs that append inside a command-substitution subshell whose copy of the array is discarded on exit — so a root registered only that way was never in the parent's array (every-host leak, nothing to sweep) and, with the array left genuinely empty, `"${arr[@]}"` under `set -u` raised `unbound variable` in the EXIT trap on bash < 4.4 (stock macOS `/bin/bash` is 3.2.57), turning a fully passing suite into a false exit 1 — confirmed live on `test_daemon_log_freshness.sh`, which went from "ALL CHECKS PASSED" + exit 1 + `unbound variable` on stderr to the same pass banner with a truthful exit 0 and clean stderr. Fix: the registry is now a file instead of an array, one `mktemp` per top-level script process, captured once and exported so any subshell inherits the same path — a file survives a fork the way a shell variable never can, so `register_tmp_dir` appends to it from any shell depth, and the EXIT trap reads it back with a plain `while read` loop, no array indexing anywhere so nothing can raise `unbound variable` regardless of how many lines the registry holds, including zero. None of the ~61 sourcing test files were touched — the fix lives entirely in the shared lib, per the ticket's own constraint that the lib adapts to the established convention, not the other way round. `test_tmp_cleanup_lib.sh` is the lib's first unit test, covering subshell registration, the empty-registry case, mixed direct+subshell registrations, and concurrent-process isolation via explicit flag-file sync; a same-parcel hardener pass added a scenario proving the registry FILE itself (not just the roots it names) is removed on exit, closing a small-file leak a hand-authored mutation sweep surfaced. No human-facing command or setting; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-867/BL-868/BL-800.

**A periodic sweep now clears the existing stock of stale acceptance-test sandboxes from `/tmp` (BL-413).** BL-459 above bounds new accumulation going forward; this bounds what had already piled up. `sandbox_sweep_lib.bb`'s pure `removable?` predicate (allowlist-only known prefixes, staleness, no live process rooted in the entry, the swarm's own legacy socket dir excluded first and unconditionally) is wired into `operator_runtime.bb`'s existing tick loop as a bounded-per-tick `sandbox-sweep!`, reading its temp root and the legacy socket dir through the same redirectable env-seam convention `kill_all_swarm.sh` already established — it never touches the real `/tmp` in a test. **Cleaner pass, same ticket:** the `/proc` cwd+fd liveness scan this predicate depends on was deduped into a shared `proc_fd_scan_lib.bb` rather than living inline. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** the architect's own bounce is verified — liveness detection now checks a candidate directory's open file descriptors, not just its working directory, since a process can hold a sandbox dir open (a file handle) without that dir being its cwd, which the cwd-only check missed. No human-facing command or setting; this is internal test-infrastructure hygiene.

**The BL-413/BL-458 `/tmp` sweeps were a production no-op — they bounded the SCAN, not the DELETES — and now make provable per-tick progress (BL-460).** Live incident, Operator directive relayed 2026-07-16, against work QA had approved and closed the same day: both `sandbox-sweep!` (`operator_runtime.bb`) and `sweep!` (`fixture_reaper_sweep_lib.bb`) did `(take cap (list-entries root))` every tick — a bounded scan that always started at the same fixed readdir position, so a listing whose first `cap` (default 100) entries never contained a reapable one (live: 0 of the first 100, 76 orphan fixture processes untouched after 40+ ticks, `/tmp` growing) re-scanned that same dead window forever. The pure `removable?`/`reapable?` predicates from BL-413/BL-458 were correct and untouched; the defect was entirely in the windowing. Fix: a new shared `bounded_delete_sweep_lib.bb` maintains a persisted cursor that advances every tick over a stable sorted listing and wraps at the end, so both sweeps cover the whole directory over `ceil(count/cap)` ticks regardless of how many leading entries are non-reapable; `record-tick!` (added in a same-ticket cleaner pass) dedupes the cursor-persist and reaped/nothing-streak bookkeeping both callers had hand-rolled around it. Both sweeps now log a reap-summary line when they remove something and a periodic (not per-tick) nothing-found line otherwise — previously the reaper logged nothing at all and the dir sweep logged only on a removal, so a silent no-op was indistinguishable from success. `sandbox_sweep_lib.bb`'s allowlist gained 9 prefixes observed at volume in production, all traced to plain Vitest `mkTmpDir` fixtures in `extension/test/*.test.js` (no process spawning, so they belong to the dir sweep, not the reaper's process-killing allowlist) — allowlist-only, never a glob. No new human-facing command or setting; this is the same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-458/BL-459, and the acceptance contract requires the fix to be proven on the live production box (orphan process count and `/tmp` entry count actually falling over successive ticks), not only in a fixture.

**BL-459's cleanup-trap guard verdict rotted because its zero-violation assertion lived where no standing gate runs it, letting 18 files land unguarded over three weeks (BL-872).** BL-459 shipped a static regression guard (`specs/pipeline/steps/lib/tempDirTrapGuard.js`) flagging any `.sh`/`.bb` file under `swarmforge/scripts` that creates a temp root (`mktemp -d` / `fs/create-temp-dir`) without a cleanup mechanism — the shell/babashka sibling of BL-420's extension-side `rawMkdtempGuard`. The guard itself was correct; what rotted was where its verdict was consumed: the zero-violation assertion lived only in `specs/pipeline/test/tempDirTrapGuard.test.js`, invoked ad hoc by a role naming individual files, never by a standing gate — unlike its BL-420 sibling, which rides the Vitest suite every parcel runs. Measured on a clean `main` working tree, 2026-08-10, over the regression window BL-519 (2026-07-18) through BL-849 (2026-08-09): 18 violations — 13 babashka test runners, 4 shell harnesses, and one production file, `swarmforge/scripts/pre_qa_gate_gather_lib.bb`, which creates two `fs/create-temp-dir` roots per pre-QA gate evaluation (a gate that runs on every documenter → QA handoff) and cleaned up neither, feeding the very `/tmp` accumulation BL-413/BL-459 exist to stop. Fix: all 18 remediated — the 4 shell files register directly in the parent shell via `swarmforge/scripts/test/lib/tmp_cleanup.sh`'s `register_tmp_dir` (never the `ROOT="$(make_root)"` command-substitution pattern BL-801 fixed the registration-loss for), the babashka test runners add a shutdown hook matching the 11 already-clean runners, and `pre_qa_gate_gather_lib.bb`'s two production roots move to a caller-level atom cleaned up in one `finally` covering every branch — and the guard gets a standing home: `extension/test/tempDirTrapGuard.test.js` calls the same `scanForTempDirTrapViolations` the acceptance contract and BL-459's own suite already use, riding the Vitest suite every parcel runs, mirroring BL-420's `tmpDirMigrationGuard.test.js`. A same-parcel property suite (`extension/test/tempDirTrapGuard.property.test.js`, BL-654) covers the ticket's three declared invariants against a deliberately broken classifier to prove non-vacuousness. No human-facing command or setting; internal swarm machinery only, same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-800/BL-801/BL-867/BL-868/BL-460.

**The property lane ran an uncapped worker pool while the unit lane deliberately caps its own, so a full property run's failing file moved between repeats instead of being a function of the code under test (BL-871).** `extension/vitest.properties.config.mjs` set `globals`/`environment`/`include`/`testTimeout` only — no `pool`, no `poolOptions`, no worker ceiling, no per-worker heap limit — while the unit lane's `vitest.config.mjs` reads `MAX_WORKERS`/`PER_WORKER_HEAP_MB` from the shared `vitest-worker-memory-budget` module (see "Bounded test-run memory footprint (BL-422)" above) through `resolveWorkerPoolSize`, sized to the host's real RAM. On the reference 4-CPU/8192MB host the two lanes diverged exactly where it mattered: the property lane ran 4 forks with no heap bound at all, over 65 files that spawn real subprocesses, while the unit lane ran 3 forks capped at 1280MB. The observable symptom was a full `npm run test:properties` run whose failing file moved between repeats (`bl760DuplicateChainGuard`, then `bl787NamedTunnelInvariants`, then `bl805RotateGateOnUnfinishedInProcessParcel` — each passes 3-for-3 run alone), making the lane's verdict a function of host contention rather than of the code under test. Fix: `vitest.properties.config.mjs` now reads the same shared budget module through the same `resolveWorkerPoolSize` call as the unit config, so neither lane carries its own copy of the worker/heap numbers — a change to the caps reaches both lanes or neither. (BL-935 later moved that shared call one level down: both lanes now call `resolveVitestWorkerPool`, which composes the CPU-axis ceiling with the same `resolveWorkerPoolSize` budget — one route for both lanes still, and now for both ceilings.) Stryker's own vitest-runner hardcodes `pool: 'threads'`/`maxThreads: 1` and reads `poolOptions.threads`, so mutation runs are unaffected, matching the BL-422 note above. No production script changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-422/BL-445/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-800/BL-801/BL-867/BL-868/BL-872.

QA's re-verification of this fix found the worker-pool cap alone was not sufficient to make the lane reliably green, and bounced two further items in the same mechanism class: the three property files that shell out to real subprocesses per iteration (`bl760DuplicateChainGuard`, `bl787NamedTunnelInvariants`, `bl797MutationGateProbeCrashFallback`) still timed out under contention even with the fork/heap cap in place, since the cap bounds Vitest's own workers, not the CPU a worker's real child processes consume; and the acceptance scenario's own `spawnSync` timeout (300s) was shorter than the fix's real passing runtime (400-470s) on the reference host. Both are tuning-constant fixes: the three files' outer `testTimeout`s and inner `spawnSync` timeouts were raised (20-120s → 240s outer, 15s → 30s inner; `bl787`'s launcher poll budget widened 2s → 20s), and the acceptance step handler's own `spawnSync` timeout raised 300000ms → 900000ms (`specs/pipeline/steps/bl871PropertyLaneWorkerPoolCapSteps.js`). Re-verifying those fixes surfaced a third, independent mechanism with no config knob: Vitest's worker-RPC layer (`birpc`) hardcodes a 60-second timeout on a worker's own `onTaskUpdate` status callback to the main thread; a worker fork spending 100-240s+ inside a synchronous `spawnSync`/`execFileSync` call blocks its event loop for that whole span, so it cannot service the heartbeat, which fires an "Unhandled Error: timeout calling onTaskUpdate" close to unconditionally for these specific files — flipping an otherwise-clean 232/232-test run to a non-zero exit code even though no test failed. Fixed by adding `dangerouslyIgnoreUnhandledErrors: true` to `vitest.properties.config.mjs` only (the unit lane has no analogous long-blocking-sync-subprocess pattern); this only gates the exit-code side effect of an unhandled error, the "Unhandled Errors" section still prints so a genuinely different unhandled error remains visible, and it was verified against all logged instances across three runs being the identical benign `onTaskUpdate` message before being added.

**Six tests in the Babashka layer's only quality gate were red on macOS because they backdated fixture mtimes with GNU-only relative-time syntax, which stock BSD userland rejects (BL-874).** `test_operator_runtime_sandbox_sweep.sh`, `test_operator_runtime_sandbox_sweep_bounded_progress.sh`, `test_operator_runtime_fixture_reaper_sweep.sh`, `test_operator_runtime_fixture_reaper_sweep_bounded_progress.sh`, `test_operator_runtime_tick.sh`, and `test_handoffd_stuck_escalation_email_wiring.sh` (all under `swarmforge/scripts/test/`) each backdated a fixture file's mtime with `touch -d "<relative-time>"` or `date -d "<relative-time>"` — GNU-only forms stock BSD `touch`/`date` reject outright (`illegal time specification` / `illegal option -- d`), so all six exited non-zero on macOS, the declared target OS (local-engineering.prompt) and the host this swarm runs on. `swarmforge/scripts/test/` is the sole gate for the Babashka/Clojure layer — engineering.prompt's Startup Tools rule states that layer has no mutation/CRAP/DRY tooling and is "gated ONLY by their own unit-test suite" — so this left that layer's one safety signal partly dark on the machine that needs it. Fix: a new `swarmforge/scripts/portable_time_lib.sh` (mirroring `portable_stat_lib.sh`'s shape — one function, the BSD/GNU split hidden inside it, callers unaware) resolves a relative-time offset to the portable `touch -t YYYYMMDDhhmm.SS` form, trying BSD's `date -v` first and falling back to GNU's `date -d`; all six sites now call its `portable_touch_relative` instead of the GNU-only syntax, with the same backdated-mtime assertions unchanged. The guard is given a standing home, mirroring BL-872's placement: `extension/test/portableTimeGuard.test.js` asserts zero GNU-only relative-time invocations remain under `swarmforge/scripts`, riding the Vitest suite every parcel runs — the same "rots because no standing gate checks it" failure mode as BL-872's temp-dir traps and BL-420's raw-mkdtemp guard. No production behavior changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-800/BL-801/BL-867/BL-868/BL-872/BL-871.

**Sandbox-sweep's stale-directory guard and the fixture reaper's orphan-kill were both silently inert on macOS, because process-liveness detection only ever read `/proc` (BL-877).** `swarmforge/scripts/proc_fd_scan_lib.bb`'s `process-cwd-path`/`process-open-paths` are Linux/WSL-only; both consumers' own `live-process-paths!` caught the resulting exception and returned an empty set/map when `/proc` didn't exist, and the two callers degrade in OPPOSITE directions from that same "nothing is live" verdict — `operator_runtime.bb`'s sandbox sweep treats it as "safe to delete" (a stale-by-mtime sandbox is removed out from under a live process), while `fixture_reaper_sweep_lib.bb`'s reaper treats it as "nothing to kill" (an orphan keeps running). Three tests asserting the Linux-only behavior were red on macOS, the declared target OS this swarm runs on. Fix: `proc_fd_scan_lib.bb` gained a portable `live-pid-paths!` entry point — `/proc` when present (Linux/WSL, unchanged), a single `lsof -F pfn` invocation otherwise (Darwin, matching the "scan once per sweep pass" cost discipline the `/proc` branch already followed) — and now returns `nil`, never a coerced-empty collection, when NEITHER facility is reachable, so "cannot determine liveness" survives as a distinct state from "determined, nothing found" (mirroring `process_table_lib.bb`'s BL-849 contract). Both callers were rewired onto the shared primitive: the sandbox sweep's `nil` handling flips to its OWN safe direction — an undetermined pass now assumes every candidate IS live rather than none — since ITS dangerous direction is deleting a root a live process still needs; the fixture reaper's `nil` passes through unchanged, since its own safe direction ("kill nothing it cannot see") already matched an empty result. Both entry paths are also resolved to their real path before matching, since macOS's `$TMPDIR`/`mktemp` roots live under a `/var` symlink to `/private/var` that `lsof` (like `/proc`'s own real-path reads) reports resolved, not aliased. A same-parcel bounce fix (hardener) moved the reaper's liveness-undetermined log line from `default-adapters` into `sweep!` itself, after `:log!` is resolved from the caller's overrides — logging it earlier meant the message always went to stdout even when a caller (`operator_runtime.bb`) overrides `:log!` to write into its own `runtime.log`. No human-facing command or setting; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-458/BL-459/BL-460/BL-849/BL-872/BL-874.

**Nine handoffd wiring tests spawned their daemon through `setsid`, absent from stock macOS, and failed as an invisible timeout rather than a named error (BL-878).** `setsid` is util-linux and absent from stock macOS; ten unguarded call sites across nine scripts under `swarmforge/scripts/test/` backgrounded the handoff daemon spawn through it directly (`... setsid bb "$HANDOFFD" "$ROOT" &`). On a host without `setsid`, `env: setsid: No such file or directory` fired inside that backgrounded job — invisible to the script's own control flow — so the daemon never started, and the test only found out much later inside its own `wait_for_log` poll, reading as a slow/flaky daemon rather than a missing tool; that is why nine scripts sat dark rather than one obvious red. Fix: a new shared `swarmforge/scripts/portable_daemon_spawn_lib.sh` exposes `portable_spawn_daemon_or_fail <required-interpreter> <cmd...>` — prefers `setsid` when present (Linux/WSL, unchanged), falls back to plain `nohup ... &` otherwise (macOS), the same shape BL-802 established for production's `start_babysitterd.sh` and the shape one in-suite script, `test_handoffd_role_context_clear_skip_rotation_router.sh`, already used correctly — and checks the daemon's own interpreter is on `PATH` *before* ever backgrounding, failing loud and naming the tool in the foreground rather than letting a second silent failure hide the same way. All nine scripts now call the shared helper instead of duplicating the guard inline, so its semantics can't drift between call sites; a new `test_portable_daemon_spawn_lib.sh` unit-tests the helper itself (setsid path, nohup fallback, missing-interpreter failure) in isolation. Fixing the setsid blocker let six of the nine scripts run to completion on this host for the first time, surfacing two independent pre-existing bugs fixed in the same commit since already touching these files: five scripts' "the sweep fires on more than one poll cycle" assertions raced a blind `sleep 6` against the daemon's real ~10s+ gated chase-sweep cadence — switched to the polling `wait_for_count` helper `test_handoffd_push_sweep_wiring.sh` already used for this exact class of flake; and `test_handoffd_role_context_clear_wiring.sh` asserted the pre-BL-519 "Re-read constitution.prompt" tmux message instead of the current BL-519 launch-kickoff text. Neither changes what either test actually asserts. A third finding in that investigation — `handoffd.bb`'s BL-617 comment saying sibling sweeps "keep running unconditionally" while they still share `chase-sweep-every-cycles` — looked like a ~10x cadence regression but was comment prose only; BL-882 rewords that comment to "pause-exempt, never every-tick" with no gate change. No production behavior changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-800/BL-801/BL-867/BL-868/BL-871/BL-872/BL-874/BL-877.

**Orphaned SwarmForge agent processes (leftover `claude` processes from a dry-run) are now auto-reaped, on the same BL-458 fixture-reaper pattern with a BL-367-safe never-touch-a-live-agent guard (BL-486).** Human-directed via the Operator front desk, 2026-07-17: a 6h43m-old orphaned coder process from an FES/second-swarm dry-run (launched from a `/tmp` mktemp checkout, no `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, cwd already deleted, no children, ~0% CPU) was found and killed by hand. Because auto-killing `claude` processes is the exact bug class behind BL-367 (an unscoped socket glob killed the live swarm's own socket five times in one session), this reaper follows the same discipline every existing reaper (`kill_all_swarm.sh`, `swarm-cleanup.sh`) already uses: enumeration only ever SURFACES candidates, never a `pgrep pattern | kill`; the kill decision is per-pid through a pure predicate whose exclusions win first. `orphan_agent_reaper_lib.bb`'s `reapable?` (mirroring `fixture_reaper_lib.bb`'s shape) checks, in order: NOT a member of the live control socket's tmux window set (the decapitation guard, wins first — enumerated the same way `kill_all_swarm.sh` does, via the tracked socket + `list-panes` + descendant `pgrep -P`) → cwd is `(deleted)` or resolves outside `$ROOT/.swarmforge` → no child processes → past a stale-age threshold (`SWARMFORGE_ORPHAN_REAP_STALE_HOURS`, default 6.0h, matching the incident and the fixture reaper's own default) — candidate scope is restricted to `--remote-control SwarmForge-*` cmdlines only. `orphan_agent_reaper_sweep_lib.bb` is the impure wiring half, every real read/action (cmdline, cwd, children, live-window-set, kill) an injectable adapter so a wiring test never scans the tester's own real `/proc`. Wired into the same always-alive janitor tick `operator_runtime.bb` already runs the BL-458 fixture sweep from, plus a standalone `reap_orphan_agents.bb` CLI for manual/human triggering — one real implementation, two callers. Every kill appends one UTC-timestamped line (pid, resolved cwd, age, gates-passed) to a dedicated audit log, never silent. No new human-facing command or setting beyond the env-overridable stale-age threshold; this is the same internal-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-458/BL-459/BL-460, scoped to agent processes rather than fixture directories.

**A new `mono-rotate` pack lets ONE resident agent process serve the whole pipeline in turn, for hosts too memory-constrained to run one process per role (BL-448).** An Operator directive: FES's second-swarm host (15GB) OOM-crashed under a full swarm, so mono-rotate becomes FES's new default bring-up, superseding BL-439's 2-pack (BL-439 reshaped in the same pass to depend on and point at it). The human fixed the design up front: **all quality gates stay full-strength** — acceptance, coverage, mutation/no-surviving-mutants, CRAP<=6, QA's final pass — the memory saving comes only from one resident process, never from a lighter gate; slower wall-clock is the accepted cost. `swarmforge/packs/mono-rotate.conf` declares `config rotation sequential` plus the full coder → cleaner → architect → hardener → documenter → QA window list (the coordinator stays separately auto-provisioned, per BL-243, never part of the rotation); `is_sequential_dormant` (`swarmforge.sh`) is the new gating logic that still provisions every role's own worktree and `roles.tsv` entry (so mailbox resolution is correct the instant the resident agent becomes that role) but launches a real tmux session/process only for the first window line. `swarmforge/packs/mono-rotate.prompt` is the resident agent's own overlay: each pipeline role's `swarmforge/roles/<role>.prompt` stays the unmodified authority for that role's substance, and the overlay adds only the rotation step — once a role's handoff is sent, the agent looks up the next role's worktree path in `roles.tsv`, exports `SWARMFORGE_ROLE`, `cd`s in, re-reads the constitution and that role's prompt as if freshly started, then runs `ready_for_next.sh` to pick up the very handoff it just sent. The ticket's own central risk — SwarmForge's quality model rests on role INDEPENDENCE, and one agent playing both sides of a bounce is a self-review — is named explicitly rather than papered over: the overlay instructs the agent to evaluate each role's work as a genuinely fresh, skeptical reader, not from what it remembers deciding a minute ago, and documents that an automated context-reset-and-rebootstrap watcher (closing that gap for real) is a deferred, architect-owned mechanism decision, not part of this pass. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** added a boundary assertion (`test_rotation_sequential_pack.sh`) proving the LAST pipeline role (QA), immediately adjacent to the always-resident coordinator, is also correctly sequential-dormant — the existing middle-role assertions alone couldn't catch an off-by-one at the upper bound. New human-facing surface: `./swarm <target> --pack mono-rotate` launches this pack.

**`./swarm ensure` respawned five roles the launcher deliberately left dormant on a `mono-rotate` pack, because the launcher and ensure disagreed about what `rotation sequential` means (BL-571).** `swarmforge.sh`'s `is_sequential_dormant` treats `rotation sequential` and `rotation router` as the SAME single-resident topology — only the resident agent and the coordinator get a real tmux session, every middle pipeline role stays dormant (worktree + `roles.tsv` entry + a pre-generated launch script, no process) until the resident respawns its own pane as that role. Ensure's `rotation-router-mode?` matched the literal `router` alone, so on the one shipped pack declaring `config rotation sequential` — `mono-rotate` — ensure classified those five dormant roles as broken panes and drove them into repair. The failure was silent in the worst way: the ensure report showed *repairs*, not a warning, so the operator read "healed" where the truth was "over-provisioned" — and it started five extra agent processes on precisely the memory-constrained host mono-rotate exists to serve (its own conf names the FES 15GB box, which had already OOM-crashed under a full swarm). Nothing about the swarm running today changed; it declares `rotation router`, which both sides already agreed on. Fix: `mono_router_lib.bb` gains `single-resident-rotation?` and `single-resident-rotation-from-identity?`, recognising the topology by every value the launcher accepts, and `swarm_ensure.bb`'s `rotation-router-mode?` consumes those instead. The router-ONLY `conf-rotation-router?`/`rotation-router-from-identity?` deliberately stay as they are and keep their exact meaning, because `ready_for_next_task.bb` and `ready_for_next_batch.bb` consume them for the ROTATE_HOME backstop — widening THAT changes when a non-home role gets sent home, which is a behavior change owing its own spec and tests, and an acceptance scenario pins that path unchanged. The four predicates are now two pairs over ONE mechanism (a `[config ]rotation <value>` conf line or a `swarm-identity` `rotation` key, matched against an accepted set), written once, with each pair naming only its own set — the sets differ, and that difference is the load-bearing part. **Kept honest across a language boundary no import can bridge (BL-897):** `single-resident-rotation-values` mirrors a set of bash string literals in `is_sequential_dormant`, and a "widen both sides together" docstring is a comment, not a gate. `mono_router_lib_test_runner.bb` therefore DERIVES the launcher's accepted set by parsing `swarmforge.sh`'s own function body and asserts set EQUALITY, so drift in either direction fails loudly; a functional sweep then sources the real launcher function and confirms each derived value is genuinely accepted (and a control value rejected), so the textual derivation cannot rot into matching nothing. No human-facing command or setting changes — `./swarm <target> --pack mono-rotate` and `./swarm ensure` are invoked exactly as before; what changes is that ensure now leaves the dormant roles alone.

**Perplexity mono-router and aider coordinator model wiring (2026-07-19).** Operators can run the full mono-router topology on Perplexity Sonar via aider with `./swarm <root> --pack perplexity-mono-router` after setting `SWARMFORGE_USE_PERPLEXITY=1` and `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` (key never written to disk under the target; same BL-130 ephemeral `-e` posture as Cerebras). Role→model bands: reasoning Sonar for specifier/architect, Sonar Pro for coder/hardender/QA, Sonar for cleaner/documenter/coordinator. Launch scripts, ensure, and rotate/chase remap the Perplexity key onto `OPENAI_API_*` and point at `https://api.perplexity.ai` **without** `/v1` (that path 404s), and deliberately skip forwarding a host `OPENAI_API_KEY` so real OpenAI credentials cannot shadow Sonar. Separately, `provision_coordinator` now passes `--model $COORDINATOR_MODEL` when `config coordinator_agent aider` (it already did for claude and codex) — without that, an aider coordinator launched as bare `aider --yes-always` and could not use the pack's `coordinator_model`. Mono-router pack overlays (`*-mono-router.prompt`) now require the home resident to **stop** after `ready_for_next.sh` returns `NO_TASK` (no re-poll/`/loop`), and when `backlog/active/` is empty while `backlog/paused/` has eligible work, to send one coordinator note then idle; the coordinator on wake promotes under `active_backlog_max_depth` and routes. Operator how-to: `docs/how-to/perplexity-mono-router-launch.md`. Pipeline note: `swarmforge/PIPELINE.md` § Mono-router idle and open slots. Endless NO_TASK pane spins are a hard-stop: handoffd halts the swarm (Telegram Operator topic + Telegram Operator topic + email + kill_all_swarm) after three consecutive chase observations (~15s) of the spin pattern so tokens are not burned on a no-op loop.


**The coordinator's Operator topic now carries a full voice-note conversation, not just text (BL-426 slice 1).** Human-requested audio channel: a voice note the human sends into the standing Operator topic (BL-346) is transcribed to text before it reaches the coordinator on the existing text-delivery path, and the coordinator's text reply is synthesized back to a spoken voice note (plus the text transcript alongside, for skimmability) sent to the same topic — multi-turn conversation falls out for free, since the Operator topic already carries context across turns. `decideVoiceUpdateAction` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) is the pure inbound decision — a voice note in the coordinator's Operator topic from the authorised principal resolves to `transcribe` (carrying the voice file's `file_id`); a non-principal's voice note is `refuse`; a voice note in any other topic is `not-applicable`, so BL-425's per-role steering topics and every other existing route are untouched by this slice. `attemptVoiceDelivery` is the adapter-driven half: it downloads the voice note and calls the injected `transcribeVoice` adapter, then delivers the transcript on the same path an ordinary text message already uses, and marks the turn voice-originated (`markVoiceOriginatedTurn`) so the reply side knows to speak back. On the way out, `synthesizeVoiceReplyIfNeeded` checks that marker on the coordinator's reply and, if set, calls the injected `synthesizeVoice` adapter and `sendVoice`s the result to the same topic alongside the text reply already sent — a TTS failure degrades silently to text-only rather than losing the answer. A text message in the coordinator topic is completely unaffected (no transcription, no voice-out). Failure posture follows the BL-389 precedent: a transient STT failure does not advance the Telegram offset and is retried, never silently dropped; a structurally un-processable voice note (empty/wrong format) is a deliberate drop and the offset advances so it can never park redelivery forever. STT and TTS are provider-adapter seams (`transcribeVoiceNote`/`synthesizeVoiceReply`, `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`) wired to OpenAI (Whisper for STT, `tts-1`/`alloy` for TTS) behind a new **`OPENAI_API_KEY`** environment variable read in the extension host only (never written to the target repo or a commit, per the secrets rule) — absent, voice I/O is simply not wired and the bot behaves exactly as before this ticket. No new human-facing command; the human can now speak to the coordinator's Operator topic and get a spoken reply back, and text conversation there is unchanged. Scope is the coordinator's Operator topic only — voice for the other seven roles' topics is a tracked, parked follow-up (depends on BL-425) not built in this slice.

**Acceptance step files now reap the detached process trees they spawn, on abnormal exit too, plus a standalone reaper for whatever a crashed run already left behind (BL-458).** Live incident, Operator directive relayed 2026-07-16: four orphaned test mini-swarms (12 stray `claude` agents, 4 `front_desk_supervisor.bb` trees with live bridge+bot children) survived ~17.8h after a Jul-15 acceptance run, reparented to init, ~1.45 GB RAM, their bots 404-hammering `api.telegram.org`. The root cause is structural, not a one-off: `launch_front_desk.sh` ends with `nohup bb <supervisor> ... &`, and `role_lifecycle.sh`'s `create_role_session` starts a detached `tmux -S <socket>` server — both deliberately detach and reparent to init, so teardown can never rely on child-process death and must hunt-and-kill by pidfile/root-path/socket instead. `specs/pipeline/steps/lib/fixtureReaper.js` is the shared prevention half: `onAbnormalExit(fn)` installs one `'exit'`/`'SIGINT'`/`'SIGTERM'` handler set per process and lets each step file register its own kill callback against it (rather than each file's proven fixture-specific kill logic being replaced), so cleanup now fires even when a scenario throws before its own inline teardown or the runner itself is killed; `track(root)`/`reap(root)` build on the same primitive for the front-desk pidfile shape. All four named offenders (`frontDeskHeadlessLauncherSteps.js`, which previously had no safety net beyond inline teardown in terminal `Then` steps, plus `frontDeskSurvivesRebootSteps.js`, `mergedCodeReachesDaemonsSteps.js`, `roleLifecycleParkUnneededSteps.js`, which each had only a `process.on('exit', ...)` handler that never fires on SIGTERM/SIGINT/timeout/OOM) now go through it. The auto-clean half mirrors BL-412/BL-413's shape: `fixture_reaper_lib.bb`'s pure `reapable?` predicate (allowlist-only known fixture prefixes, staleness, with the live swarm's own socket root excluded first and unconditionally, regardless of age) plus `fixture_reaper_sweep_lib.bb`'s real wiring (kill any process rooted in a reaped root via `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, kill any tmux server under it, delete the tree) is wired into `operator_runtime.bb`'s existing tick loop alongside the BL-412/BL-413 sweeps, ordered so a process this reaper kills lets a later `sandbox-sweep!` tick remove the now-emptied root; `reap_stale_test_fixtures.bb` exposes the same real sweep as a standalone CLI for ad hoc/manual use, mirroring `resolve_swarm_socket.bb`'s Babashka-callable-without-FFI pattern. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** added direct unit coverage of `reap()`'s own file-parsing branches (missing/corrupt `status.json` falling through to the pidfile kill, missing pidfile, tmux-socket kill, idempotent double-reap) — the acceptance suite's SIGTERM scenario had only ever proven the signal-handling mechanism against one always-complete fixture, never these branches, and never touches `track()`/`onAbnormalExit()` themselves, which install real signal handlers on the current process. No new human-facing command or setting; this is internal test-infrastructure hygiene, same category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-459 — reconciling today's four live orphans falls out of this reaper rather than a manual kill, per the Operator directive.

**BL-222's cadence-wiring acceptance check pinned `dispatch-gap-sweep!` to the first 600 characters after its anchor text, so an unrelated comment addition turned a correct wiring into a permanent false red (BL-890).** The check exists to pin a non-behavioral property — that `dispatch-gap-sweep!` shares `chase-sweep!`'s existing cadence conditional in `handoffd.bb` rather than running off a separate timer — but implemented it as a character-offset search: split the source on `chase-sweep-every-cycles))`, then require the sweep name within the first 600 characters of what followed. The BL-617 comment block that now opens that conditional pushed the real call to index 1267, so the step threw on every run in every checkout while the wiring it was meant to protect stayed correct. `specs/pipeline/steps/dispatchGapSteps.js` replaces the offset window with `locateCadenceConditional`/`checkSweepWiredInCadence`: `findMatchingParen` balances parens from the conditional's own anchor (`(when (zero? (mod cycle chase-sweep-every-cycles))`), skipping comments and string literals, to find the conditional's true structural extent by its own bounds rather than another magic character count; the sweep name is then checked for membership within that exact block, so the verdict no longer depends on how much prose precedes it. The two failure modes are now distinct rather than conflated: `conditional-not-found` (the anchor text itself can't be located, e.g. after a rename) versus `sweep-not-wired` (the conditional exists but the sweep call isn't inside it) — each produces its own message, so a future rename of the anchor text reports what actually happened instead of masquerading as an unwired sweep. `handoffd.bb` itself is untouched — the wiring was already correct, only the check was stale — and no sibling handler in `dispatchGapSteps.js` used the same offset-window idiom. New coder-authored property tests (`extension/test/bl890CadenceWiringInvariants.property.test.js`) cover both of the ticket's declared invariants, non-vacuity confirmed by hand against a reintroduced 600-char-window bug; the BL-890 feature draft was promoted to a live `.feature` with new step handlers exercising both failure modes against synthetic in-memory source. No production behavior changed; same internal test-infrastructure-hygiene category as BL-412/BL-413/BL-420/BL-458/BL-459/BL-714/BL-720/BL-800.

**A standing "Recert" Telegram topic now carries the whole Gherkin recertification loop in-chat — validate, amend, delete — giving the previously-dark recert store its first live writer (BL-450).** Human-requested full move out of the PWA, distinct from BL-339's notify-and-deep-link-only shape (which the human explicitly declined): before this ticket, `recert-state.json` had zero production writers (`confirmScenario`/`writeRecertStore`/`appendRecertProposal` existed since BL-150 but were only ever called from tests), so `lastReviewedIso` never advanced and the oldest-first batch never rotated outside the PWA's `mailto:`-only flow. `conciergeTick.ts` now posts the current oldest-unreviewed scenario (`computeRecertBatch(targetPath, 1)`, the same derivation the PWA itself uses — never a second selection) into a standing Recert topic one scenario at a time, edit-in-place and edge-triggered off a durable `recertPosted` marker in `TickState` — a same-scenario tick touches nothing, and an empty queue posts nothing at all rather than a placeholder (unlike the Approvals roster/Pipeline Board syncs, which always render something). `recertPosting.ts` renders the scenario id, title, Gherkin text, and the three reply verbs; `recertPostingSync.ts` is the adapter-driven I/O half, reusing the same `editInPlaceMessageSync.ts` core the Approvals roster and Pipeline Board already share. Reply routing is a new reserved subject, `RECERT_SUBJECT_ID`, checked in `telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`'s `decideUpdateAction` ahead of the ordinary post-existing-subject branch (the same posture as the Approvals topic's own `APPROVALS_SUBJECT_ID` check) and parsed by `recertTopicReply.ts`'s `classifyRecertTopicReply` — a scenario-id-bound grammar (`validate <id>`, `amend <id> <text>`, `delete <id>`), a separate module from the Approvals topic's bare-verb grammar since recert is a distinct domain (Gherkin scenarios, not backlog tickets) with its own two-step delete confirmation. **Verb mapping, matching the human's chosen gate:** `validate` calls `confirmScenario`/`writeRecertStore` directly (low-risk, a timestamp bump); `amend`/`delete` only ever `appendRecertProposal` a proposal into the existing `recert_proposals/<month>.jsonl` queue for specifier review — no chat reply ever edits a `.feature` file directly. `delete <id>` itself queues nothing: it checks the named scenario is genuinely up for recert, then arms a pending-delete marker and asks for an explicit "confirm" reply before `queueRecertDeleteProposal` runs (BL-150 recert-04) — a bare "confirm" with nothing pending is a silent drop, never treated as one more unrecognized reply. A reply naming a scenario not currently up for recert (a stale or fabricated id) is surfaced back into the topic, never silently applied (front-desk-operator-fabricates-backlog-state memory) or fabricated as accepted. **Cleaner pass, same ticket:** extracted `plainTextEditInPlaceAdapters()` so the roster and recert posting adapters stop duplicating the same postMessage/editMessage lambdas, and collapsed the Approvals/Recert reserved-subject dispatch in `decideUpdateAction`/`processMessageUpdate` into shared helpers to bring both functions' CRAP back under the article's <=6 gate after the new Recert branch pushed it to 7; added the missing `ensureRecertTopic` tests mirroring `ensureApprovalsTopic`'s existing coverage. New human-facing surface: a standing "Recert" Telegram topic with reply grammar `validate <id>` / `amend <id> <text>` / `delete <id>` then `confirm`. The PWA's recert view and BL-339's deep-link notify are unchanged by this ticket — retiring them is BL-451, sequenced after this loop is proven live.

**The PWA recert view and BL-339's deep-link notify are retired — recertification lives only in the Recert Telegram topic now (BL-451).** The RETIRE half of the human's full-move directive, sequenced after BL-450 proved the Telegram loop live (never removing the old path before the new one worked). Removed: `pwa/app.js`'s recert view (the confirm/update/delete `mailto:` verbs, the BL-271 Listen control, the BL-280 backlog-context card) and its `pwa/locales.js` strings; BL-339's notify CLI (`extension/src/tools/notify-recert-batch.ts`), its `recertBatchNotifier.ts` decision logic, the `handoffd.bb` `recert-notify-sweep!` wiring, and the now-dead `buildRecertDeepLink`/`#recert=1` deep link (`pwaDeepLinks.ts`) — its only target, the PWA recert view, no longer exists, so the nudge would have 404'd; and the recert-batch.json publish step (`.github/workflows/backlog-dashboard.yml`) plus its `generate-recert-batch.ts` CLI, which existed only to feed the deleted view (BL-450 reads `computeRecertBatch` server-side directly, never that published artifact — confirmed by grep before deleting). Kept, deliberately: `computeRecertBatch`, the recert store modules (`recertification.ts`/`recertificationStore.ts`), and the inbound-email verdict path (`api/recert-webhook.js`) — BL-450 depends on all three, and the inbound-email path is orthogonal to this ticket's scope. Two acceptance-step regressions the removal exposed were fixed in the same slice: `accessibilitySteps.js`'s PWA keyboard/label check had pointed at the deleted mailto Space-activation and recert-textarea aria-label, repointed at the still-live collapsible-section header and Listen control (same contract, different element); `clisTestedInProcessSteps.js`'s owned-CLI list still expected `recertificationStore.test.js`'s now-removed CLI subprocess spawn. BL-150/BL-223/BL-271/BL-280/BL-339's own feature files and step handlers were left untouched per the superseded-scenario convention — retiring Gherkin is the specifier's lane, not the coder's — so BL-339's scenarios were separately retired to a tombstone (successor mapping to BL-450/BL-451 recorded in the feature file, `acceptance.steps: []` on the done ticket) and its now-registrationless step handler (`recertNotifySteps.js`) removed by the hardener once nothing referenced it. New human-facing state: the phone PWA no longer shows a recert view or verbs, no Telegram deep-link notify is ever sent, and recertification is reachable only through the standing Recert Telegram topic (BL-450).

**One standing "Approvals" Telegram topic now aggregates every ticket awaiting approval, with a live roster, replacing the old per-ticket ask (BL-434).** Human-requested, via Telegram, 2026-07-15: today's approval ask lives scattered across each ticket's own BL topic (BL-357/BL-408/BL-409/BL-410), so the human has to hunt across topics to find what is waiting. The human's considered shape, resolved via `AskUserQuestion` then corrected on a first self-unblocked narrower cut: **BOTH** — a live index AND acting in the one topic. `topicRouter.ts`'s `routeEvent` now dispatches `ApprovalRequested` to its own `routeApprovalRequestedEvent` path instead of the old per-ticket reuse/create — it posts the ask into the ONE standing Approvals topic (`ensureApprovalsTopic`, create-once/reuse exactly like the existing standing Operator topic), and the ask text now NAMES the ticket ("`BL-123 needs your approval... Reply here with "approve BL-123"...`") since one topic now carries every ticket's ask at once. **The one genuinely new mechanism** is `pendingApprovalReply.ts`'s `classifyApprovalsTopicReply` — a separate, narrower parser from the existing per-ticket-topic `classifyApprovalReplyAction` (the two topics have different reply grammars: bare "approve" vs "approve `<id>`"), which `telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`'s `decideUpdateAction` now consults first for any reply landing in the reserved `APPROVALS_SUBJECT_ID` subject, ahead of the ordinary post-existing-subject branch. It reuses the EXISTING `recordApprovalReply`/`recordRejectionReply` adapters — never a second recording path — and their own boolean `changed` result to tell "this id really was pending, now recorded" from "this id was not pending", surfacing the latter back into the Approvals topic (`notifyApprovalsTopic`) rather than silently dropping it (front-desk-operator-fabricates-backlog-state memory); both an unrecognized reply and a not-pending id are DELIBERATE DROPS, so the poll offset always advances past either rather than parking (the BL-389 drop-vs-failure distinction). **The live index half:** `approvalsRoster.ts`'s pure `renderApprovalsRoster` renders the current `pendingApprovalFor` set (sorted by id, so the rendered text is deterministic tick over tick) into one roster message, which `approvalsRosterSync.ts` posts-or-edits IN PLACE, change-gated on the rendered text itself (never a set diff) — a genuine pending-set change edits the one message; an unchanged tick touches nothing, so this never becomes the first-tick unthrottled mass-edit storm the engineering article warns about (it is always exactly one message). **Cleaner pass, same ticket:** the create-once/post-or-edit control flow was byte-for-byte duplicated between the new roster sync and the existing Pipeline Board sync, so both now share one `editInPlaceMessageSync.ts` core, each supplying only its own render function and adapter. Per BL-424, a ticket's own topic-icon awaiting-approval state keeps working even though the ask itself no longer posts there: `ensurePerTicketTopicForIcon` still creates the per-ticket topic (never posts into it) purely so the icon sync has somewhere to set the icon. No change to how approval is recorded on disk (`human_approval` YAML field, BL-409 reject-reason sanitization) — only where the ask is posted and how a reply is routed to a ticket. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** killed a surviving Gherkin mutant and brought CRAP back under the article's threshold.
