New human-facing surface: a standing "Approvals" Telegram topic, and the reply grammar in that topic is now `approve <id>` / `reject <id> <reason>` rather than bare `approve`/`reject <reason>`.

**The Approvals-topic ask now carries the ticket's title, a what-it-solves summary, and its acceptance signal, not just a bare id (BL-480).** Human-reported defect, 2026-07-17, on receiving the first BL-479 approval ask: "there is not enough info to approve." Before this ticket `approvalRequestedText` (`topicRouter.ts`) rendered only the frozen `<id> needs your approval... Reply here with...` line — the human had to leave Telegram and open the repo to see what they were being asked to approve, defeating BL-410's one-tap Approve/Amend/Reject buttons. `approvalRequestedText` now takes the full event (mirroring BL-322's `taskStartedText` shape: same field truncation, same `firstParagraph`/`truncate` helpers) and, when a ticket summary is available, prepends `<id> — <title>`, a `What it solves:` line drawn from the ticket's `notes:`, a `First acceptance signal:` line, and — when the ticket sets it — an `Approval context:` line from BL-479's `approval_context` field; a ticket with no summary source still falls back to the original bare line. The frozen reply-grammar clause and the `needs your approval` substring (which five sibling step files locate the ask by) are always appended verbatim AFTER the enrichment body's own truncation, so the reply grammar, the Approve/Amend/Reject buttons, and those five locators stay byte-identical regardless of how long the enrichment runs; the whole message is still capped under Telegram's 4096-char limit. Wires `approval_context` end-to-end for the first time: parsed in `backlogReader.ts`, carried through `conciergeTick.ts`'s `TicketSummary`/`ticketSummariesFor` (which now also builds its map from paused tickets, not just active ones, so a paused ticket's ask no longer silently degrades to the bare id-only line), and threaded into `ApprovalRequested`'s event payload (`swarmEventStream.ts`), which previously was always `{}`. No new human-facing command; an existing Approvals-topic ask now shows enough context to decide from without leaving Telegram.

**An agent's clarifying question now surfaces directly on Telegram — as a native poll when it has discrete options, starting with the specifier (BL-466).** Human-requested via the Operator front desk, 2026-07-16, for iso-functionality with the in-editor `AskUserQuestion` UI: previously a specifier's question reached the human only indirectly through the Concierge's derived-event machinery. `operator_ask.bb <project-root> --thread <SUP-###> --question <q> [--options '["a","b"]']` now accepts an optional `--options` (a JSON array of 2+ strings); `parse-options` (`operator_lib.bb`) normalizes it to `nil` on any malformed input (invalid JSON, a bare number, an array of non-strings) rather than crashing and losing the question outright, so a bad `--options` value degrades to the same plain-message path as no options at all, never a dropped ask. Every reply-outbox entry `operator_ask.bb` writes — including its escalate-once and re-home continuations (BL-306/BL-354) — is now marked `agentQuestion: true`, alongside `options` when present, so the front-desk bot can distinguish an agent's own question from an ordinary Operator/approval message without a second channel. A new standing "Agent Questions" Telegram topic (`AGENT_QUESTIONS_SUBJECT_ID`, create-once/reuse exactly like the existing standing Operator/Approvals topics) is where these land: `telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`'s `deliverAgentQuestion` renders a native poll via `telegramClient.ts`'s new `sendPoll` wrapper when `options` has 2+ entries, or a plain message otherwise — the two-or-none contract the ticket specifies, never a one-option poll. The Agent Questions side channel is attempted LAST, after the ordinary per-ticket/Operator/Approvals routing, so it only ever fires for a genuine `agentQuestion` record. The human's answer flows back through BL-325's EXISTING awaiting-answer/unblock machinery, never a parallel path: a poll vote or an in-topic reply resolves to the pending question's own `SUP-###` thread via `resolvePollThread`/`getPendingAgentQuestionThread`, backed by a `readPollMap`/`writePollMap` poll-id-to-thread lookup and the runtime's own `awaiting-answer.json` read — both newly exported and given fixture-backed wiring tests (including a break-then-fix proof that the `awaiting-answer.json` read is load-bearing, since the wiring test's fixture had never actually placed the file). An unanswered question inherits BL-306/BL-325's bounded-await posture unchanged — escalate once, then drop the awaiting state — so a poll can never block an agent forever. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** the cooldown gate (BL-149/BL-463) skip-cooldown'd the touched TS files and Babashka scripts this pass, each independently touched by a sibling ticket on `main` within the preceding few hours; Gherkin mutation was out of scope (the feature file uses plain `Scenario`, no `Scenario Outline`/`Examples`). No change to the pipeline's derived-event/topic-routing machinery for tickets or approvals — this is a new, narrower delivery path scoped to an agent's own clarifying question. New human-facing surface: a standing "Agent Questions" Telegram topic; a discrete-option question now appears there as a native poll, an open-ended one as a plain message, and either resolves back to the asking agent exactly like any other BL-325 answer.

**A single `build_freshness_cli.bb sync` pass now settles operator_runtime's staleness instead of requiring a second pass (BL-433).** Root cause, confirmed in code: `restart-operator-group!` relaunches the stale `operator_runtime.bb` process asynchronously and returns immediately, without clearing or waiting on its `status.json`; `run-sync!` then reports from a snapshot gathered BEFORE the restart. So even a perfect restart's own sync output — and any immediate `report` right after it — still showed operator_runtime stale, and the coordinator had been papering over this by re-syncing on every bookkeeping cycle. Fix, mirroring the front-desk group's own restart path (which already deletes its `status.json` and relaunches synchronously, so it never exhibited this race): `restart-operator-group!` now deletes operator_runtime's `status.json` before relaunching, then blocks up to a human-approved 10s for it to reappear with `:build_sha` == `main` HEAD; `run-sync!`'s report reflects that settled post-restart state, not the pre-restart snapshot. If the new process never publishes fresh status within the 10s bound, `sync` fails loudly (non-zero exit) rather than hanging or falsely reporting fresh. Front-desk and handoffd sync behavior is unchanged — only the operator-group race is closed. No new human-facing command; this is an internal fix to the swarm's own build-freshness tool (`swarmforge/scripts/build_freshness_cli.bb`), removing the need for the coordinator's re-sync workaround.

**A Claude Code AskUserQuestion (or kin) menu that blocks a role pane now auto-surfaces in that role's Telegram steering topic as a non-anonymous mapped poll — or a text fallback naming the RC session when Telegram poll caps cannot carry the option set honestly — and only the human's poll_answer drives the menu (BL-568).** Live incident 2026-07-23: steering the coordinator from topic 1602 could not see or answer an in-pane menu; BL-466 polls covered operator_ask / Agent Questions only. Chase (`chase_sweep_lib.bb` `bl568DetectMenuBlocked` / extract / poll-surface-plan) classifies menu chrome + options as BLOCKED (not idle), plans a poll under Telegram caps (question ≤300, ≤10 options, option ≤100, ellipsis truncate) or a text+RC fallback when caps would force a lying poll, and fingerprints question+options at surface time. Front desk extends BL-466 `sendPoll`/`recordPollMapping` with mapping kind `menu-answer` (`telegramClient.ts` `bl568MenuAnswerPollMapping`): role, pane id, option order, fingerprint, multi-select, free-text option indexes; `is_anonymous` false; `allows_multiple_answers` mirrors checkbox menus. On `poll_answer`, `bl568PlanMenuAnswerDrive` re-checks the live fingerprint before any keystroke — stale or cleared menus drop with a receipt, never type blind; free-text election converts to a guarded in-topic text hand-off once the menu reaches text-entry. Ordinary BL-425/BL-566 steers while menu-blocked are not injected; `formatSteerReceipt` gains `menu_blocked` (`⚠ <role> is menu_blocked — see live poll …`). Timeout leaves the menu untouched and re-notifies at most once — the automation never auto-answers. Out of scope: non-principal voters, operator_ask flows, RC deep-links in the poll message, non-Claude menus. New human-facing surface: answering an in-pane menu from the same role steering topic via poll (or RC-named text fallback), plus the `menu_blocked` steer receipt. How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-568-menu-blocked-pane-questions-as-mapped-polls.md`.

**A live production caller now actually reaches the poll path above (BL-466 wiring fix).** QA bounced the ticket above as shipped-but-dark: `--options` and its whole poll machinery were fully built, unit- and acceptance-tested, but the only real (non-test) invocation site of `operator_ask.bb` — the disposable Operator LLM's own ASK instructions in `swarmforge/roles/operator.prompt` — still only ever constructed the plain `--question` form, so a specifier's discrete-option question would degrade to a plain message forever in the live swarm (the same "correct and green but invoked by nothing" class already on file for `mutation_cooldown_gate.bb`, BL-149). Fix: `operator.prompt`'s ASK section now instructs the Operator to also pass `--options '["<choice-1>","<choice-2>",...]'` when the question it is relaying has a small, fixed set of discrete answers (e.g. a specifier's `AskUserQuestion`-style decision menu), and to omit it for a genuinely open-ended question — degrading, exactly as `parse-options` already handles, to the plain-message form. No code changes; this closes the wiring gap in the Operator's own prompt instructions, the one real caller BL-466's poll machinery needed.

**Multi-option agent questions now render as tappable Telegram buttons instead of a native poll (BL-483).** Human-requested 2026-07-17, from a screenshot of the coordinator's remote-control multi-option question, asking for iso-functionality on Telegram. Supersedes BL-466's poll branch for this case — a poll cannot carry a per-option description, cannot be edited after answering, and forces a 2-option minimum, all real gaps against the in-editor `AskUserQuestion` shape (label + short description per option, plus an implicit "type something else"). `operator_ask.bb`'s `--options` now accepts each element as a plain string OR a `{label, description}` object, normalized by `operator-lib/ask-options` (unlike poll-options, a single usable option is kept — no artificial minimum). `deliverAgentQuestion` renders one inline-keyboard button per option (label on the button, description in the message body) plus a standing "reply with your own answer" hint — Telegram's own reply box is the free-text affordance. A tap's `callback_data` carries the ask's thread id plus the option's own INDEX, never the label text (Telegram's 64-byte `callback_data` cap); the chosen label routes back through `postToBridge`, the SAME shared answer effect path a typed reply and BL-466's poll answer both already use — one effect path, never a second one. Staleness (a tap on a retracted or already-answered ask) reuses the existing `awaiting-answer.json` "one pending question at a time" store as the single source of truth: a tap on a thread that is no longer the pending one produces no side effect and edits the message to a "no longer open" notice instead, mirroring BL-484's approval-ask closing routine. BL-466's `sendPoll`/`recordPollMapping`/`processPollAnswer` stay wired (still-correct, generically reusable poll-answer handling) but are no longer reached from this path. Out of scope here (specifier work, human-reviewed wording): the role-prompt change routing an unattended role's multi-option question through this mechanism. New human-facing behavior: an agent's multi-option question in the "Agent Questions" Telegram topic now shows tappable buttons with per-option descriptions instead of a native poll; an open-ended question is unchanged.

**The front-desk standing topic is rebranded Operator -> Concierge: bell icon (🛎), "Concierge" label (BL-453).** Human-requested rebrand, glyph human-chosen 2026-07-16 ("The bell is fine" = 🛎), superseding BL-418's opera-house (🏛) choice for this one standing topic — the support/intake (🎟), approvals (📋), and recert (📜) standing-topic icons are unchanged. `STANDING_TOPIC_ICON.operator` in `topicIcon.ts` changes from 🏛 to 🛎; the live tick's `syncStandingTopicIcons` never re-touches an already-seen topic on its own, so an existing install's front-desk topic only picks up the new sticker via a one-time `backfill-standing-topic-icons.js` run — the same operational step BL-342/BL-418 already established, not new wiring. `OPERATOR_TOPIC_NAME` in `telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts` changes from `'Operator'` to `'Concierge'`; since the front-desk topic is already created and bound for any existing install, a name-constant change alone would never reach it, so `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`'s `ensureOperatorTopic` gained `syncStandingTopicTitleIfNeeded` — on the existing "reuse" path it renames the live topic via `editForumTopic` exactly once (a durable, bot-owned, machine-local `telegram-standing-topic-titles.json` record, gitignored under `.swarmforge/`, prevents re-editing an already-correct title on every restart), while a brand-new install's create path gets the new name for free and records it immediately so the reuse-path check never fires a redundant rename. `OPERATOR_SUBJECT_ID` (the durable binding/ownership key) is unchanged — only the icon and the display name move; the existing bound topic is reused, never re-minted. Out of scope: the broader Operator -> Concierge rename of message signatures/bylines is a separate, still-unfiled follow-up. No new human-facing command; the same front-desk topic now shows the bell icon and is titled "Concierge" instead of the opera house and "Operator".

**Pipeline board: the new message now posts before the old one is deleted, so a board is always visible (BL-468).** Human-requested directly 2026-07-16: "first add the new one, then remove the old one, so there is at least always 1 to look at." Before this, BL-462's repost-at-bottom mechanism deleted the old board message FIRST, then posted the fresh one — a window with zero board messages in the topic, and if the fresh post then failed, the old message was already gone while `state.messageId` still pointed at it. `pipelineBoardSync.ts`'s `postBoardMessage` now reorders to post-new-then-delete-old: on a successful post, the prior message is deleted best-effort only AFTER the new one exists (the delete's existing best-effort posture — a failed or already-gone delete never blocks); on a FAILED post, the prior message is left alone and the outcome reports a failed post with the prior `messageId` still tracked in state, so the existing board stays visible. No renderer, change-gate, or adapter-interface change — only the call order inside `postBoardMessage` and the failed-post branch. Two board messages can briefly coexist during the swap; this is compatible with BL-467's pin sync (pins the newest, continuously unpins the old) and BL-465's render. No new human-facing command; the "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now never has a moment with no board message visible, even across a post failure.

**Pipeline-board stage map: a differently-cased ticket id in a handoff header no longer risks silently dropping an active ticket from the board (BL-471).** Defensive hardening of BL-464's authoritative ticket->stage source, from a coordinator note whose specific live claim did not reproduce (verified 2026-07-16: every real handoff header in the tree already uses upper-case `BL-`, and the reported "missing" ticket was simply not held by any role at the time — correct behaviour, not a bug). The latent gap itself is real: `swarmforge/scripts/pipeline_stage_lib.bb` joined a role's held-ticket id (extracted verbatim, whatever case a note/task header used) against the canonical, always-upper-case `id:` field of each active backlog item by an exact-case `contains?` — so a handoff header that ever led with a lower- or mixed-case id (e.g. a note whose `message:` begins "bl-447 ...") would fail that membership test and vanish from the board with no error. The ticket-id join is now case-insensitive: the extracted header id is canonicalized to upper-case before both the active-set membership check and the stage-map reconciliation, so a handoff header leading with a differently-cased id resolves to the same active ticket and appears on the board at its correct stage. Kept pure/side-effect-free, matching the file's existing posture. No new human-facing command; this is a robustness fix to the internal "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic's ticket-stage data source, not a behavior change for any header that was already upper-case (i.e. every real header observed in production).

**Swarm stop (drain or emergency), restart, and a timed intake-freeze pause are now driven from a guarded Telegram control topic (BL-423).** Human-requested via the Operator front desk (2026-07-15, amended same day for drain/emergency-stop split and timed pause): drive swarm stop/start from the phone without needing the VS Code extension host in the foreground. Three verbs, one dedicated control topic, sent by the authorised principal only — the same principal/topic guard BL-408/409 already use for Telegram verbs, applied here to a destructive/administrative surface for the first time:
- **`/stop`** posts one confirmation with two action buttons plus Cancel — **Drain & stop** and **Emergency stop** — executing nothing until a button is tapped; there is no separate `/forcestop` verb. Emergency stop tears down immediately with no drain wait. Drain stop waits for every role's `inbox/in_process` to empty first, bounded by a drain timeout (default 10 minutes, human-set, env-overridable for tests); if the pipeline has not drained by then, teardown is forced and the outcome is reported `forced` rather than `drained`. Both modes reap every swarm-owned process — tmux windows and any reparented orphaned vitest workers, the exact class behind the BL-422 OOM-spiral — through `kill_all_swarm.sh`'s socket-scoped path.
- **`/restart`** posts a confirmation and, on confirm, reuses the existing sanctioned bounce path (`remote_bounce.sh` sentinel -> the extension host's `bounceWatcher`/`bounceDrain`/`bounceAck`) rather than a new respawn mechanism, streaming each bounce phase (draining -> stopping -> relaunching -> done/failed) back into the control topic. A relaunch that creates tmux windows but never actually bootstraps agents into them (the earlier `SWARM_CONTROL_LOST` half-launch failure mode) is reported `failed`, not `done` — the verify-ready step checks agents actually bootstrapped, not merely that windows exist.
- **`/pause`** posts a duration menu (15 min / 1 hr / 4 hr / Until I resume); picking a duration IS the action, no separate confirm, since pause is non-destructive and auto-reverting. The semantic is FREEZE NEW-WORK INTAKE only — agents stay alive, in-flight parcels finish, no new paused item is promoted — never a process suspend or a teardown+relaunch. The freeze rides the coordinator's own effective-active-backlog-depth read (`swarmforge/scripts/backlog_depth_lib.bb`, the same primitive the health-throttling circuit breaker already uses to drop the cap to 0): a live, unexpired pause marker under `.swarmforge/` (gitignored, host-persisted, reached through a redirectable env seam) makes that computation return 0, so the existing promotion gate freezes with no new per-caller logic. A timed pick auto-resumes and posts a "resumed" notice to the control topic when its duration elapses (evaluated against an injected clock via the daemon's existing sweep cadence); "Until I resume" has no timer and stays frozen until an explicit `Resume now` tap, which restores intake immediately and clears any pending auto-resume.

Every inline-button tap (a stop-mode pick, a pause-duration pick, Resume) RE-APPLIES the principal + topic guards — an unauthorised tap on someone else's pending control button is refused with no swarm action, since anyone in a Telegram group can tap another human's button. An unauthorised sender's verb, or any of the three verbs sent outside the dedicated control topic, is likewise refused/ignored with no action. The verb/callback parse, guards, confirm state machine, and pause state machine are one pure host-side module (`telegramControlCore.ts`, mirroring `operatorDecideStatus.ts`'s shape): given a message/callback, principal, topic, pending-confirm state, pause state, and the current time, it decides `ignore | prompt-stop-modes | prompt-restart-confirm | execute-emergency-stop | execute-drain-stop | execute-restart | cancel | post-pause-menu | apply-pause | auto-resume | resume-now | refuse` — unit-tested with fixtures, no live Telegram or tmux. New human-facing surface: a dedicated Telegram control topic with `/stop`, `/restart`, and `/pause` (plus their confirmation buttons and, while paused, a `Resume now` button).

**Pipeline board render round 2: a short kebab slug leads every entry, PK/AA per-line labels are dropped in favour of their own sections, and a tappable GitHub link list rides below the grid (BL-465).** Human-requested via the Operator front desk 2026-07-16, refined the same day ("add the slug back to the pipeline board grid — there will be room enough for 2 or 3 words"): the aligned stage GRID's dedicated slug column now shows only a short (2-3 word) kebab slug derived from the ticket's backlog filename (e.g. `BL-467-pipeline-board-only-pin` -> `pipeline-board-only-pin`) — the grid has no separate title column to widen, so it carries the slug alone. The BELOW-GRID lists (parked / awaiting-approval / paused / root-intake / recently-closed) lead each entry with that same kebab slug and then fill the remaining landscape width with more of the truncated title than before. This deliberately supersedes BL-462's own "wider slug in the grid" contract (`deriveTicketSlug`/`PIPELINE_BOARD_SLUG_MAX_LENGTH` used to size the grid's own slug column for a wide truncated title); a follow-up retires BL-462's now-stale grid-slug scenario the same way BL-470 retired BL-452's superseded scenarios. The redundant per-line "PK" label is dropped from the parked list (the section header already says parked); awaiting-approval keeps its distinction via its own "AWAITING APPROVAL:" section instead of a per-line "AA" label. Two new sections appear alongside parked: PAUSED (`backlog/paused/` items) and ROOT-INTAKE (raw `backlog/` root asks), plus a RECENTLY-CLOSED section. Since Telegram cannot render links inside a `<pre>` block, every ticket id (grid rows and every below-grid section) is instead linked in a separate TAPPABLE LINK LIST below the grid, keyed by ticket id and pointing at the ticket's backlog file on GitHub (active/paused/done path resolved from the item's actual folder, base URL derived from the origin remote) — the aligned monospace grid itself stays link-free. `conciergeTick.ts` supplies the paused list, root-intake list, recently-closed list, and repo base URL as live local/git reads (the board is the live holistic surface per the local-engineering two-surface rule, not the static PWA projection). No new human-facing command; the existing "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now shows a kebab-slug-led grid, four below-grid sections instead of inline PK/AA labels, and a tappable GitHub link list.

**Bug fix, same feature (BL-465 bounce): the RECENTLY-CLOSED section now actually shows the N most-recently-closed tickets, in closure order.** Two compounding defects had it showing an arbitrary subset in an arbitrary order instead: `conciergeTick.ts`'s `recentlyClosedItems` fed `folders.done` straight through with no ordering at all before `PIPELINE_BOARD_RECENTLY_CLOSED_MAX`'s `slice(0, N)` truncated whatever order `readdir` happened to return, and `pipelineBoard.ts`'s `computePipelineBoard` then re-sorted the already-sliced list alphabetically by id — silently discarding any order a caller did supply, contradicting the module's own documented "the caller decides ordering" contract. Fixed by adding a durable, monotonic `doneClosedAtMs` map on `TickState` (stamped once per ticket the first tick it's observed in `folders.done`, deliberately independent of the event-routing retry snapshot so a stuck completion message never rejuvenates a ticket's recorded close time — the same durability posture `standingIconSeenIds` already uses), sorting `recentlyClosedItems` by it before slicing, and dropping `computePipelineBoard`'s alphabetical re-sort so the caller's recency order survives to render. A ticket closed before this field existed has no timestamp and sorts after every timestamped ticket, the same one-time eventual-consistency gap BL-418's `standingIconSeenIds` backfill already accepts. No new human-facing command; the existing "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic's RECENTLY-CLOSED section now reflects actual closure recency instead of directory-listing order.

**Each of the 8 per-agent steering topics now carries its own human-chosen icon, so they're tellable apart at a glance (BL-469).** Human-requested via the Operator front desk 2026-07-16, folding into the BL-425 per-agent-steering-topic cluster (BL-425 shipped the eight topics themselves; this adds their icons — icon-only, no change to BL-425's question/redirect routing). BL-425's eight role steering topics were visually identical in the topic list; each now gets a firm, human-picked icon keyed by the canonical role token (`roleTopicMapStore.ALL_SWARM_ROLES`). `topicIcon.ts` gains a third table, `ROLE_TOPIC_ICON`, alongside the existing `ICON_EMOJI` (ticket state) and `STANDING_TOPIC_ICON` (standing topics) — never overloading either. `conciergeTick.ts` builds per-agent icon targets from BL-425's `roleTopicMapStore.readRoleTopicMap` and syncs each newly-owned per-agent topic's icon through the existing `topicIconSync.syncTopicIcon` (mirroring `syncStandingTopicIcons`'s newly-entering-only posture) — no new Telegram adapter, no renderer change, and the icon is set once on first ownership rather than re-edited every tick, per the engineering article's first-tick-mass-transition rule. `syncTopicIcon`'s existing guarantees carry over unchanged: it validates the desired emoji against Telegram's live `getForumTopicIconStickers` set, never touches an icon the swarm did not set (ownership), and degrades to the existing `skipped-unresolved-icon` outcome (logged, never a silent no-op or a crash) if an icon isn't in the live set. **QA bounce, same ticket (2026-07-17):** the originally-proposed eight literals (compass/note/crane/keyboard/broom/shield/magnifier/books) were only 2 of 8 (specifier, documenter) present in Telegram's live `getForumTopicIconStickers` set — the other six silently degraded to `skipped-unresolved-icon`. The table was remapped to a human-approved, live-verified set: coordinator 🎬, specifier 📝, architect 🏛, coder 💻, cleaner 🧼, hardender 🧪, QA 🔎, documenter 📚 — all eight re-verified present in the live sticker set before adoption. QA's new 🔎 also resolves the prior accepted collision with `ICON_EMOJI.paused` (🔍): the two are now visually distinct. **2nd QA bounce, same ticket (2026-07-17):** the remap above passed live-set validation but collided with the live epic-icon pool — 🎬 is `KNOWN_EPIC_ICON` (the onboarding epic) and 📚 is `EPIC_ICON_POOL`'s tail; the original "no collision" check had compared against a stale, BL-449-retired epic list (🏆⚡📁) instead of the current musical-form pool. Fixed by remapping just those two, re-verified against every live pool: coordinator 🎬 → 📣 (megaphone), documenter 📚 → 📰 (newspaper). The firm, current mapping is coordinator 📣, specifier 📝, architect 🏛, coder 💻, cleaner 🧼, hardender 🧪, QA 🔎, documenter 📰. No new human-facing command; each of the 8 per-agent steering topics now shows its own icon instead of being visually identical.

**A shared checkout's writers can no longer silently drop each other's staged content (BL-419).** Twice caught live and once directly (2026-07-15 12:19 BST): a writer staged an edit to a YAML on `main` — the coordinator's own live master checkout, shared with no isolation — committed, and `git show <new-sha>:<path>` afterward read the PRE-edit content, most visibly a just-approved ticket landing as `human_approval: pending`, re-triggering the front desk's re-ask and making the human doubt their approval landed. Root cause, confirmed directly: the master checkout has many concurrent writers sharing ONE `.git/index` (coordinator bookkeeping, the ~8/min BL-topic-record writer, QA's fast-forward/push, the specifier's spec commits, `operator_file_question.bb`), and a bare `git commit` with no pathspec commits the WHOLE index — two git invocations don't hold the index lock across their own add-to-commit gap, so whichever writer commits next captures whatever another writer staged at that instant, either clearing this writer's own staged change or sweeping it into an unrelated commit. `commit_integrity_lib.bb`'s `commit-with-integrity!` is the shared helper every master-checkout writer is meant to route through: it serializes the stage-to-commit window behind a lock scoped to the checkout's own git directory (`git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir`, so linked worktrees — each with their own physical git-dir — are never serialized against each other, only genuine same-checkout writers are), pathspec-scopes every add/commit to exactly the caller's own paths (an unrelated concurrent commit can never sweep this writer's paths into its own sha, nor vice versa), and verifies the committed content via `git show <sha>:<path>` against what the caller actually staged, retrying (a fresh commit, never an amend) within a bounded budget and failing loudly (`:success false`, non-zero exit) rather than ever reporting a dropped edit as a successful commit. `commit_integrity_cli.bb` is a thin shell wrapper over the same library for non-Babashka callers. `operator_file_question.bb` — one of the writers named in the bug report — is the first real wiring, replacing its own hand-rolled add/commit/rev-parse with a single `commit-with-integrity!` call. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** the lock acquisition itself was an unbounded `Thread/sleep` spin with no cap — a process that dies mid-lock (kill -9, OOM, host reboot) would have orphaned the lock directory forever, hanging every future caller for that checkout indefinitely, a worse and silent failure mode than the dropped-commit race this helper exists to fix. `acquire-lock!`/`release-lock!` are now bounded (default 100 attempts × 50ms) and a failed acquisition reports a loud `{:success false :reason :lock-timeout}` instead of hanging or silently proceeding unlocked. Per the ticket's own no-real-timers note, the race itself is proven via injected git-show/commit seams returning a scripted mismatch (no real concurrency), plus a real-git fixture proving pathspec scoping. **QA bounce, same ticket:** the ticket's own scope had explicitly named the coordinator's ticket-close as in-scope — the originally observed victim — but `coordinator.prompt` still described a hand-typed `git mv` + `git commit` for it, the exact unmitigated path that produced both documented incidents; the "Close" bookkeeping step now routes through `commit_integrity_cli.bb` instead. Wiring this real caller up surfaced a genuine defect in the helper itself: `default-add!`'s `git add -- oldpath newpath` failed its entire pathspec atomically once a prior `git mv` had already fully staged the rename, because the old path is no longer resolvable on disk or in the index for `git add` to match (unlike a plain `rm`, which is still index-resolvable) — every real coordinator invocation would have hit `:add-failed`. Fixed by filtering `default-add!`'s pathspec to paths that still exist on disk before calling `git add`; a path a caller's own `git mv`/`git rm` already fully staged needs no re-adding, and the verify step still catches a genuinely wrong outcome. A git-mv-shaped regression test (old path gone, new path present, an unrelated concurrently-staged path untouched) now reproduces the coordinator's real usage — the original unit suite covered only pure content edits, never a rename. The other named writers (BL-topic-record writer, QA's push, the specifier) remain open follow-up work. No new human-facing command; this is internal write-path hardening for the swarm's own shared master checkout.

**Upstream drift-watch mechanism (BL-477).** `local-engineering.prompt`'s Architecture Rule 2 already promised a drift-watch review backed by `upstream-watch.json` and `docs/upstream-deviations.md`, but neither existed until now. `upstream-watch.json` (repo root) records the last-**reviewed** commit SHA per watched upstream repo/branch — the baseline "we have looked at everything up to here" — for `unclebob/swarm-forge` (`main`, `adversaries`) and `unclebob/Acceptance-Pipeline-Specification` (`main`). `swarmforge/scripts/upstream_drift_check.bb` (+ a pure comparator lib) reads that baseline, `git ls-remote`s each watched repo, and reports any branch whose live head has advanced past the recorded SHA or any branch present upstream with no watch-file entry at all; it is strictly read-only — it never fetches into the working tree, never rewrites the watch file, and never bumps an install pin (`swarmforge.lock.json` stays the separate install-pin concern). Advancing a watch SHA is always a human decision made by editing `upstream-watch.json` directly, exactly like bumping an install pin, never something the check script does itself. This fork has no common git ancestor with `unclebob/swarm-forge`, so adopting anything a drift review finds is always a manual, deliberate reimplementation reviewed by a human, never a git merge/cherry-pick. `docs/upstream-deviations.md` is the human-readable review log the rule refers to, seeded 2026-07-17 with the baseline review (one novel `adversaries`-branch element found and dispositioned separately as BL-478). Run with `bb swarmforge/scripts/upstream_drift_check.bb`; no new human-facing command outside the swarm's own engineering tooling.

**Property testing gets an owner: the architect (BL-479).** A same-day, deeper follow-on to the BL-477 drift-watch survey: `engineering.prompt` already legislated property tests as a verification category kept separate from normal coverage/mutation/CRAP — "unless the role owns property-test verification" — but no role prompt claimed that ownership; `unclebob/swarm-forge`'s `six-pack` branch closes exactly this hole by giving its architect the job, after architectural review and before the hardener. Adapted (not ported, per BL-477's no-common-ancestor rule) into this fork: `architect.prompt` gains a "## Property Testing" section (human-approved wording) — assess property coverage of the pure modules the current task/batch touched (round-trips, conservation/counting invariants, idempotence, ordering/monotonicity, parsing/formatting stability), add or improve a `fast-check` property test where a useful property is undercovered, and demonstrate any new/changed property test non-vacuous (fails when its invariant is deliberately broken, then restored) — a support/improvement phase, not a hard pass/fail gate, so a parcel touching no property-shaped module needs nothing new. `hardender.prompt`/`QA.prompt` each gained a bullet requiring the separate property command green as part of their own verification sequence, without folding property files into coverage/mutation/CRAP/DRY. The tooling: `fast-check` is a new, exactly-pinned devDependency; `npm run test:properties` (`extension/package.json`) compiles then runs only `**/*.property.test.js` via a dedicated `vitest.properties.config.mjs`, and that same glob is excluded from the default `vitest.config.mjs` so the normal unit/coverage run and Stryker's mutation run (which reuses that config, per BL-124) never pick property files up. Seeded with one real, non-vacuous suite, `extension/test/benchmarkAggregate.property.test.js`, against `computeMean`/`computeStdDev` — mean bounded by `[min, max]`, non-negative stddev, ~0 stddev on a constant array, order-invariance, self-duplication-invariance, over a broad `fast-check`-generated range with relative-tolerance floating-point comparisons; deliberately breaking `computeMean`'s `+` into `-` fails 3 of 5 properties immediately, restoring it passes all 5 again, confirmed flake-free across 5 repeat runs. A secondary upstream finding from the same survey — the `six-pack` cleaner's mutation-site SIZE gate (split a file exceeding 100 changed-file mutation sites before handoff) — was filed as its own ticket, BL-485 (paused), rather than built here; both decisions are recorded in `docs/upstream-deviations.md`'s review log.

**Declared-invariant property tests move to the coder; the architect verifies, never first-authors (BL-654).** BL-633 gave the specifier and architect prompts an `invariants:` vocabulary, but left a measured gap: `grep -ic invariant` was 6 hits in `specifier.prompt`, 11 in `architect.prompt`, 0 in `coder.prompt` — nobody told the coder. The consequence surfaced on the mechanism's first live night: BL-635's architect send-back #1 caught a declared invariant (pre-epoch absence must render unavailable, never a fabricated `0`) only in the architect's review sweep, the FIRST point the property was ever executed — making the architect look like the property-testing role by default, the same pattern BL-590's P5/P6 architect-authored property tests showed earlier. This ticket completes the BL-633 chain (state → encode → verify → stress): `coder.prompt` gains an "Invariants" section requiring an executable property test for each `invariants:` entry on the ticket, in the same parcel as the behavior change, with the generator-reach contract stated as part of the rule rather than a footnote — the test must demonstrably reach the states the invariant quantifies over, an asserted coverage floor rather than hoped-for coverage (per [[property-test-generator-must-reach-deep-state]]). `architect.prompt`'s Invariants Review now checks existence and non-vacuity of that test FIRST, before any hand-verification of the property, and records a missing or vacuous property test under its own `invariant-unencoded` failure class, distinct from a violated-property bounce, so BL-635's bounce-class metric can tell "never encoded" apart from "violated" — the architect's `## Property Testing` section from BL-479 is otherwise unchanged and still covers undeclared properties on pure modules. The `bl654PreEpochTrend`/`bl654PreEpochInvariant` fixtures are a self-contained worked example standing in for BL-635's invariants[2] (BL-635 itself is parked, not yet on `main`), with a coder-authored property test asserting both the invariant and a counted reachability floor, runs only via `npm run test:properties`. **Hardener bounce, same ticket:** the non-vacuity check's failure-matching regex (`/pre-epoch/i`) could not distinguish the invariant assertion actually firing from the generator merely under-reaching the deep state, since the reachability-floor message also contains the string "pre-epoch" — low-severity (the generator's 8:1 epoch-index weighting made a live collision unlikely) but tightened because this file is the worked example the coder's new prompt section points at; both the real property test and the acceptance step handler now explicitly rule out a reachability-floor message before accepting a pre-epoch match.

**Per-swarm Telegram creds: a swarm's bot identity is a property of the swarm, not the launching shell (BL-436).** The one-bot-per-target rule (no shared token/chat, per BL-380) was already enforced once a swarm was running, but fragile at the launch boundary: `front_desk_supervisor.bb` resolved `botToken`/`chatId` from the ambient environment (`TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`/`TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`) and `bridgePort` from `BRIDGE_PORT`, so a second supervisor (e.g. the FES second-swarm epic's own guinea pig) launched from a shell that still had the primary's token exported would silently inherit it — a 409 conflict or, worse, silent inbound-message theft. `fleet_telegram_creds_lib.bb` (+ `fleet_telegram_creds_cli.bb`, a thin non-Babashka wrapper) reads a per-swarm creds file at `~/.swarmforge/fleet/<swarm_name>/telegram.json` (`{ botToken, chatId, bridgePort }`, under the host `$HOME`, never inside the target working tree — the same secrets-stay-outside-the-target rule this project already follows elsewhere) keyed by the supervisor's own runtime `swarm_name` — read via `swarm_identity_lib.bb`'s `own-swarm-name`, the live launch-time identity `swarmforge.sh` persists to `.swarmforge/swarm-identity`, never an ambient `SWARM_NAME` env var (which isn't even exported to child processes), defaulting `primary` per BL-090. The creds file wins WHOLESALE when present — never merged field-by-field with the environment, so a creds file can never let an inherited env token leak through a partially-present file — falling back to the environment entirely only when no file exists at all for that `swarm_name` (the mandatory primary-swarm compatibility path). `front_desk_supervisor.bb` now resolves creds through this helper: a non-primary swarm with a creds file uses ITS OWN token/chat/port regardless of what the environment exports; the primary swarm with no creds file present falls back to the existing env vars exactly as before, so the single-swarm setup is unchanged. `SWARMFORGE_FLEET_HOME` overrides the fleet root for tests, the project's established live-shared-path test seam — load-bearing here since `~/.swarmforge/fleet/` is genuinely populated with other fleet state on real hosts. `provision-onboarding-telegram-channel.js`'s CLI signature gains two new positional args, `<swarm-name>` (required) and `[bridge-port]` (optional, default `8765`) — documented in `docs/tutorials/Onboarding-New-Project.md`. `extension/src/onboarding/fleetTelegramCredsStore.ts` is the TypeScript-side writer, and `provision-onboarding-telegram-channel.ts` now persists a successful group-detection's `botToken`/`chatId`/`bridgePort` into that same per-swarm file instead of wherever it wrote before. Round-trip covered by both an example-based unit suite and a new property test (`fleetTelegramCredsStore.property.test.js`, `npm run test:properties`, per BL-479's new separate command) proving the store's read↔write is a genuine identity over a broad range of generated creds. No change to `getUpdates`/offset semantics (BL-380/BL-444) — only where the creds come from.

**A decided approval ask now survives Telegram rate-limiting: the real rejection reason is logged and a 429's `retry_after` is honoured with a bounded retry (BL-496).** Operator-verified, intermittent, batch-correlated post-ship gap in BL-484: approving a burst of asks left some (e.g. two of five in one observed batch) with live, re-tappable buttons and no verdict line, because the close-out edit silently failed against Telegram's live API with no visible reason. Root cause, verified in source: `telegramClient.ts`'s `callTelegramApi` already extracted a 429's `retryAfterSeconds`, but `editMessageText`'s `EditMessageTextResult` dropped it, returning only `{success, error}`; the bot wiring further discarded `error` (`editApprovalAskMessage: (...) => editMessageText(...).then(r => r.success)`), so `closeApprovalAskIfPossible` could log only a generic "message edit failed or not wired" line. `EditMessageTextResult` now carries `retryAfterSeconds`, the `editApprovalAskMessage` adapter widens from a bare `Promise<boolean>` to the full `Promise<EditMessageTextResult>`, and `closeApprovalAskIfPossible` logs the real Telegram rejection reason on any non-rate-limited failure. A rate-limited edit (`retryAfterSeconds` present) is retried by the new `editApprovalAskWithBoundedRateLimitRetry` loop, waiting exactly Telegram's own told-you-so `retry_after` between attempts — via an injected `waitForAskCloseRetry` seam (a real `setTimeout` wait in production, an instant-resolving double in tests, so the retry's timing is provable with no real clock) — up to a bounded `askCloseRetryBudget` (default 5, env/adapter-overridable for tests). Exhausting the budget logs the undelivered close loudly, naming the ticket and the last `retry_after`; a non-rate-limited rejection is logged once with its real reason and never retried. Neither path ever crashes the bot's poll loop, and the disk `human_approval` flip stays the single source of decision truth throughout — the message edit only ever mirrors it. The roster/pipeline-board edit-in-place adapters, which only read `.success`, are unaffected; the widened result is additive. Real-path acceptance now approves a burst of asks against a rate-limit-simulating Telegram double and asserts every one eventually closes. No new human-facing command; a Telegram approval-ask burst that previously left some asks stuck with live buttons under rate-limiting now always converges to closed, with the real rejection reason visible in `.swarmforge/operator/front-desk-supervisor.log` on a transient failure.

**A decided approval ask now closes itself: buttons stripped, verdict appended (BL-484).** Human-reported defect, 2026-07-17, with a screenshot of two already-decided asks (BL-479, BL-480) still showing live Approve/Amend/Reject buttons — BL-410's buttons flow recorded the decision on disk but never touched the posted message afterwards, so the topic looked like every ask was still open and a stale button stayed tappable forever. `approvalAskClosing.ts` is the new pure core: `composeDecidedAskText(originalText, verdict, nowMs)` appends a decision line below the original ask text (never replacing it, so the topic stays an audit trail) — `-- Approved <UTC timestamp>` for an approval, `-- Rejected: <reason>` for a rejection (`decisionLineFor`, timestamp from an injected `nowMs`, never a bare clock read) — and `alreadyDecidedToastText(verdict)` renders the stale-tap guard's toast text. `recordApprovalDecisionAndClose` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) is the ONE closing routine both decision entry points call — a callback-query button tap and a typed reply (a per-ticket-topic bare reply or the standing Approvals-topic `approve <id>`/`reject <id> <reason>` form) — so the two can never drift into different edited shapes: it records the decision through the existing `recordApprovalReply`/`recordRejectionReply` adapters (unchanged contract, never a second recording path) and, only on a real transition (`changed === true`, never on an already-decided or unknown ticket), edits the posted message via `closeApprovalAskIfPossible`. An `amend` reply is unaffected — it still only posts operator context and leaves the ticket pending, per the ticket's own scope. Wiring: `topicRouter.ts`'s `routeApprovalRequestedEvent` now calls a `sendApprovalAsk` adapter that reports the posted message's `message_id`, immediately persisted via `recordApprovalAskMessageId`; `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts` stores `{topicId, messageId, text}` per ticket in a new machine-local sidecar (`approvalAskMessagesPath`, same pattern as the roster/pipeline-board message-id state) and reads it back on close. `telegramClient.ts`'s `editMessageText` gains an explicit `buttons: null` strip (Telegram otherwise leaves an existing keyboard untouched on a text-only edit) and `answerCallbackQuery` gains an optional toast-text parameter — both additive, every existing call site unaffected. A tap on an already-decided ask is answered with the "Already decided: `<verdict>`" toast and performs no side effect, rather than re-entering the decision path (the escalation-resends-retracted-question failure class this ticket closes off). A failed message edit (e.g. the message was deleted) is logged to stderr but never blocks or unwinds the already-successful `human_approval` recording — the YAML flip stays the single source of decision truth, the message edit only mirrors it. **Architect pass, same ticket:** added `approvalAskClosing.property.test.js` (`npm run test:properties`, per BL-479's separate command) proving `composeDecidedAskText`'s original-text-prefix / decision-line-suffix contract holds over a broad generated range.

**Pipeline board: every ticket physically in `backlog/active/` gets a row — a not-yet-held ticket renders NOT-STARTED instead of vanishing (BL-473).** Human-requested directly, 2026-07-16: "show as active the BL ticket physically sitting in the active backlog folder ... at a minimum, the pipeline board should be as good as the PWA for displaying active tickets." Root gap (verified in code): the board's active rows were built only from the role-held map (`.swarmforge/board/ticket-stage-map.json` via `readRoleHeldTickets`), so a freshly-promoted ticket no role had dequeued yet — or one momentarily between two stages — produced no row and silently vanished, even though it physically sat in `backlog/active/`. `computePipelineBoard` (`pipelineBoard.ts`) gains an optional `activeIds` membership set: when supplied, it is the SOLE source of row membership — every id in it gets exactly one grid row (`buildGridRows`), with the role-held map only deciding that row's column, defaulting to a new sentinel column, `PIPELINE_BOARD_NOT_STARTED_COLUMN` (label `NS`), when no role currently holds it. That column is appended LAST in `PIPELINE_BOARD_COLUMN_ORDER` — the human's own stated preference for a dedicated "not started" column on the grid's right-hand side over a bare "?" marker. Omitting `activeIds` (every pre-existing call site) keeps rendering identically to before. `conciergeTick.ts`'s `syncBoardIfWired` wires physical `backlog/active/` membership (`folders.active`, read via the existing `folders` snapshot) into `activeIds` via `activeMembershipIds`. **Same-day bounce fix:** the first cut also defensively unioned `folders.active` with every currently role-held id, reasoning a role only ever holds a ticket the coordinator already promoted; that union let a ticket a role still reported holding — but that the coordinator had already moved out of `backlog/active/` (closed, or bounced off-pipeline) — keep rendering a stale active row, violating the ticket's own "and only those" acceptance clause (`board-active-membership-03`). `activeMembershipIds` now returns `folders.active`'s ids alone, never unioned with `roleHeldTickets`; a role-held id absent from `folders.active` gets no row at all. **Also folded in this same batch, no separate ticket:** `buildGridRows`' existing double-row guard (a ticket id seen under more than one role collapsing to its most-downstream role, BL-464) was split out into its own `heldRoleByTicketId` helper, behavior unchanged. No new human-facing command — the pipeline board's active-row count now always matches `ls backlog/active/*.yaml` one-for-one, and a not-started ticket a role then picks up moves to that role's column on the next tick, per the ticket's own E2E procedure.

**Pipeline board: role-held stage now recomputes live every tick instead of trusting the coordinator's cache (BL-487).** BL-474's stage-1 audit found the board's stage source, `.swarmforge/board/ticket-stage-map.json`, was a lazily-invalidated cache whose only invalidator was the coordinator LLM remembering to run `pipeline_stage_cli.bb sync` after every parcel move — no daemon/cron/tick recomputed it, so a skipped, crashed, cooldown'd, or simply forgotten sync left a genuinely-held ticket mis-staged (or absent from the board entirely) for an unbounded time; verified live, a 6-ticket `backlog/active/` had only 2 entries in the cache. Of the two candidate fixes the ticket left open — shell out to `pipeline_stage_cli.bb`'s existing side-effect-free `report` subcommand each tick, or reimplement the same reconciliation in TypeScript — the build took the shell-out path: it reuses `report`'s one canonical computation (note-aware header resolution across `task`/`message`, cross-role reconciliation, stale-id filtering) rather than duplicating that logic in a second language. `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts` gained `readLiveRoleHeldTickets`, and `conciergeTick.ts`'s `syncBoardIfWired` now awaits it instead of reading the cache synchronously. The coordinator's `sync` call is unchanged and keeps running — it is now a cache-warm for other consumers of the file, never the board's source of truth, so a skipped or stale `sync` can no longer durably mis-stage a held ticket. No new human-facing command; the existing "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now reflects live mailbox state on every tick regardless of coordinator bookkeeping.

**Pipeline board and dispatch-gap sweep: a held ticket's id resolves even when a handoff header doesn't lead with it (BL-488).** BL-474's audit finding #3: `pipeline_stage_lib.bb`'s `extract-ticket-id` anchored on the id being the FIRST token of a `git_handoff`'s `task` header or a `note`'s `message` header (`^([A-Za-z]+-\d+)`), so a header carrying any textual prefix before the id — "Re: BL-476 …", "continuing BL-476 next slice" — matched nothing and resolved to nil, reading as a durable false NOT-STARTED on the board even though the ticket was genuinely held. The extractor now resolves the FIRST ticket-id-shaped token anywhere in the header (deterministic first-id-wins, still upper-cased per BL-471), byte-identical on an already-leading id and strictly more permissive otherwise — a header with no id-shaped token still resolves to nothing, so no false positive is introduced. A second gap surfaced fixing the first: a bare `[A-Za-z]+` prefix has no word-boundary against a glued stray letter ("ABL-476" swallowed as if "ABL" were the ticket's own prefix), so both `pipeline_stage_lib.bb` and its independently-duplicated sibling `chase_sweep_lib.bb` (the BL-217/BL-222 dispatch-gap sweep's own id extractor) now match against a closed `known-ticket-prefixes` allowlist (`BL`, `GH`) instead of an unbounded letter run. No new human-facing command; the pipeline board and the dispatch-gap sweep both now resolve a held/dispatched ticket's id correctly regardless of where in the header it sits or what's glued in front of it.

**Pipeline board: a mis-cased `backlog/active/` yaml id can no longer silently drop a held ticket (BL-489).** BL-474 audit follow-up F-3 (finding #4): `pipeline_stage_cli.bb`'s `active-ticket-ids` read each `backlog/active/*.yaml`'s `id:` field verbatim, while the stage-map side (`extract-ticket-id`, upper-cased per BL-471 above) canonicalizes every id it extracts to upper-case — so `filter-active`'s exact-case set membership test would silently drop a ticket whose yaml `id:` was written mis-cased (`bl-490`/`Bl-490`) from the board entirely, with no error. `active-ticket-ids` now upper-cases each yaml id it reads before building the active set, matching the stage-map side's own canonicalization. Latent today (production ids are conventionally upper-case) but a total, silent drop when it does hit. No new human-facing command; the pipeline board now resolves a held active ticket regardless of the letter-case of its `backlog/active/` yaml `id:` field.

**The Telegram approval ask gains a fourth "Expedite" button: approve + force-promote + dispatch now, bypassing the coordinator's sequencing triage (BL-490).** Human-requested 2026-07-17 (the human had to hand-drive an equivalent promote+dispatch note through the coordinator earlier that session). Alongside the existing Approve/Amend/Reject buttons (BL-410), the ask now renders a fourth `expedite:<id>` button through the same callback round-trip — never a second callback path. Tapping it runs three ordered effects: (a) **approve** — routes through the same `recordApprovalReply` effect a plain Approve tap already uses, so approval has one source of truth; (b) **promote** — a new `backlogWriter.promoteToActive` mover (mirroring `markDone`'s `fs.rename` pattern) moves a `paused/` ticket into `active/`, or no-ops if the ticket is already active; (c) **dispatch** — shells out to the existing `route_backlog_to_coder.sh` injector to post a routing handoff immediately, bypassing the coordinator's orthogonality/sequencing triage the human explicitly opted to skip. Before dispatching, `expediteSafety.ts`'s pure `findFileCollision` checks whether an in-flight ticket's touched-file set (extracted from ticket text via `extractScopePaths`) overlaps the expedited ticket's own scope; on a collision the ticket is still approved and promoted but NOT dispatched — the human sees an "unsafe — queued behind in-flight `<id>` (same file), not preempted" toast instead, per the project's existing "an in-flight coder task cannot be preempted" precedent. An Expedite tap folds into BL-484's one closing routine (buttons stripped, `-- Expedited <UTC>` appended) and is guarded by the same stale-ask check as the other three verbs (a tap on an already-decided ask is a no-op toast, no side effect). New human-facing surface: the approval ask in Telegram now shows four buttons instead of three, and tapping Expedite jumps a paused ticket straight to build without waiting for the coordinator's normal promotion cycle. **QA bounce fix, same ticket (BL-490-VIOLATION):** the first cut's approve+promote writes were plain uncommitted `fs` mutations against the shared master checkout — exactly the dangling-working-tree-edit hazard the spec itself flagged and deferred, one `git reset`/checkout away from silent loss, with a build able to dispatch against a promotion that never durably landed. `commitExpediteWrites` (`telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`) now durably commits the ticket's current file (`backlogWriter.findBacklogFilePath`, checked active-then-paused) through the shared, locked `commit_integrity_cli.bb` (BL-419) — never a hand-typed git add/commit — consulted after promote and before dispatch, so a build never starts against an uncommitted promotion; a commit failure degrades to `false` rather than throwing, same as this file's other optional adapters. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** split `decideCallbackQueryAction` and `dispatchRecognizedCallbackDecision` (each pushed over the CRAP threshold by the new `expedite` branch) into named helpers, and added coverage for a multi-candidate file-collision search.

**A one-time reconcile CLI closes every legacy per-ticket Telegram topic now that epic/Backlog routing has replaced them (BL-494, migration slice of the topic-consolidation epic, depends on BL-493).** Before BL-492/493, every ticket minted its own Telegram topic; that model is retired, leaving hundreds of now-legacy per-ticket topics in the live group with nothing routing into them anymore. `close-legacy-ticket-topics.ts` is a **hand-run operator CLI** (deliberately not an automatic sweep — a mass close over a live group should not fire unattended) that reads `backlog-topic-map.json`, selects per-ticket entries via `legacyTopicReconcile.ts`'s `selectLegacyPerTicketTopics` — a positive `BL-###`-shaped allowlist, so epic topic ids and the reserved Backlog topic key are excluded by construction, never an enumerated exclusion list — and calls Telegram's `closeForumTopic` (via a new `closeForumTopicWithRateLimitRetry` in `telegramClient.ts`, the same 429/`retry_after`-honoring mechanism `backfill-topic-icons.ts` already uses) on each one. `closeForumTopic` collapses a topic to read-only and **preserves its history**; it is never deleted. A ticket's map entry is dropped only on a confirmed close, so a re-run is a safe no-op for already-closed topics and a genuine failure is simply retried on the next run rather than silently lost. Usage: `node close-legacy-ticket-topics.js <target-repo-path>` (reads `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`/`TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` from the environment). New human-facing surface: running this CLI once against the live front-desk group closes every legacy per-ticket topic (read-only, history intact) while leaving epic topics, the standing Backlog topic, and other standing topics untouched; recreating topics minted before this shipped and any repair path are explicitly out of scope here (follow-up BL-495).

**Pipeline board and dispatch-gap sweep: both `.bb` ticket-id extractors make the prefix hyphen optional (BL-503).** Live daemon defect surfaced by the coordinator's 2026-07-17 `rule_proposal`: `pipeline_stage_lib.bb`'s `ticket-id-pattern` and `chase_sweep_lib.bb`'s `leading-ticket-id-pattern` both required a hyphen between the `(BL|GH)` prefix and the digits, but ~14 in-flight coder tickets — including the then-active BL-493 — were minted with the no-hyphen task-header form (`bl493-fold-ticket-events`), so `extract-ticket-id` returned nil for them: BL-493 silently dropped off the pipeline board (the live sync showed only BL-502) and the dispatch-gap sweep, seeing no trail, was about to falsely auto-route it to the coordinator as a spurious gap. The hyphen is now optional (`-?`) in both extractors' patterns, and `chase_sweep_lib.bb`'s `extract-ticket-id` — which previously returned its match raw, un-canonicalized — now upper-cases and re-hyphenates every match to the canonical `BL-NNN`/`GH-NNN` form like `pipeline_stage_lib.bb` already did per BL-471, so a lower-case hyphenated match (`bl-493`) no longer silently fails the case-sensitive active-id join either. The `(BL|GH)` allowlist and glued-prefix guards (BL-217/BL-222/BL-488) are unchanged — `ABL-217` and `usable493` still resolve to nil. No new human-facing command; the pipeline board and dispatch-gap sweep now resolve a no-hyphen-tasked ticket correctly instead of silently dropping/false-flagging it.

**TS metrics: the shared `extractTicketId` no longer drops no-hyphen ticket names or over-matches non-tickets (BL-504).** Sibling of the `.bb` extractors' BL-217/BL-222/BL-488 allowlist fixes (this is the extension-host TS side, a different subsystem, filed separately by the coordinator's 2026-07-17 `rule_proposal`). `swarmMetrics.ts`'s exported `extractTicketId` — shared by `stageDwell.ts`, `ticketHoldingWindows.ts`, `reworkObservatorySource.ts`, and `swarmState.ts` — previously matched `/^([A-Za-z]+-\d+)/`: an unbounded letter-run prefix that both required a hyphen (so a no-hyphen task header like `bl493-fold-ticket-events` resolved to nothing and the ticket vanished from stage-dwell / holding-window / rework metrics) and over-matched any non-ticket word-prefix (`usable-493-x` resolved to `usable-493`, `ABL-217-x` to `ABL-217` — the exact id-swallowing the `.bb` allowlist was introduced to prevent, never adopted here). It now uses `/^(BL|GH)-?(\d+)/i`: a closed `(BL|GH)` prefix allowlist (closing the over-match), an optional hyphen (closing the no-hyphen drop), and canonicalizes every match to upper-case hyphenated `BL-NNN`/`GH-NNN` regardless of the input's case or hyphenation, so downstream keys/joins agree. `gitHistoryAdapter.ts`'s own separate `extractTicketId(filePath)` over canonical backlog file paths is a different function and was not touched. No new human-facing command; derived metrics (stage-dwell, ticket holding windows, rework observatory) now include a no-hyphen-task ticket that was previously silently omitted, and no longer inject a bogus row for a non-`(BL|GH)` task-name prefix.

**Operator reacts out-of-cycle to a fresh inbound Telegram message (BL-481).** Human-requested, 2026-07-17, from a live incident: a Concierge-topic question felt unanswered for an extended window. Root cause (verified against real code, not assumed): `operator_runtime.bb`'s `-main` loop ran `tick!` then unconditionally slept a full `OPERATOR_INTERVAL_MS` (default 30s) before the next tick, so a Telegram message landing just after a tick sat unread in `events.jsonl` for up to a whole interval before the Operator was even launched to answer it — a fixed polling tax on top of the LLM's own reasoning time. The expensive full health sweep was already gated to its own `OPERATOR_SWARM_CHECK_MS` cadence (default 30m) via `timer-due?`, not run every tick, so the fix decouples event-dispatch latency from that sweep bundle's cadence rather than touching it. `-main`'s loop now wakes every short, bounded, env-overridable `OPERATOR_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (default 3000ms, floored at 1000ms by `resolve-poll-interval-ms` so a missing/zero/negative value can never busy-spin) instead of the full interval: on each wake it runs the full `tick!` only when `interval-ms` is actually due (the same `timer-due?` gate swarm-check already used, tracked via a process-local `last-full-tick-ms` — never persisted, so a restart simply runs one full tick immediately, exactly the pre-existing startup behavior), otherwise it runs the new cheap `poll!` — event-detection plus a launch decision only (`operator_lib.bb`'s `next-poll-decision`, built on the same `should-launch-operator?`/`should-launch-front-desk-operator?` gates a full tick uses, so a fast wake never launches under looser rules than a full tick would). A fast poll's launch decision reads a cheap `cached-provider-state` (the persisted cooldown record only, no live tmux pane capture) rather than the full tick's live pane scan — sufficient for the launch guard, at the cost of not detecting a brand-new usage-limit banner with no prior cooldown record until the next full tick. `operator_runtime.bb <project-root> --poll-once` is a new CLI mode (alongside the existing `--tick-once`) for running a single out-of-cycle poll. No new human-facing command or config beyond the env var; the effect is a Telegram reply that starts within a few seconds of a message arriving instead of up to ~30s later, with the periodic health sweep still firing at most once per its own cadence regardless of how often the faster poll wakes.

**A standing "Backlog" catch-all Telegram topic is now ensured once at boot — the epic-consolidation epic's foundation slice (BL-492, epic `topic-consolidation`/BL-491).** Most tickets carry no `epic` (`epic: ""`), so they had no shared standing topic to route into and were heading toward a per-ticket topic each — the topic-consolidation epic's premise is one catch-all instead. `ensureBacklogTopic` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) is an exact twin of the existing `ensureApprovalsTopic`/`ensureRecertTopic`/`ensureAgentQuestionsTopic`: reuse-or-create against a new reserved subject id (`BACKLOG_SUBJECT_ID`, topic name "Backlog"), verified not to collide with any existing reserved id (`OPERATOR`/`APPROVALS`/`RECERT`/`AGENT_QUESTIONS`/`CONTROL`). Called once at boot in `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts` alongside the other `ensure*Topic` calls, before any loop starts polling — the same ordering every sibling standing topic already follows. This slice only ensures the topic exists; nothing routes ticket events into it yet (that is BL-493), and no icon is assigned to it in this slice. Existing standing topics and the per-role STEERING topics are untouched — verified by acceptance driving the real compiled `ensureBacklogTopic` against a fixture for create-when-absent, reuse-when-present, and non-disturbance. New human-facing surface: a "Backlog" topic now appears in the front-desk group on first boot after this lands, currently empty (routing lands in a follow-up ticket).

**The pipeline board is now the ONLY pinned message in the Telegram group, continuously enforced (BL-467).** Human-requested via the Operator front desk 2026-07-16 ("at the moment, I only want the pipeline board to be pinned"), with a specifier clarifying round settling the enforcement posture: continuous, every concierge tick, including unpinning a message a human pins by hand later — the literal reading of "nothing else should be pinned" — until the human asks to disable it. Telegram pins are CHAT-level (`pinChatMessage` takes no `message_thread_id`), which matches "pinned in the group" directly even though the board message physically lives in the dedicated "Pipeline Board" topic. Three thin Bot API wrappers land in `telegramClient.ts` — `pinChatMessage` (always `disable_notification: true`, so a re-pin never alerts the group), `unpinAllChatMessages`, and `getChatPinnedMessageId` (extracts `pinned_message.message_id` off a `getChat` response, `undefined` when nothing is pinned). A new pure module, `pipelineBoardPinSync.ts`, mirrors `pipelineBoardSync.ts`'s shape: `decidePipelineBoardPinAction(currentTopPinnedId, boardMessageId)` returns `skip-no-board` (board not posted yet), `skip-clean` (the board is already the top pin — the change-gate that keeps an unchanged tick a complete no-op, no API calls at all), or `enforce` (anything else, including nothing pinned or a human's hand-pin); `syncPipelineBoardPin` reads the current top pin fresh on every call (never cached) and, only on `enforce`, unpins everything then pins the board — one unpin-all plus one pin, not a per-topic fan-out, so BL-342's rate-limit backfill-storm concern doesn't apply here. Wired into `conciergeTick.ts`'s `syncPinIfWired`, which runs after `syncBoardIfWired` so it always sees the freshly-reposted board's message id, and is a no-op when the optional `pinAdapters` aren't wired — same absent-adapter posture as the board sync itself. `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts` builds the live adapters over the three new wrappers alongside the existing `boardAdapters` block. Like the board's own `deleteMessage` adapter, every pin/unpin/getChat call is best-effort: a failure is never branched on, never throws, never aborts the tick. No new human-facing command; the "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic's message is now the sole pinned message in the group, re-enforced every tick even against a human hand-pinning something else.

**Live outage fix: the pipeline board no longer retries a dead topic forever in silence — it surfaces the swallowed Telegram error, self-heals a gone topic, and raises exactly one operator alert after a bounded number of failures (BL-497).** The board message went unchanged for 10+ hours in production; the Approvals roster kept updating on the same bot/chat/API path in the same window, which isolated the fault to the board's own post path. Root cause: `boardAdapters.postMessage`/`ensureBoardTopic` (`telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`) mapped a failed Telegram call to a bare `undefined`, discarding the underlying error string entirely, and `syncBoardIfWired` (`conciergeTick.ts`) discarded `result.outcome` too — so a dead board topic reposted, failed, and said nothing, tick after tick, forever. Fix, scoped to the post path only (the render/content-signature change-gate contract from BL-462/464/465/468/473 is untouched): `PipelineBoardAdapters.ensureBoardTopic`/`postMessage` are widened from `Promise<number | undefined>` to `Promise<{ topicId?/messageId?; error? }>`, carrying the real Telegram error up; `syncBoardIfWired` now logs every failed outcome's `error`/`failureClass` to stderr instead of discarding it. `classifyBoardFailure` (`pipelineBoardSync.ts`) is a pure function over an explicit signature lookup (never a bare substring branch, per the acceptance-mutation rule) sorting an error into `topic-gone` (`"message thread not found"`), `transient` (429/`retry after`/`ENOTFOUND`/5xx-class strings), or `unknown` — a `topic-gone` failed post clears the tracked `topicId`/`messageId` so the next tick's `resolveBoardTopicId` re-ensures a genuinely fresh topic and posts into it (self-heal, no human intervention); `transient` and `unknown` both retain the topic and never recreate it, so a blip can never spawn a duplicate "Pipeline Board" topic (the ticket's own conservative choice for the unclassifiable case). `PipelineBoardState` gains `consecutiveFailures`/`alertArmed`, persisted across ticks; after `PIPELINE_BOARD_ALERT_FAILURE_CAP` (5) consecutive failed ticks, `syncPipelineBoard` calls the new optional `emitFailureAlert` adapter exactly once, naming the failure count and last error — wired to `emitPipelineBoardFailureAlert`, which reuses the existing Operator topic (no new alert channel). Armed only on the adapter's CONFIRMED delivery, never on the mere attempt (the BL-215/BL-333 "never arm on the attempt" rule): a failed or unwired alert leaves the state untouched so the very next failing tick tries again rather than suppressing it. A single successful post clears `consecutiveFailures` and `alertArmed` back to zero/false, so a later episode alarms fresh. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** extracted the two `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts` adapter closures (`ensureBoardTopicAdapter`, `emitPipelineBoardFailureAlert`) into named exports so a unit test can drive their success/failure branches directly, bringing CRAP back under the article's gate and documenting one equivalent Gherkin mutant. No new human-facing command; a dead "Pipeline Board" topic now recovers on its own within a few ticks instead of freezing silently, and the Operator topic receives one alert naming the frozen board if it can't.

**Live outage fix: the pipeline board's tappable link list is now budgeted to Telegram's send limit, so the board posts at any backlog size instead of freezing on an oversized message (BL-502).** Follow-on to BL-497, which made the failure visible for the first time by logging the real rejection instead of swallowing it: `Telegram API responded with status 400: Bad Request: text is too long`. Root cause, verified against the live build: BL-465's tappable GitHub link list (`renderPipelineBoardLinks`) has no length budget — one `<a href>` line per grid/parked/awaiting-approval/paused/root-intake/recently-closed entry, ~150-190 chars each — so for only 16 linkable entries the composed board message (grid/parked body + link block) already exceeds Telegram's 4096-char `sendMessage` limit, and every post is rejected. Unlike a transient failure, retrying the identical oversized payload never succeeds; the payload itself has to shrink. Fix: a new exported constant, `PIPELINE_BOARD_MESSAGE_MAX_LENGTH` (4000, a safety margin below Telegram's 4096 absorbing `escapeHtml`'s entity expansion), and a new pure function, `budgetPipelineBoardLinks` (`pipelineBoard.ts`), that composes the link block against whatever space remains after the fixed grid/parked body (always included in full — it is small and bounded by backlog size). When the full link list fits, rendering is byte-identical to before (`omittedCount` 0, the common case). When it doesn't, links are trimmed in list order to the largest prefix that still leaves room for a visible `+N more` line naming exactly how many were dropped — never a silent cap, mirroring `PIPELINE_BOARD_RECENTLY_CLOSED_MAX`'s own bounded-list posture. `pipelineBoardSync.ts`'s `syncPipelineBoard` computes the remaining budget from the wrapped grid/parked body's own length before calling `budgetPipelineBoardLinks`, so the composed message `postBoardMessage` actually sends is always within budget. Defense in depth: `classifyBoardFailure` gains a `too-long` class (`"text is too long"`, an explicit signature per the acceptance-mutation rule, not a bare substring branch) distinct from `topic-gone`/`transient`/`unknown`, so if a payload is ever still over the limit the failure is labelled correctly instead of lumped under "unknown" — and, since the topic itself is fine and only the payload was too big, a `too-long` failure retains the tracked topic exactly like `transient`/`unknown` do, never recreating it. No render, change-gate, or failure-recovery contract from BL-462/464/465/468/473/497 changes otherwise. No new human-facing command; the "Pipeline Board" Telegram topic now posts successfully at any backlog size, showing a "+N more" line under the link list only when the list had to be trimmed to fit.

**Silent daemon defect fixed: the chase sweep no longer re-chases a `new/` handoff forever once it is already resolved in `completed/` (BL-499).** Coordinator-observed live, 2026-07-17: a stale duplicate handoff sitting in a role's `inbox/new/` — the exact already-terminal residue the dequeue path's BL-218 skip already knows to ignore — kept getting chased by `handoffd.bb`'s chase sweep with exponential backoff and no cap, waking an active recipient every cycle indefinitely (`chaseCount` reached 12+ in one observed session), because `chase_sweep_lib.bb`'s `scan-inbox-new` enumerated every file in `new/` with no dedup against `completed/`/`abandoned/`, and its per-item decision only ever dead-lettered a stuck item when the recipient was IDLE — an active recipient's stale duplicate had no exit and no visibility (no alert, no dead-letter, just an endless silent wake-up). Fix: the chase sweep now applies the SAME already-terminal check (`handoff_lib.bb`'s existing `already-terminal?`/`dedup-new-candidates`, reused rather than duplicated) before deciding a `new/` item's fate. A handoff whose id is already terminal in `completed/` or `abandoned/` is now REAPED, not chased and not dead-lettered: no wake-up is sent, `chaseCount` is not incremented, the stale duplicate (and its orphaned `.chase.json` sidecar) is removed from `new/` entirely, and a logged "already-processed" line plus a chase-telemetry reap event record the event audibly — this precedence holds regardless of the recipient's liveness, so an idle recipient's already-resolved duplicate is reaped rather than raising a false dead-letter alarm either. A genuinely stuck, not-yet-terminal handoff is chased (active recipient) or dead-lettered (idle recipient, `maxChases` exhausted) exactly as before — scope is strictly the already-resolved-duplicate case. No new human-facing command or config; a role that previously kept getting woken for mail its own intake would forever skip now sees that duplicate disappear silently (but auditably) instead.

**A ticket's swarm events now fold into its epic's topic (or the standing Backlog topic) as one edit-in-place status message — per-ticket topics are no longer minted (BL-493, the wiring slice of the BL-491 topic-consolidation epic, depends on BL-492's standing Backlog topic).** Before this ticket, every ticket event (`routeTaggedOrUntaggedEvent` → `decideTopicAction`) created a brand-new "BL-### - Title" forum topic per ticket, which is exactly the topic sprawl the topic-consolidation epic exists to end. Now the ticket's own `epic` field (`BacklogItem.epic`, read straight off the backlog — never inferred from `notes:` prose, mirroring BL-341's epic-membership rule) decides the target: a non-empty `epic` routes to that epic's topic (created via the existing `decideEpicTopicAction`/`postEpicAction` path if it doesn't exist yet), an empty `epic` routes to the standing Backlog topic (BL-492). Two new pure "testable seam" modules do the deciding: `ticketStatusMessage.ts`'s `resolveTicketStatusTarget` (epic id or Backlog) and `buildTicketStatusText` (`"BL-### <glyph> <state> — <title>"`, reusing `topicIcon.ts`'s existing `ICON_EMOJI` glyphs — done ✅ / in progress 🎵🦠 / paused/awaiting-approval 🔍 — now carried in the message text itself since there is no longer a per-ticket topic icon to hold that state), and `ticketMessageMapStore.ts`, a new machine-local store (`.swarmforge/operator/ticket-message-map.json`, gitignored like the other operator maps) keyed ticket-id → `{topicId, messageId}`.
