On a ticket's first event a status message posts and its identity is recorded; every later lifecycle transition reuses that identity to edit the SAME message in place via the existing `syncEditInPlaceMessage` (never a new message per transition). The per-ticket-topic-for-icon machinery (`ensurePerTicketTopicForIcon`, `routeTaggedOrUntaggedEvent`, `routeCompletionEvent`) is fully removed — an `ApprovalRequested` event now surfaces solely via the standing Approvals topic (BL-434), no throwaway per-ticket topic minted just to carry a 👀 icon. **Same-ticket fix (architect bounce):** `topicReconciliation.ts`'s `reconcileTopicLifecycle` originally built its route context with `epicTitle: ticket.epic` — the epic's raw id, not its human title — so a reconciled epic topic could be misnamed; fixed to resolve the title through the same `epicDefinitionsFor`/`epicTitleFor` lookup `conciergeTick.ts`'s live-tick path already used, falling back to the id only when the epic is genuinely undocumented. **Same-ticket fix (existing legacy-topic-deletion sweep):** `topicDeletion.ts`'s retention gate, which age-outs a ticket's now-legacy per-ticket topic once its completion is verified, matched against the old `completionSummaryText` format; it now matches against `buildTicketStatusText(id, title, 'done')` — the same text the new mechanism records — so a topic created before this ticket shipped remains eligible for cleanup under the new format. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** pinned the retention gate's completion match to require BOTH the message's `type === 'outbound'` AND its text equalling the completion text together (never a decoy matching only one half), and pinned reconciliation's "already reconciled" check to the ticket's actual done-state text plus its post's delivery result, so a post that fails to deliver is never counted as reconciled. Out of scope for this ticket: closing topics minted before this ticket shipped (BL-494) and the recreation repair path (BL-495). New human-facing surface: a ticket's lifecycle now shows as a single message inside its epic's topic (or the Backlog topic) that updates in place — e.g. "BL-493 🎵 in progress — Title" edited to "BL-493 ✅ done — Title" — instead of a new topic being created per ticket.

**The Pipeline Board's grid and below-grid lists are narrower, and the not-started column now leads instead of trails (BL-505).** Human-requested 2026-07-17, from the root-intake queue: looking at a live board render on a phone, the grid plus its PARKED/AWAITING APPROVAL/ROOT INTAKE/RECENTLY CLOSED list lines were too wide to fit without horizontal scroll. `pipelineBoard.ts`'s grid TICKET column now shows the ticket NUMBER only — a recognised `BL-`/`GH-` prefix is stripped (`BL-493` → `493`); an id with no recognised ticket prefix (e.g. a root-intake filename stem) is shown unchanged — and its header shortens from "TICKET" to "ID" so the column floors no wider than the numbers it holds. `deriveKebabSlug`'s cap drops from 3 kebab words to 2 for the grid slug. The below-grid list lines drop their wide truncated-title tail (`deriveTicketSlug`, now dead code, removed by the cleaner) and show only the short kebab slug, with ids rendered number-only the same way the grid's are. A same-day human follow-up moved the not-started (NS) sentinel column to lead the stage columns (`PIPELINE_BOARD_COLUMN_ORDER`) instead of trailing them — reversing BL-473's "right-hand side" placement, which that ticket had already declared a cosmetic, non-gating detail. This ticket supersedes BL-462/BL-465's wider-slug/full-title-tail scenarios (retired rather than reworded, per the specifier's own superseded-scenario convention) and reconciles every id/slug/width assertion across the pipeline-board acceptance step handlers and unit tests that assumed the old raw-prefixed id or 3-word/full-title rendering. The LINKS section is unchanged (its width is BL-502's concern, its ordering BL-506's). **Architect pass, same ticket:** added property-based coverage for `deriveKebabSlug`/the new display-id helper. New human-facing surface: the Pipeline Board's grid shows bare ticket numbers with a narrower "ID" column and a 2-word slug, its list sections show kebab-only entries, and the not-started column now appears first among the stage columns.

**Tapping the Approvals card's Amend button now actually steers the ticket: it prompts for the change, marks the ticket `amending`, and queues the steer for the specifier — closing the loop BL-410's Amend button only stubbed (BL-509 EPIC, slice 1 of 3).** Human-requested 2026-07-17: "when asked to approve a ticket, the amend button should enable me to steer the ticket." Before this slice, Amend did almost nothing: a tap silently stashed a pending-button marker with no prompt to the human (despite BL-410's own title claiming otherwise), the human's next reply was filed as an operator-context note while `human_approval` stayed `pending`, and the one live consumer of that note (`operator_runtime.bb`'s `bl-topic-approval-sweep!`) treated the text as an APPROVAL ANSWER rather than a steer — the specifier never saw it. This slice makes Amend prompt for real: tapping it now sends `"What would you like to change about <id>?"` (`amendPromptText`, `telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`), and the human's reply is handled by a new `recordAmendDecisionAndClose` routine — a sibling of the existing approve/reject closing routines — that (1) flips the ticket's `human_approval` to the new `amending` value via `recordAmendReply` (`pendingApprovalReply.ts`), a distinct non-terminal state (added to the schema enum, `swarmforge/backlog-schema.md`) rather than `pending`/`approved`/`rejected`; (2) closes the approval ask (buttons stripped, per BL-484's existing closing contract) since `amending` is no longer `pending`; (3) resets the ticket's `ApprovalRequested` emitted-state (`resetApprovalAskEmittedState`) so a later slice's `amending` → `pending` re-present re-fires the ask instead of being silently suppressed as already-emitted (the BL-357/BL-496 emittedKeys concern); and (4) queues a **distinct** `TELEGRAM_BL_AMEND_STEER` event (`queueAmendSteerDirective`, `telegram-front-desk-bot.ts`) — deliberately a different event type from the existing `TELEGRAM_BL_TOPIC_MESSAGE` the approval-answer sweep consumes, so a later slice can route it to the specifier instead of it being misread as an approval reply. **This slice supersedes BL-409/BL-410's original Amend contract** ("amend posts a note without changing approval state") — revised in the same parcel per BL-233 (a feature edit without its matching step change breaks the acceptance runner): `specs/features/BL-409-approve-reject-amend-verbs-from-telegram.feature` and `specs/features/BL-410-approval-inline-keyboard-buttons.feature` (plus their step handlers and `telegramFrontDeskBotCore.test.js`/`pendingApprovalReply.test.js`) now reflect the prompt-and-steer behavior instead of the old no-op-on-state text. Out of scope for this slice, tracked as its own follow-on work (parked in `BL-509-amend-button-steers-ticket.slices-2-3-wiring-loop.feature.draft`): the daemon actually delivering the queued steer to the specifier's mailbox (slice 2), and the specifier revising the ticket per the steer and re-presenting it for approval (slice 3) — until those land, a ticket that goes `amending` has nothing yet acting on it. New human-facing surface: tapping Amend on an Approvals-topic ticket now asks what to change, and the ticket's approval card closes and shows `amending` instead of staying silently `pending`.

**The Pipeline Board's LINKS section now lists the most-recent tickets first, numeric-aware (BL-506).** Human root-intake follow-up 2026-07-17 to BL-505: "the ordering of the yaml links has to go from most recent." `buildLinks` (`pipelineBoard.ts`) previously sorted every link — across all four sources (active rows, parked, recently-closed, root-intake) — by id STRING ascending, so the section always led with `BL-001`. The human confirmed "most recent" means highest ticket NUMBER first, not a real chronological sort: the merged link sources carry only `{id, path}`, no closed-at/created-at timestamp, so true recency would need extra plumbing the human chose to skip in favor of the id-based proxy. A new pure comparator, `compareLinksMostRecentFirst`, orders links by ticket number descending; ticket numbers are extracted with the same anchored `TICKET_ID_PREFIX_PATTERN` `deriveDisplayTicketId` already uses (not a generic trailing-digit regex), so a root-intake filename stem that happens to end in an embedded timestamp digit string is never misread as a ticket number. The comparator is numeric, not lexicographic, so `BL-1000` sorts above `BL-999` — the exact boundary a plain string sort gets wrong, and one a live root-intake doc already referenced. An id with no parseable ticket number (a root-intake stem) sorts after every numbered link, tie-broken by plain id order for a render that stays deterministic tick-over-tick (the board's own content-signature change-gate depends on it). Only the LINKS ordering changes: the grid, the below-grid lists, the link text/format, and BL-502's link-budget/"+N more" overflow behavior are unchanged — with most-recent-first, the budget now trims the OLDEST links first, which is the desirable direction. **Architect pass, same ticket:** added property-based coverage for `compareLinksMostRecentFirst`. New human-facing surface: the Pipeline Board's LINKS section now leads with the highest-numbered ticket instead of `BL-001`.

**The Pipeline Board grid drops its Coordinator ("CD") column; a ticket briefly held by the coordinator now marks the QA column instead (BL-507).** Human-requested directly to the specifier 2026-07-17: "take the Coordinator column out." The coordinator is not a forward parcel stage — it does post-QA backlog bookkeeping only (`PIPELINE.md`; constitution BL-247) — so its column never belonged among the pipeline-stage columns the grid shows. `PIPELINE_BOARD_COLUMN_ORDER` (`pipelineBoard.ts`) is now built from the forward `PIPELINE_CHAIN` (`specifier..QA`, imported from `rolePack.ts`) plus the not-started sentinel, instead of `ALL_SWARM_ROLES`; `ALL_SWARM_ROLES` itself is untouched, since it still legitimately drives the coordinator's own standing steering topic (`roleTopicMapStore.ts`, BL-425). The specifier asked the human one clarifying question — where a coordinator-held active ticket (the brief post-QA window after QA has landed the commit but before the coordinator has moved the file to `backlog/done/`) should render once its column is gone — and the human chose "mark it under QA," reading as end-of-line rather than blank or not-started. `buildGridRows` now remaps a coordinator-held row's stage to `'QA'` before rendering it: `heldRoleByTicketId` still iterates `ALL_SWARM_ROLES` unchanged and so still resolves such a ticket to `'coordinator'`, which the grid no longer has a column for — left unremapped it would render as an all-dots row with no `X` at all. Everything else is unchanged: a held ticket still marks exactly its own stage (BL-452), a not-started ticket still marks only NS (BL-473), row membership is still exactly `backlog/active/` (BL-473), and the below-grid lists and LINKS section are untouched. **Cleaner pass, same ticket:** removed the now-dead `COLUMN_LABEL['coordinator']` entry. **Architect pass, same ticket:** added property-based coverage generalizing the coordinator-held remap across every `ALL_SWARM_ROLES` role, confirmed non-vacuous by temporarily removing the remap and observing the `role=coordinator` case fail. New human-facing surface: the Pipeline Board grid no longer shows a Coordinator column, and a ticket in the brief post-QA bookkeeping window now marks QA instead of CD.

**The front-desk bot's degraded warning names its cause, and a sustained poll or relay outage escalates to the human once per episode (BL-621).** Two defects, one theme: sustained degradation was silent. During the 2026-07-24 token-theft incident, 9 hours of "poll degraded — 5 consecutive failures, still retrying" hid a 409 Conflict that names a rival poller in one line, because `pollAndForward` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) already received `getUpdates`' own fully-formatted transport error and threw it away before the degraded-warning line (`applyPollCycleResult`) ever saw it — the reply-relay twin's warning already interpolated its own error, making the poll path the asymmetric one. `PollResult` now carries the error and `PollCycleResult` surfaces it through to the warning, both funneled through a shared `describeOutageCause` so neither line can ever print "undefined". Separately, nothing escalated a sustained outage at all: the poll heartbeat deliberately stamps on failed cycles (BL-370's "handled failure counts as liveness"), so a permanently-failing loop reads healthy to the supervisor, and the reply-relay's `for(;;)` retry-forever loop (60s-capped backoff) logged one stderr line per streak with no escalate arm — BL-320 stated "retry forever, capped backoff, escalate — never silently" in prose but shipped no escalation, and BL-302 explicitly excluded this loop. `decideSustainedOutage` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`) is the new episode state machine: it opens on a loop's first failure, escalates exactly ONCE once the outage has run continuously past a configurable threshold, and closes on the next success, so a later outage is a new episode with its own single escalation — a pure function of `(episode state, ok, injected clock, threshold)`, with the clock arriving as a plain number so no test depends on wall time. Both the poll and reply-relay loops now carry an episode plus an escalate adapter wired to the same direct-Telegram-send channel `escalateStuckDelivery` (BL-369) already uses — still reachable while `getUpdates` itself is 409-ing, because sending a message does not poll. `formatSustainedOutageEscalation` composes the alert text (which loop, how long it has been down via `swarmMetrics.ts`'s existing `formatDurationMs`, and the last error via the same `describeOutageCause`). The threshold is the new conf key `front_desk_sustained_outage_minutes` (default 30 minutes; `sustainedOutageThresholdMs` honours fractions so a live end-to-end check can use a short window with no code change, and an absent, malformed, zero, or negative value all degrade to the default — `DEFAULT_SUSTAINED_OUTAGE_THRESHOLD_MS` is the single source of truth for that literal, not duplicated into `swarmforge.conf`'s own commented-out example). Retry-forever with capped backoff is unchanged on both loops — only the silence goes; a failed escalation send is logged and swallowed rather than faulting the loop it was reporting on; and heartbeat semantics are untouched (a sustained-outage escalation is a new, independent signal, never a substitute for or interaction with BL-370's heartbeat). **Architect pass, same ticket:** added a property test generalizing `decideSustainedOutage`'s once-per-episode invariant across arbitrary failure/recovery sequences and arbitrary thresholds/clocks, verified non-vacuous by temporarily dropping the `escalated` guard (red) and restoring it (green). No new human-facing command; the front-desk bot's degraded-poll and degraded-relay warnings now name the real underlying error instead of a bare count, and a poll or reply-relay outage that runs continuously past the threshold now produces exactly one direct Telegram alert naming the loop, the outage's duration, and its last error, with a later outage after recovery alerting again.

**A silently no-op Approve tap now says so — durably, with a diagnostic trail that survives the process, and a healthy front-desk bot stops serving a stale build past a grace period (BL-582).** Human-reported, 2026-07-23: tapping Approve on three queued asks left every button row intact with no verdict text and no yaml change. This ticket does NOT claim the root cause is settled — a counter-observation (BL-588, 2026-07-23) and a live incident (BL-1026, 2026-08-21) both show a tap failing to record on a build the supervisor still considered fresh, so the residual question is deliberately scoped out to the specifier, triggered by the next such failure on a build the supervisor considers fresh — but it closes the three hardening gaps that made ANY such failure unreadable, whatever causes it. **(a) Every callback drop path now emits a distinguishable diagnostic.** `not-my-chat`/`not-principal` taps stay answered NEVER — answering an unauthorized tap would confirm the bot exists to a stranger — but are now logged; the two human-facing failure paths (an unrecognized `callback_data`, and an Approve tap whose record changed nothing) answer with a toast naming why. Answering the Approve tap's callback query had to move from immediately-on-tap to the instant the record outcome is known — a callback query can only be answered once, so a spinner cleared up front can no longer carry a reason — riding a new optional `onDecisionRecorded` hook on `recordApprovalDecisionAndClose` (`telegramFrontDeskBotCore.ts`), preserving BL-484's single-closing-routine constraint. `pendingApprovalReply.ts`'s new `classifyApprovalRecordNoOp`/`explainApprovalRecordNoOp` turn `recordApprovalReply`'s bare boolean into one of six named reasons a human can act on (`no-ticket-file`, `already-approved`, `already-rejected`, `already-amending`, `no-human-approval-field`, `human-approval-not-pending`); a no-op record now counts as `dropped` rather than `posted` in poll telemetry — counting it posted is how a silent failure looked healthy before. **(b) The approval write already commits itself** (BL-892's `commitApprovalDecision`, sharing `commitIntegrityRunner`'s `commitApprovalWrites` with expedite) — a scenario now gates that wiring so a future edit cannot quietly repoint either write off the shared committer. **(c) `front_desk_supervisor_lib.bb` checks build freshness on the HEALTHY tick, not only on a crash respawn** — the reason a healthy bot served a stale build for 2h23m on 2026-07-23, with every tap in that window silently doing nothing. A newly-stale build starts a grace (`FRONT_DESK_BUILD_GRACE_MS`, default 5 minutes, so a merge landing mid-conversation doesn't yank the front desk away mid-tap); a build still stale past the grace moves the process to a new `stale-build` status and restarts it through the same bounded-backoff clause a crash already uses, under its own `:build-stale-detected`/`:build-stale` events — deliberately checked LAST in `check-one!`'s cond so it can never starve the pre-existing once-per-process `:healthy-reset` bookkeeping. Every diagnostic — a drop, a no-op record, and a repaint that fails after a successful record (the human still sees stale buttons even though the verdict is safely on disk and is NOT rolled back) — now lands in a new durable sink, `.swarmforge/operator/front-desk-diagnostics.log` (append-only, bounded to one rotation generation), closing the gap that left the 2026-07-23 failure window with no bot output preserved anywhere (the bot's stderr was `:inherit`-ed by the supervisor and kept nowhere). The declared invariant — every approval tap produces an observable, durable outcome — is encoded as a property test (`bl582ApprovalTapObservable.property.test.js`) over all five outcome classes, verified non-vacuous by deleting either diagnostic emit and confirming it fails on the first tap of that class. New human-facing surface: an Approve tap that fails to record now clears its spinner with a toast naming why instead of just clearing silently, and a stale-build front desk self-heals within `FRONT_DESK_BUILD_GRACE_MS` of a merge rather than serving the old build indefinitely. **Hardener pass, same ticket:** added tests for the two previously-unreached `repaintFailureCause` branches (rate-limited retry-budget exhaustion; the message-edit-failed-or-not-wired default) and for `check-one!`'s stale-build-vs-healthy-reset precedence ordering, both verified non-vacuous by hand-flipping the condition under test.

## Gaps & Things Still Missing

A scan of what the spec doesn't yet cover, roughly in priority order. Not all are v1, but each is a real decision waiting to be made. (Several earlier gaps — untracked human input, completion-measurement point, reroute livelock, item-completion loop, workflow field-ownership, salvage/rollback, and the `to: human` gate mechanism — are now addressed in the body and removed from this list.)

### Likely needed for a usable v1

- **Secrets & auth.** Backends that manage their own auth (Copilot CLI, Claude Code) need nothing from the extension — it never sees those credentials. The open question is narrower: backends that need raw API keys, plus the GitHub token for pushing branches / opening PRs. Where do those live and how are they kept out of the clone and out of commits? (Likely: extension-host environment, never written into the worktree.)
- **Cost & rate-limit controls.** Multiple agents on paid models running for hours. Need per-run token/cost tracking, a budget cap that pauses the swarm, and backoff handling when a backend rate-limits. Surfaced per-tile and as a run total. (The reroute budget and `to: human` escalation in Correctness are the per-item backstop; this is the per-run/$ backstop.)
- **`to: human` gate UX.** The mechanism is specced (a message type, surfaced on desktop + mobile, blocks the item). What's left is the interaction detail: how a gate is presented, how options are offered, timeout behavior if the human never answers, and whether a gate can be delegated/snoozed.

### Important but can follow

- **Remote-access security (BL-241 landed: rotation, revocation, read-vs-control scope + step-up).** The bridge's auth layer is now a persisted device registry (`extension/src/bridge/deviceRegistry.ts` + `deviceRegistryStore.ts`, stored in VS Code `SecretStorage` only — never the target repo or a commit), replacing the original single static bearer token. Per device: a base token grants read access (rotatable — the old token stops working, the new one doesn't, other devices are unaffected) and revocation removes just that device's access. Control actions (currently just BL-240's gate-answer route) require a genuine step-up: a control-scoped device carries a *separate* control token and must present it via an `X-Control-Token` header alongside its bearer token; a read-scoped device has no control token and can never satisfy this. Not yet built: the bootstrap "Start Bridge" command still mints one bootstrap token that satisfies control by presenting itself twice, rather than provisioning distinct devices per client — per-device registration/rotation/revocation exists as a host-side module surface (`BridgeHandle`'s `registerDevice`/`revokeDevice`/`rotateToken`/`getRegistry`) but has no dedicated command/UI yet. Off-LAN relay choice (self-hosted vs hosted) remains an open decision with privacy implications, since agent output could traverse it — unresolved by this hardening pass.
- **Observability / run artifacts.** A durable run log, transcript export, and the ability to inspect a finished run after the fact (what each agent did, decisions made). Useful for debugging a bad PR.
- **Test/lint command discovery.** Completion tracking assumes the extension can run the target's tests *on the dev branch*. How does it learn the test command — from `engineering.prompt`, auto-detected, or configured? Same for lint.
- **Multiple concurrent backlog items.** The next-item loop (see Correctness) defaults to one item at a time. Whether the swarm can work several in parallel (more worktrees, parallel dev branches) is a later question affecting branch/PR strategy.
- **Backlog item dependencies.** Eligibility now respects dependencies (see Correctness), but the *authoring* of dependencies and their visualization in the Work Tree (blocked badges, ordering) still needs detail.
- **Constitution / prompt versioning.** Partly addressed by the Governance model (rule changes are attributable commits, so a PR traces to the governance text in force). Remaining: pinning the exact prompt/constitution commit-hash *per run* in the run log, and deciding whether mid-run governance changes apply immediately (on respawn) or are staged to the next item boundary for consistency across agents in a run.

### Smaller / polish

- **Desktop/VS Code notifications.** Integrated notifications when a run finishes, a PR is ready, or an agent dead-letters — so the human isn't babysitting the panel. (Email notifications for needs-human events are now implemented; mobile push covered by the phone app.)
- **Onboarding for a fresh target.** First-run experience: `Initialize Target` exists, but a guided "this repo has no swarm files, set it up?" flow would help.
- **Diff review inside the extension.** Reviewing the PR without leaving VS Code.
- **Accessibility (BL-238 pass landed).** Tile headers, work-tree rows, collapse toggles, and the recert PWA controls are now keyboard-operable (`tabindex`, `role="button"`, Enter/Space handlers, visible `:focus-visible` rings) and screen-reader-labelled (`aria-label`/`aria-expanded` on tiles, dropdowns, buttons, and tree rows; `role="log"` on the live output pane, deliberately without `aria-live` since a continuously-streaming transcript would announce every update). Liveness/completion status now also carries a text badge (Dead/Needs human/Stalled/Working) alongside its existing color cue, so it is never color-only. Additive only — no behavior changed. Remaining: this pass covers the existing markup/controls at the time it landed; any new interactive control added later needs the same treatment, and a full assistive-technology walkthrough (vs. the markup/DOM-level checks QA ran) is still open.
- **Telemetry (opt-in).** Anonymous metrics on swarm effectiveness — items completed, chase rates, respawn frequency — to tune heuristics.

---

## Out of Scope (v1)

- The swarm writing back to its own tool library autonomously (tool promotion is manual/human-curated in v1)
- Multi-target support in a single run
- Auto-merge on green CI (human reviews all PRs)
- Extension marketplace publication (internal use first)
- Native Windows (tmux has no native Windows port; a Windows-hosted swarm runs via WSL2 instead — BL-091)

## Synthetic LLM Cost Estimates (BL-565)

BL-551 appends `llm_invocation` records for pipeline handoffs and operator
paths. Max-subscription seats had no per-call price, so tokens and `costUsd`
stayed null and rollups ranked those roles by invocation count only.

### Rule

| Record shape | Rollup treatment |
|--------------|------------------|
| Provider-billed (`costUsd` set) | Counts toward **billed** totals only |
| Tokens + model in price table, no bill | `syntheticCostUsd` from list prices → **synthetic estimate** totals |
| Tokens + model missing from table | `syntheticCostUsd` null; counted in **unknown-price** bucket |
| Usage unobservable | Null tokens; delivery never blocked |

Billed and synthetic totals are **separate labelled columns** in CLI
cost-rank, bridge `/cost-rank`, and the BL-213 cost-health sidecar (with
pricing-table `as_of` on estimate lines). They are never merged silently.

Token capture prefers existing GH-22 context-telemetry / transcript usage;
no parallel unsupervised collector when that path suffices. Historical lines
are not backfilled.

### See Also

- **BL-551** — LLM cost ledger foundation.
- **BL-665 / GH-22** — context-telemetry producer and recorder.
- How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-565-cost-ledger-synthetic-pricing-max-billed-roles.md`.

## Budget-Aware Shift Governor (BL-666)

BL-619 projects weekly exhaustion in the briefing (read-only). BL-666 is the
acting counterpart at each shift boundary hosted by
`shift_schedule_applier_lib.bb`: human Usage anchors (same store as BL-619)
plus BL-664 transcript-derived burn choose a shift verdict.

### Verdict ladder

| Preference | When |
|------------|------|
| **full** | Measured burn per shift ≤ affordable pace to replenish |
| **SHORT** | Moderate overrun — trimmed hours |
| **CHEAP** | Severe overrun — ModelFactory `assign --mode cheap` on certified seats only |
| **SKIP** | Tank cannot afford shift; approvals/Telegram drain at next start |

Every verdict announcement includes remaining %, days-to-reset, and measured vs
affordable burn — never silent. Stale anchors (> threshold) enter degraded
mode with no exact projection presented as confident. Paid credits are never
spent without explicit opt-in; BL-305 PROVIDER_LIMIT/cooldown stays the hard
floor.

### See Also

- **BL-619** — token-burn briefing warning (anchors + projection).
- **BL-660** — three shift packs / shift applier host.
- **BL-664** — transcript walker (burn meter input).
- How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-666-budget-aware-shift-governor.md`.

## Work-Note Mutation Cost Attribution (BL-1185)

BL-1001 filters multi-seat claims by ticket `mutation_cost` vs declared
`--seat-tier`. Cost resolution used only the `task:` header. Coordinator
**Work** route notes are `type: note` with `message: Work BL-…` and **must
not** carry `task:` (`swarm_handoff` — task is git_handoff-only). Nil task
→ nil cost → a hard seat `:defer-better-fit` when an easy sibling is idle
→ `NO_TASK` while an ambulance patient sat in `new/`.

### Fix

`difficulty-allows-claim?` attributes Work notes the same way
`supersede_lib/task-name-from-content` already does:

| Input | Cost attribution |
|-------|------------------|
| `task:` present (git_handoff) | Use that task name → ticket `mutation_cost` |
| `type: note`, message `Work BL-…`, no `task:` | Parse Work message → ticket `mutation_cost` |
| Non-Work note, no `task:` | Cost remains unset (legacy defer path unchanged) |

**Do not** stamp `task:` onto notes. Measurement of seat fit only — no
change to BL-1001 tier ceilings.

### See Also

- **BL-1001** — difficulty-aware coder seat routing.
- **BL-983** — multi-seat stage claim (idle-first).
- How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1185-work-note-missing-task-header-defers-hard-seat.md`.

## Same-Model Seat Tier Bypass (BL-1167)

BL-1001 filters multi-seat claims by ticket `mutation_cost` vs declared
`--seat-tier`. When every seat of a stage shares the same effective pack
`--model` (e.g. `cursor-forge` `coder` and `coder@cursor2` both `--model
auto`), tier filtering would starve the easy-tier seat of medium/high work
without reducing bounce risk — seats are model-equivalent.

### Rule

| Stage seat models | Claim filtering |
|-------------------|-----------------|
| All declared seats share one effective `--model` | Bypass BL-1001 tiers; BL-983 idle-first among seats (any `mutation_cost`) |
| Seats declare distinct effective models | BL-1001 tier filtering unchanged |

Detection is pack-conf only (`parse-seat-models` / `stage-models-equivalent?` in
`seat_difficulty_lib.bb`) — not runtime agent state. Stage-addressed
coordinator routing is unchanged.

### See Also

- **BL-1001** — difficulty-aware coder seat routing (when models differ).
- **BL-983** — multi-seat idle-first claim.
- How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1167-same-model-coder-seats-bypass-tier-routing.md`.

## Standing Property-Suite Allowlist (BL-1175)

The BL-570 pre-commit property-suite drift guard refused commits whenever
`npm run test:properties` reported any failure — including long-standing
reds unrelated to the staged parcel. That blocked landing an otherwise
green BL-605 tip without `SWARMFORGE_SKIP_PROPERTY_SUITE_GUARD=1` (forbidden
as a standing recipe by BL-1121).

### Fix

`property_suite_standing_allowlist.tsv` names each standing red with an
`allowlist` or `fix` disposition and rationale.
`check_property_suite_drift.sh` (via `property_suite_standing_allowlist_lib.sh`)
allows the commit when **every** failing file is allowlisted; any
non-allowlisted failure still refuses and names the files.

| Suite outcome | Guard |
|---------------|-------|
| All green | Allow |
| Red, all failures allowlisted | Allow (`allowlisted-standing-reds`) |
| Red, any non-allowlisted failure | Refuse |
| `SWARMFORGE_SKIP_PROPERTY_SUITE_GUARD=1` | Allow (recovery only — never standing recipe) |

Stock suite runs must not trip the BL-1124 shared-repo canary.

### See Also

- **BL-570** — property-suite drift guard.
- **BL-1121** — reconcile-import skip (standing recipe vs env override).
- **BL-1124** — fixtures must not mutate shared main.
- How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-1175-property-suite-standing-reds-block-unrelated-commits.md`.

## BL-718 Acceptance Step Wiring (BL-726)

BL-718's Bubble talk mirror product code and unit tests landed, but its
acceptance feature under `specs/features/BL-718-*.feature` had **zero** step
handlers — every scenario failed `no step handler matched` at
`specs/pipeline/runtime.js`, so the Gherkin gate never actually ran.

### Fix

`specs/pipeline/steps/bl718BubbleTalkMirrorSteps.js` registers handlers for
every BL-718 Given/When/Then and drives committed
`mirrorLetsTalkTurnToBubble` / `splitTelegramChunks` behaviour (not
prompt-text assertions). The module is required from
`specs/pipeline/steps/index.js`. Companion pilot-process gap: BL-727 (done).

### See Also

- **BL-718** — Bubble talk mirror chunks and fails loudly.
- How-to: `docs/how-to/BL-726-bl718-acceptance-feature-has-no-step-handlers.md`,
  `docs/how-to/BL-718-bubble-talk-mirror-chunks-and-fails-loudly.md`.
